# Realistic Ocean Foam — Deep Research

*Research synthesis for poseidon (WebGPU / three.js TSL FFT ocean). Ten research agents across six angles — physical oceanography, shipped games, film VFX, academic papers, texture advection, foam optics — plus a completeness pass covering validation protocols, airborne spray, and foam-to-geometry feedback. ~600 sources consulted; every claim below carries a citation in its chapter.*

## Executive summary

**The architecture poseidon already has is the published state of the art.** The persistent per-texel turbulence accumulator (`min(J, recover)`) is, almost symbol for symbol, Tessendorf, Reinhard & Gao 2023's whitecap map, NVIDIA WaveWorks / War Thunder's shipped "turbulent energy" field, and Crest's foam sim. The strain-driven carve thresholds are War Thunder's stretch-modulated foam thickness. The Voronoi F2−F1 lace texture is physically literal — aged foam rafts *are* Plateau-border networks whose cells coarsen exactly the way the carve ages ours. The trail-band-as-age design is independently confirmed by Horizon Forbidden West, which drives breaking foam purely by wave age past the break. And the deliberately mild 0.35× flow warp sits inside Weta's published foam-drag window — they report fully flow-locked foam looks "stringy," which is the artifact we found empirically. No shipped game does anything fundamentally different for open-ocean whitecaps without particles.

**What the research says to change is calibration, statistics, and dynamics — not architecture:**

1. **Foam is not white and does not stay bright.** Fresh caps reflect 40–55%, decaying to 3–10% within ~10 s (time-averaged effective ≈ 22%). Foam is spectrally flat white at the surface; only *submerged* bubble plumes take the water's green. And lit foam should be budgeted below the tonemapper's knee — energy conservation guarantees Lambertian foam ≤ diffuse white, so it never legitimately clips.
2. **Coverage has ground truth.** Monahan & O'Muircheartaigh: W = 3.84×10⁻⁶·U₁₀³·⁴¹ — about 1% of the sea at 10 m/s, 4% at 15, 10% at 20, saturating near 4% for *active* caps even in hurricanes (the escalation above Beaufort 9 is streaks and airborne spray, not more caps). This turns `foamThreshold` from a hand-tuned dial into a computed quantity, and turns `tools/foamprobe.mjs` into a regression test.
3. **Lifecycle has measured constants.** Growth within one wave period; exponential area decay with e-folding ≈ 3.5–4 s in seawater; trail persistence 5–10× the active phase; decay time scaling with breaker size (big-cascade foam should recover more slowly than small-cascade foam); two-regime decay in surfactant-rich water.
4. **The accumulator is missing two dynamics both industry and academia converged on:** *spatial* dissipation (blur the energy as it decays, so patches spread and soften — War Thunder, ATLAS, and Sea of Thieves all do this) and *advection* (one semi-Lagrangian back-trace in the existing compute ping-pong, so trails stream with the water instead of ghosting in place).
5. **The statistics of the Jacobian matter more than its point values.** Dupuy & Bruneton's real contribution is the closure: store J and J², let mips average both, and coverage = ½ + ½·erf((ε−μ)/(σ√2)) is analytically anti-aliased at every distance. Tessendorf 2023 adds: use the *minimum eigenvalue* of the deformation (fires at the true onset of folding, and its eigenvector gives the per-pixel breaking direction — a physically correct local replacement for the global wind frame).

## The ranked roadmap

Ordered by visual return per unit of effort, mapped to the existing pipeline.

### Tier 1 — drop-in upgrades to what exists

| # | Change | Where | Why |
|---|--------|-------|-----|
| 1 | **Spatial dissipation**: small blur of the turbulence accumulator as it decays | `maps.js` assemble pass | The one mechanism every shipped sim has that ours lacks; aged foam spreads and softens instead of dissolving in place |
| 2 | **Semi-Lagrangian advection**: sample previous accumulator at `uv − v·dt` (coarse-mip horizontal displacement already fetched) | `maps.js` | Trails stream with the water; kills in-place ghosting with zero new buffers |
| 3 | **λmin eigenvalue** instead of det J as the breaking criterion; its eigenvector replaces the global wind frame for the cap carve | `maps.js` + carve frame | Earlier, cleaner breaking onset; crest-following anisotropy instead of one global comb direction |
| 4 | **Wind-calibrated threshold**: invert the criterion's CDF against Monahan W(U₁₀) per preset | params / small precompute | Kills hand-tuning; coverage lands on measured reality at every wind speed (published thresholds ranged 0.034→0.534 from calm to 25 m/s — no constant serves all) |
| 5 | **Roughness coupling**: foam coverage raises specular roughness (≈ `base + foam·(1−F)`) | shading | The highest-return missing shading piece; glints broaden and die under films the way they visibly do at sea |
| 6 | **Physical albedo ramp**: fresh 0.45 → aged 0.05, front-loaded in age; green tint only on submerged layers; keep lit foam at or below the tone-curve knee | tonal ladder | Our caps currently hit ~1.5 pre-tonemap and flatten in the compressed zone; real foam separation comes from structure, not brightness |

### The validation loop

The research also returned an evaluation protocol worth adopting outright: binarize renders at two thresholds (strict = active caps, permissive = all foam) the way field science does; regression-test coverage against Callaghan's cubics per wind preset with `foamprobe`; check patch-area distribution (peak ~8–16 m²) and boundary fractal dimension (≈1.7 at 0.1% coverage → ≈2.25 at 10%); downloadable ground-truth datasets exist (Schwendeman & Thomson 2015, Malila 2022). "Inside the observed scatter" is the honest acceptance test — real coverage varies an order of magnitude at fixed wind.

## The physics of sea foam

Sea foam is not a decoration painted onto waves; it is a measurable physical population with its own birth rate, lifetime, microstructure, optics, and kinematics. Every one of those properties has been quantified by the oceanographic literature, and each maps onto a specific dial in poseidon's Jacobian-accumulator foam pipeline. This chapter collects the numbers.

### Coverage: how much of the sea is white

Whitecaps first appear near U10 ≈ 3 m/s (practically 3–4 m/s). The canonical photographic law is [Monahan & O'Muircheartaigh 1980](https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/phoc/10/12/1520-0485_1980_010_2094_opldoo_2_0_co_2.xml): W = 3.84×10⁻⁶·U10^3.41 (fraction, robust biweight fit; the OLS variant is W = 2.95×10⁻⁶·U10^3.52). That yields W ≈ 0.09% at 5 m/s, 0.29% at 7 m/s, ~1.0% at 10 m/s, 3.9% at 15 m/s, and 10.5% at 20 m/s. [Callaghan et al. 2008](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/2008GL036165) (MAP campaign, digital imagery), which fits modern imagery better at low winds, found a piecewise cubic with an explicit wind threshold: W = 3.18×10⁻³(U10−3.70)³ for 3.70 < U10 ≤ 11.25 m/s and W = 4.82×10⁻⁴(U10+1.98)³ for 9.25 < U10 ≤ 23.09 m/s (W in percent). The same study documented wind-history hysteresis: more foam at a given wind when winds are falling than when rising.

Satellite radiometry gives flatter, near-quadratic laws ([Salisbury et al. 2013](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/2013JC008797), WindSat): W10GHz = 4.6×10⁻³·U10^2.26 and W37GHz = 3.97×10⁻²·U10^1.59 (percent, valid 2–20 m/s), where W10 approximates active (stage A) foam and W37 total foam. NASA ocean-color processing uses the Stramska & Petelski (2003) fits ([Ocean Optics Web Book](https://www.oceanopticsbook.info/view/atmospheric-correction/level-2/whitecaps)): W = 5.0×10⁻⁵(U10−4.47)³ for developed seas and W = 8.75×10⁻⁵(U10−6.33)³ for undeveloped seas. Global annual mean coverage is ~3.4% (Blanchard 1963). All coefficients are compiled verbatim in [Albert et al. 2016](https://acp.copernicus.org/articles/16/13725/2016/). Two structural facts matter as much as any single curve: active stage-A crest foam is roughly a third to a half of total coverage (the rest is decaying trail foam), and instantaneous coverage at fixed wind scatters by an order of magnitude or more — wave age, SST, fetch, and surfactants all enter, largely through the effective exponent, so wind alone never fully determines W.

For poseidon: this is the ground-truth calibration curve — for each wind preset, the screen-space fraction of texels past the Jacobian foam threshold should land near W(U10): ~1% of area at 10 m/s, ~4% at 15, ~10% at 20, essentially zero below ~4 m/s. The Callaghan threshold form (U10−3.70)³ maps naturally onto a wind-scaled bias on the turbulence-accumulator threshold, and the W10/W37 ratio (~0.34 at 5 m/s, ~0.54 at 10, ~0.86 at 20) calibrates the area ratio between the fresh cap band and the full cap+trail footprint per preset.

### Lifecycle: stage A, stage B, and measured decay constants

Monahan's classification splits every whitecap into stage A — foam on and around an actively breaking crest, with air actively entrained — and stage B, the "fossil foam" raft left in the wake after entrainment stops. Individual whitecap area rises monotonically and fast during stage A (duration ≈ the active-breaking duration; Phillips et al. 2001 radar data give τ* = 5c/g ≈ 0.8× the carrier wave period, i.e. seconds), peaks, then decays quasi-exponentially: A(t) = A₀·exp(−t/τ). The classic lab constants are τ = 3.85 s in salt water versus 2.54 s in fresh water ([Monahan & Zietlow 1969](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1029/JC074i028p06961)) — salt foam lives ~50% longer because seawater inhibits bubble coalescence, producing many more sub-500 µm bubbles — and the canonical value used in the discrete-whitecap aerosol method is τ = 3.53 s ([Monahan et al., DWM manuscript](https://ams.confex.com/ams/95Annual/webprogram/Manuscript/Paper260568/AMS,%2017CAChem.,J1.%204,%20DWM.,%20Reassess,paper,ver.%20H.pdf)). Field measurements ([Callaghan et al. 2012](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/2012JC008147)) put individual decay times at 0.2–10.4 s, with the area-weighted effective decay time varying 1.4–4.8 s between deployments (a factor of 3.4); decay time increases with breaking-event speed and scale — bigger breakers leave longer-lived foam — and varies by a factor of 2–5 at fixed whitecap size under unsteady forcing. Stage B lifetime is typically 5–10× the stage A duration, and stage B covers far more ocean than stage A (Monahan & Woolf 1989) — which is exactly why total-foam laws (W37) sit well above active-foam laws (W10).

For poseidon: the accumulator's min(J, recover) recovery should implement exponential area decay with an e-folding of ~3.5–4 s (salt water) — the trail band visibly shrinking to 1/e of the fresh cap footprint in ~4 s and gone in ~10–15 s at moderate winds. Because decay time scales with breaker phase speed c, foam sourced from the 1024 m and 144 m cascades (fast, large breakers) should recover slower than 24 m cascade foam — a per-cascade recovery multiplier proportional to dominant phase speed is physically right. Growth is fast (under one wave period) and decay slow: the accumulator's asymmetric attack/release already matches observation.

### Foam thickness as the scaffolding of foam age

[Reul & Chapron 2003](https://archimer.ifremer.fr/doc/00000/10693/9320.pdf) built the standard dynamical model of foam-layer thickness for microwave radiometry — the physical scaffolding behind "foam age = foam look." Per breaking event, foam/air-water-mixture thickness grows linearly during active breaking (duration τ* = 5c/g ≈ 0.8·T_wave, from Phillips et al. 2001), reaches a maximum scaled by the breaking-front velocity (characteristic injection depth ~0.4c²/2g at threshold; characteristic thicknesses run 0–2 m for c = 0–12 m/s), then decays exponentially. Total persistence is proportional to the carrier wave period, τ = a·(2πc/g), with a ≈ 0.8 for crest (stage A) foam and a ≈ 5 for static (stage B) foam — static foam outlives crest foam by ~6×, and bigger, faster breakers leave foam that both starts thicker and lasts longer. Integrated over the breaker spectrum, two-thirds of crest-foam coverage is thinner than 60 cm and two-thirds of static-foam coverage thinner than 35 cm; raising wind from 7 to 20 m/s thickens the coverage-weighted mean layer by only ~1 cm (crest) and ~3.5 cm (static) in unstable conditions. Late-stage static foam thins from ~1–1.5 cm down to a ~1 mm emulsive monolayer before vanishing.

For poseidon: this is the cleanest justification for the layered foam bands as thickness classes — fresh cap band = meters-thick air-water mixture (opaque, max albedo); trail band = tens-of-cm to cm static foam (mid albedo, lace visible); streak film = mm monolayer (darkest, water specular returning). The a ≈ 0.8 vs a ≈ 5 ratio fixes relative lifetimes: the trail band should persist ~6× longer than the cap band in accumulator-age units. Scaling both initial strength and recovery time with carrier wave scale means the 1024 m cascade's events should write larger accumulator values with slower recovery than the 24 m cascade — one multiplier pair per cascade, driven by each cascade's characteristic phase speed.

### Streaks and windrows: Langmuir circulation

Foam streaks are Langmuir windrows: pairs of counter-rotating, wind-aligned vortices arising from the Craik–Leibovich instability of Stokes drift plus wind shear. The observed facts ([Leibovich 1983](https://www-pord.ucsd.edu/wryoung/theorySeminar/pdf15/Leibovich1983.pdf)): rows form within a few minutes of the onset of a wind ≥ 3 m/s; they lie within a few degrees of the wind (deviations up to ~20° reported — [ScienceDirect Topics](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary-sciences/langmuir-circulation)); after a wind shift the whole pattern destroys and re-forms along the new direction in 1–4 minutes, then persists for minutes to hours. Spacing runs from 1–2 m to hundreds of meters in a hierarchy: young streak fields peak at 2–5 m spacing ([J. Oceanol. Limnol.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00343-012-1201-0)), mature large streaks at 100–200 m (individual streaks up to ~500 m long), with small streaks continually forming and being swept into the larger ones through merging Y-junctions that open downwind. Cell aspect ratio L/2D ≈ 1, so dominant spacing ≈ twice the mixing/penetration depth (bounded by the mixed layer). Surface convergence collects foam into the downwelling lines: downwelling jets reach ~1% of U10, and streak-line surface jets run 1–10 cm/s faster than ambient drift (≈2× the between-streak speed). Visually, foam begins to blow into wind-aligned streaks at Beaufort 7 (~14–17 m/s), forms well-marked streaks at Beaufort 8 (17–20 m/s), and dense banding at 9–10 ([NOAA NWS Beaufort scale](https://www.spc.noaa.gov/faq/tornado/beaufort.html)).

For poseidon: streaks should be (a) nearly wind-parallel with a few degrees of jitter, (b) present only above roughly Beaufort 6–7, and (c) drawn at two coexisting scales — fine 2–5 m spacing riding inside coarse 50–200 m spacing — which maps cleanly onto two of the domain-warped carve scales evaluated in the wind frame. Streak lifetime is minutes, far longer than any wave event, so the streak film must not be driven by the per-event turbulence accumulator; a quasi-static wind-frame pattern (as poseidon does) is the physically correct cheat, and the 100–200 m spacing conveniently lives at the 144 m cascade / coarse-mip regional-signal scale. Y-junction merges opening downwind are a cheap authenticity detail for the streak texture.

### Microstructure: from bubble plume to Plateau-border lace

Bubble creation under a breaker spans <0.1 mm to >10 mm radius with a break at the Hinze scale (~1 mm radius): number density ∝ r^(−3/2) below it (jet/drop impact) and ∝ r^(−10/3) above it (turbulent fragmentation) ([Deane & Stokes 2002](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature00967)). Bubbles with r ≳ 0.7 mm rise within seconds and coalesce into the visible raft; smaller ones linger as the milky submerged plume ([Callaghan, Deane & Stokes 2017](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/2017jc012809)). Surface rafts show bubbles mostly 0.75–10 mm in diameter, with coalescence growing cells past 4 mm (long-lived cells persisting >1 s) while rising bulk bubbles average 1.9–2.3 mm diameter ([Flow, Cambridge](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/flow/article/clustering-coalescing-and-bursting-processes-in-surface-bubbles-of-surfactant-water-flows/2B134D64B6264326C041E2B69BBE7BC8)). Raft evolution is a drainage cascade: films between touching bubbles drain through Plateau borders (capillary suction at triple junctions), thin, and rupture; coalescence makes cells coarsen with age — cell size grows, cell count drops — so an aging patch turns from dense micro-froth into an open polygonal net (reticulation) before dissolving into isolated patches. Bordonskyi et al. (1978) observed thick foam layers (1–1.5 cm) spontaneously decaying into a ~0.1 cm "emulsive monolayer" — late-stage foam is a single-bubble-thick lace film ([Reul & Chapron 2003](https://archimer.ifremer.fr/doc/00000/10693/9320.pdf)).

For poseidon: this validates the baked Voronoi F2−F1 lace as literally the right texture — an aged raft IS a Plateau-border edge network. Real cells run ~1 mm–1 cm (sub-texel), so the rendered lace scales are stylized magnifications; what must be honored is the aging sequence: fresh cap = solid unresolved white (lace invisible, dissolve threshold low), mid-age trail = fine dense lace, old trail = coarser and more open (fewer, bigger cells). Driving both lace-scale selection and dissolve threshold from accumulator age reproduces coarsening plus film rupture; the endpoint should be a one-cell-thick open web, not a uniform fade.

### Environmental modifiers: salinity, surfactants, temperature

Salinity: salt-water whitecaps persist ~50% longer than freshwater ones (τ 3.85 s vs 2.54 s; [Monahan & Zietlow 1969](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1029/JC074i028p06961)) because salt inhibits coalescence, biasing the raft toward many small bubbles. Surfactants: [Callaghan, Deane & Stokes 2013](https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/phoc/43/6/jpo-d-12-0148.1.xml) found two lab decay regimes — an early phase controlled by bubble-plume degassing (large bubbles surfacing and bursting; insensitive to surfactant, lasting roughly the first 1–2 s) and a late tail controlled by surface-film stabilization. Adding Triton X-100 stabilized foam to ~3× the clean-seawater persistence, and surfactant roughly doubles the survival time of individual surface bubbles ([Flow, Cambridge](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/flow/article/clustering-coalescing-and-bursting-processes-in-surface-bubbles-of-surfactant-water-flows/2B134D64B6264326C041E2B69BBE7BC8)) — so in biologically productive water (blooms, slicks) stage-B foam lingers far longer, forming the scummy films seen in windrows. Temperature acts twice: Bortkovskii's classes (cold <4 °C, intermediate 4–17 °C, warm >17 °C) show cold water suppressing breaking but lengthening bubble/foam lifetime, while satellite analyses find considerably more whitecap fraction in warm water at the same wind; Monahan & O'Muircheartaigh (1986) showed SST mainly modifies the wind exponent — ~2 at SST ≈ 10 °C rising to >3 above ~22 °C ([Ocean Science Journal 2022](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12601-022-00060-4)). Net for imagery: warm seas foam more readily; cold seas hold old foam longer.

For poseidon: two cheap, physically grounded dials on accumulator recovery — a water preset (fresh lake ≈ 0.66× persistence, clean ocean = 1×, bloom/surfactant-rich ≈ 3×) and a climate preset (warm sea: lower foam threshold / higher coverage exponent; cold sea: higher threshold but slower recovery). The two-regime decay also motivates a nonlinearity: recovery fast in the first ~1–2 s (degassing — the cap collapses quickly to the trail) then slow in the tail (surfactant-stabilized film), i.e. recovery rate decreasing with foam age rather than constant.

### Kinematics: what moves and organizes the foam

Foam rafts ride surface drift (~3% of wind plus Stokes drift), not the wave orbital — the raft is left nearly stationary in the water frame while waves pass under it. Whitecap area grows monotonically along and behind the crest during stage A (Kennedy & Snyder 1983; Koepke 1984 supports monotonic stage-A growth; via [Reul & Chapron 2003](https://archimer.ifremer.fr/doc/00000/10693/9320.pdf)), so the trailing patch is deposited as an elongated wake behind the translating crest — foam trails point up-wave of where the crest now is, producing the classic comet/horseshoe shapes. [Scanlon & Ward 2016](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/2015JC011230) separate the stages by exactly these signatures: stage A = bright, textured, attached to the crest; stage B = dimmer, smoother, spatially detached and advected ([separation techniques](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2211122014000061)). Beyond wind, two strain mechanisms organize the field: surface convergence collects foam as a passive tracer at convergence lines (Langmuir cells, internal-wave and frontal convergences) — accumulating where divergence is negative, stretched and thinned where positive — with Langmuir sweeping velocities of cm/s acting over minutes, while wave-orbital straining acts within each wave period, momentarily stretching crest foam (opening the lace) and compressing trough/convergence foam (closing it) ([Leibovich 1983](https://www-pord.ucsd.edu/wryoung/theorySeminar/pdf15/Leibovich1983.pdf)).

For poseidon: this endorses two existing mechanisms as physically literate. The flow-warped carve coordinates at 0.35× horizontal displacement are correct — under-advecting the carve texture relative to the displacement field matches rafts riding drift, not orbital motion, so foam visually "slips" behind the waves. The strain-driven carve thresholds use the right sign convention: negative divergence → denser, more connected foam; positive divergence → stretched, opened lace. The stage-A geometry additionally argues the fresh cap band should be biased toward the down-wave/leeward side of Jacobian minima (deposited behind the crest), which the wind-frame anisotropic sampling can approximate by offsetting the cap band up-wind of the trail.

### Foam is not white: measured albedo and its decay

Thick fresh foam reflects about half the incident visible light, not all of it. [Whitlock, Bartlett & Gurganus 1982](https://web.gps.caltech.edu/~vijay/Papers/BRDF/whitlock-etal-82.pdf) measured ~50% for multilayer foam (>0.1 m thick, referenced against a 94–99% BaSO₄ near-Lambertian standard), consistent with Payne (1972); [Dierssen 2019](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/earth-science/articles/10.3389/feart.2019.00014/full) field hyperspectral data give ~0.4–0.5 for actively breaking multilayer foam. A single bubble layer reflects only ~20% of the multilayer value (~0.1). [Koepke 1984](https://opg.optica.org/ao/abstract.cfm?uri=ao-23-11-1816) tracked individual whitecaps: reflectance 0.20–0.55 at formation dropping to 0.03–0.10 within ~10 s, giving a time-averaged "effective whitecap reflectance" of 0.22 (±50%) — the standard value in ocean-color atmospheric correction. Residual stage-B foam measures ~0.18 (Dierssen). Submerged bubble plumes are not white at all: their spectra are amplified versions of the background water color (green-peaked in coastal water) — they brighten the hue rather than whitening it. Ship radiometry ([Moore, Voss & Gordon 2000](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1029/1999JC900334)) confirms area-averaged whitecap-augmented reflectance of only 0.001–0.002 at 9–12 m/s winds (~0.1–0.2 albedo over the actual patches once coverage is divided out), with RSAR(412 nm) = 3.4×10⁻⁶·U^2.55. Kokhanovsky's (2004) radiative-transfer fit: R₀ ≈ 0.36, equivalent water-film thickness 0.099 mm, bubble diameters 0.16–1 mm, void fraction 60–99%.

For poseidon: recalibrate the tonal ladder to measured anchors — dry fresh cap ≈ 0.5 diffuse albedo (never 1.0; pure-white foam is the classic CG tell), wet web / thin trail ≈ 0.15–0.2, aged streak film ≈ 0.05–0.1, submerged plume = background water color amplified ~1.5–3× (tinted, never grey-white — the "submerged grey" should lean toward the sea-palette hue). The Koepke aging curve (0.5 → 0.05 in ~10 s) means albedo should decay with accumulator age on an e-folding similar to area decay (~3–4 s): the trail darkens as it shrinks. The ×0.2 single-layer factor justifies modulating brightness by the lace texture itself — lace-web texels (one bubble thick) should render several times darker than solid cap texels.

### Spectral shape: flat white, aging slightly cyan

Foam reflectance is spectrally flat across 400–700 nm — which is why it reads neutral white — then falls monotonically into the infrared following liquid-water absorption: −40% at 850 nm, −50% at 1020 nm, −85% at 1650 nm relative to the visible ([Frouin, Schwindling & Deschamps 1996](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/96JC00629); Whitlock found minima at 1.5 and 1.9 µm matching water-absorption peaks). The Frouin factors adopted in NASA processing: 1.0 through 555 nm, 0.889 at 670 nm, 0.760 at 765 nm, 0.645 at 865 nm ([Ocean Optics Web Book](https://www.oceanopticsbook.info/view/atmospheric-correction/level-2/whitecaps)) — the decline already begins in the deep red. Whitecap-enhanced spectra show water-absorption troughs at ~600, 756, 980, 1200, 1448, 1932 nm; the shallow 600 nm dip plus red rolloff is the only in-gamut effect, produced by photons traversing water between bubbles. In colored coastal water, thin foam and submerged bubbles pick up a green-peaked tint. [Dierssen 2019](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/earth-science/articles/10.3389/feart.2019.00014/full) fits the whole 400–2500 nm whitecap spectrum as a 3rd-order polynomial in log(water absorption) with R² = 0.975: the foam spectrum is essentially a function of how much water each photon path crosses, which grows as foam ages, thins, and wets.

For poseidon: dry thick cap is neutral (equal RGB); as foam ages, wets, and thins, red attenuates first (the 670 nm factor 0.889 is measurable even in-gamut), so the wet-web and streak-film tonal layers should shift slightly cyan/green of neutral rather than grey — multiplying aging foam color by roughly (0.9R, 1.0G, 1.0B) before blending with the water reproduces the measured physics. Submerged scud should be tinted by the water body color (an amplification of the sea palette), never desaturated grey.

### BRDF: near-Lambertian, with a grazing forward lobe

Every operational ocean-color and radiation-budget treatment models whitecap foam as a Lambertian reflector — albedo 0.22 (effective) or ~0.4–0.5 (fresh) — and field measurements are referenced against Lambertian Spectralon/BaSO₄ plaques precisely because foam is close to that ideal: multiple scattering among 60–99% void-fraction bubble layers randomizes direction efficiently ([Ocean Optics Web Book](https://www.oceanopticsbook.info/view/atmospheric-correction/level-2/whitecaps); [Dierssen 2019](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/earth-science/articles/10.3389/feart.2019.00014/full)). Recent laboratory goniometer measurements ([Infrared Physics & Technology 2025](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1350449525003585), visible + NIR, controlled foam thickness) quantify the deviation: at normal incidence BRDF·cosθr has a smooth inverted-U, quasi-Lambertian shape; as incidence angle grows, a forward-scattering peak rises above the diffuse background; peak BRDF·cosθr grows approximately linearly with layer thickness — thicker foam is brighter but still diffuse. Kokhanovsky (2004) modeled foam as a close-packed scattering medium (asymmetry-like parameter B ≈ 2.3, R₀ ≈ 0.36) — again dominantly diffuse. So Lambert is the right base; the corrections are a modest forward/specular glint at grazing view-plus-sun geometry (mostly from the wet film on and between bubbles) and brightness scaling with thickness, with no strong directional redistribution.

For poseidon: shade foam as a diffuse Lambertian term with the age-dependent albedo (0.5 fresh → 0.05 old), replacing the water's specular/Fresnel response on dry-cap texels — fresh dry foam kills the mirror term, which is why caps read matte against a glinting sea — while wet-web and streak-film texels keep a damped version of the water specular (they are water films). Add at most a small forward-scatter boost at grazing angles on thick foam; no retro-reflection, no strong gloss. Foam should also occlude subsurface scattering: it is an opaque diffuse lid on the water.

## Shading and optics of foam

The physics above fixes what foam is; this chapter covers how shipped renderers turn it into pixels — the field-standard BRDF, how foam must modify the water beneath it, the two-layer bubble trick, anti-aliasing that actually converges, and where foam must sit on the tone curve.

### The baseline: Lambert at albedo 0.4, driven by filtered Jacobian statistics

The canonical real-time whitecap paper, [Dupuy & Bruneton 2012](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2407746.2407761) ([open access](https://inria.hal.science/hal-00967078v1)), shades foam as a pure Lambertian layer over the specular sea. In the [reference GLSL](https://github.com/jdupuy/whitecaps/blob/master/ocean.glsl): coverage W = 0.5·erf(0.5·√2·(ε − μ)/√σ²) + 0.5, where μ and σ² are the mean and variance of the displacement Jacobian read from mip-mapped textures; foam radiance is l = (Lsun·max(dot(N,L),0) + Esky)/π and R_ftot = W·l·0.4 — Lambert with a constant scalar albedo of 0.4, lit by sun plus hemispherical sky irradiance, using the water normal (no separate foam normal). Coverage is thus a smooth analytic function of prefiltered quantities, not a thresholded texel. Notably, the reference composites additively (gl_FragColor.rgb += R_ftot), leaving the sun glint and sky reflection alive underneath — physically wrong at high coverage but cheap and stable.

For poseidon: the current foam light, 0.55 + 0.6·saturate(dot(N, sunDir)) on the water normal (oceanSurfaceMaterial.js, ~line 1370), is exactly this model with an ambient floor standing in for Esky/π. Two upgrades transfer directly: (1) make the ambient term the actual sky color at the zenith — one skyColor() tap, already available — so foam cools and warms with the sky presets instead of a fixed 0.55 grey; (2) poseidon already lerps rather than adds (mix(water, foamShaded·tone, coverage)), which is the energy-conserving choice the reference skipped — keep it.

### The tonal ladder, anchored to measurements

The field numbers give a hard tone continuum: fresh thick foam reflects ~40–55% in the visible at the moment of breaking (historical range 40–75%), decaying to 3–10% within ~10 s as the raft thins and submerges; the time-averaged effective reflectance is ~22% ([Koepke 1984](https://opg.optica.org/ao/abstract.cfm?uri=ao-23-11-1816)); thin residual foam and decaying plumes sit ~18% ([Dierssen 2019](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/earth-science/articles/10.3389/feart.2019.00014/full)). Foam is near-flat across the visible (white, essentially Lambertian-diffuse, no directional glint of its own) but drops steeply into the NIR (−40% by 850 nm); submerged bubble plumes shift toward a greenish peak because the light is filtered by the water column — underwater bubbles take the water's scattering tint, surface foam does not. Radiative-transfer fits give an equivalent water-film thickness of only ~0.01 mm for the average whitecap ([Kokhanovsky 2004](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2003jc002177)) — foam is optically a very thin scattering skin, which is why aging changes its brightness by an order of magnitude.

For poseidon: this validates the tonal-layer design (dry cap 1.0 / wet web 0.78–0.85 / streak film 0.66–0.8 / submerged grey 0.5 / scud 0.52–0.58): the measured fresh:aged ratio is ~55:18 ≈ 3:1, and the cap:scud tone ratio of 1.0:0.5 with coverage also falling sits in the right band. Two refinements: the decay is fast (order 10 s to ~1/5 brightness), so the accumulator recovery mapped to age should push most of the tonal drop into the first part of the trail band, not spread it linearly; and only the submerged layers (underA hole floors, the age·0.20 milky-sheet term) should pick up a green-cyan water tint — surface cap and streak lace stay spectrally neutral.

### Wrapped diffuse and crest subsurface scattering

The standard wrap formula is diffuse = max(0, (dot(N,L) + wrap)/(1 + wrap)) ([GPU Gems ch. 16](https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems/part-iii-materials/chapter-16-real-time-approximations-subsurface-scattering), example wrap = 0.2, optionally with a scatter-color smoothstep at the terminator) — the classic upgrade from flat Lambert for aerated foam, keeping the shadowed side of a crest's foam from going black. In shipped FFT oceans the bigger subsurface term sits on the water at crests, not the foam: the [Atlas GDC 2019](https://www.gdcvault.com/play/1025819/Advanced-Graphics-Techniques-Tutorial-Wakes)-derived formula, as codified in [GodotOceanWaves](https://github.com/2Retr0/GodotOceanWaves/blob/main/assets/shaders/spatial/water.gdshader), is sss_height = k1·max(0, wave_height + 2.5)·pow(max(dot(L,−V),0),4)·pow(0.5 − 0.5·dot(L,N),3), plus a near-view term sss_near = 0.5·pow(dot(N,V),2), tinted by sss_modifier = vec3(0.9, 1.15, 0.85) (green-shifted), faded by (1 − fresnel), and mixed toward foam color by foam_factor — foam and crest-SSS blended as one "aerated crest" quantity, because physically both are bubble scattering. [Sea of Thieves](https://history.siggraph.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2018-Talks-Ang_The-Technical-Art-of-Sea-of-Thieves.pdf) similarly drives a subsurface color blend from a wave-peak mask built on FFT choppiness offsets (more subsurface where light travels a shorter path through the water).

For poseidon: the transferable piece is on the foam side — replace foamLight's hard saturate(dot(N,sunDir)) with the wrap form ((dot(N,L)+w)/(1+w), w ≈ 0.2–0.4) so shadow-side foam keeps shape instead of flattening to the 0.55 ambient floor. The Atlas pattern of one shared aeration scalar also suggests reusing the turbulence accumulator to slightly boost the water's own SSS tint in the trail band — bubbles brighten the water body before they read as visible lace.

### What foam does to the water underneath

Three mechanisms recur across engines ([GodotOceanWaves](https://github.com/2Retr0/GodotOceanWaves/blob/main/assets/shaders/spatial/water.gdshader); [Unity HDRP](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.render-pipelines.high-definition@14.0/manual/WaterSystem-foam.html); [Crest](https://crest.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user/water-appearance.html)). (1) Roughness: foam is matte, so coverage must raise the water's specular roughness or the glint punches through the raft — Godot uses ROUGHNESS = (1.0 − fresnel)·foam_factor + 0.4 (base 0.4 rising toward 1 with foam); HDRP exposes "Foam Smoothness" as a first-class property and lets decals override water smoothness locally; Crest exposes Foam Smoothness on HDRP and a specular falloff/boost pair elsewhere. (2) Compositing: foam over water is an opacity blend, never additive — additive foam turns red foam pink and black foam light-blue and over-brightens everything ([Roystan](https://roystan.net/articles/toon-water/): "additive blending... is great for objects that emit light... water and foam don't"); correct is out = foam·a + water·(1−a). (3) Transmission: coverage should also suppress everything that depends on seeing into the water — refraction, depth color, caustics — since the raft is opaque; Crest's two-layer model makes the surface layer opaque white with only the bubble layer transmissive. Dupuy/Bruneton's additive compositing is the known-wrong-but-cheap outlier.

For poseidon: the coverage lerp over the finished water pixel already attenuates glitter and sky reflection under the raft. What is missing is the partial-coverage regime: in the 0.1–0.6 coverage band (scud, streak film, thin lace) the water should keep its specular but roughened — a streak-covered swell shows a broadened, dimmer sun road, not a clean glint and not none. Cheapest port: feed max(coverage, age-band paling) into the existing roughness/glitter-width parameter before the specular is computed (one multiply), mirroring the Godot formula. This is likely the single highest-visual-return change for the streak/scud layers over dark water.

### The subsurface bubble layer: Crest's two-layer model

[Crest](https://github.com/wave-harmonic/crest) renders foam as two explicit layers ([OceanFoam.hlsl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wave-harmonic/crest/master/crest/Assets/Crest/Crest/Shaders/OceanFoam.hlsl)). Surface layer: white foam thresholded by smoothstep(i_foam, i_foam + _WaveFoamFeather, textureValue), lit with ambient plus sun. Bubble layer: a second sample of the same foam texture, tinted by _FoamBubbleColor and modulated by saturate(i_foam·_WaveFoamBubblesCoverage), lit by ambient only (no sun term — it is inside the water), and offset by a view-dependent parallax, parallaxOffset = −_FoamBubbleParallax·view.xz/dot(n, view), so the bubble cloud visibly sits below the surface plane and slides against the white lace as the camera moves — that parallax slide is what sells volume with zero extra geometry. The bubble sample uses a forced coarse mip (SampleLevel mip 3) so it reads as a soft cloud, not sharp lace; UVs are advected along wind (float2(0.866, 0.5)) and nudged by the normal (0.125·n.xz). Unity HDRP has the same surface/deep foam split internally (currently monochromatic, a documented limitation). Physically this matches the measured greenish spectral peak of submerged plumes versus the flat-white surface raft ([Dierssen 2019](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/earth-science/articles/10.3389/feart.2019.00014/full)).

For poseidon: the "milky sheet" term (water = mix(water, foamShaded·0.62, age·0.20·...)) is a flat version of this bubble layer. Both missing ingredients are one-liners in TSL: (a) tint that term toward the water's own scatter green — bubbles are lit through the column — rather than foamColor grey; (b) parallax its lookup coordinate by −k·V.xz/dot(N,V) (k ≈ 0.05–0.15 m) at a forced coarse mip of the existing detail/lace texture. The differential slide between the parallaxed under-layer and the surface lace gives the trail band depth for one extra texture tap, fully within the no-screen-space-pass constraint.

### Scud: thin translucent films over dark water

No shipped title gives scud a distinct BRDF; the working recipe is mask-side. [Sea of Thieves](https://history.siggraph.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2018-Talks-Ang_The-Technical-Art-of-Sea-of-Thieves.pdf): foam generated at wave peaks (Tessendorf criterion) is progressively blurred with feedback "to simulate the foam dispersing and to give us a softer mask," then blended with artist-authored textures, with generation/dispersion/blending re-tuned per sea state (calm shows contact foam only; storm churns) — the dissolving trail is the same substance as the cap, just diffused and lower alpha, never a separate hard-edged texture. Physically, thin residual foam reflects ~18% versus 40–55% fresh ([Dierssen 2019](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/earth-science/articles/10.3389/feart.2019.00014/full)), so a scud film over dark water is only ~2–4× brighter than the water body, not white — its alpha and tone must both drop. The film must be an alpha lerp at low opacity (0.2–0.5) so the dark water and its roughened specular read through the holes; a sub-unity opacity ceiling keeps wave shading alive under the film. Crest's Foam Feather parameter ("how gradual the transition is from full foam to no foam") is the same idea as a tunable ([Crest docs](https://crest.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user/water-appearance.html)).

For poseidon: the scud layer already caps at 0.55 alpha and tone 0.58, matching the 18%-vs-white physics. The transferable Sea of Thieves lesson is the feedback blur: poseidon has no history buffer by design, but accumulator recovery IS a temporal blur of the fold signal — the equivalent move is sampling turbulence at progressively coarser mips as age rises (fresh cap from fine texels, scud from the level-3/5 neighbourhood reads it already does), so old foam is automatically softer-edged than young foam. Widening the smoothstep of the scud/streak dissolves with age (fresh: tight 0.16 window; scud: 2–3× wider) completes the "same substance, diffusing" read.

### Foam normals: shape from the foam field itself

Crest's "Foam 3D Lighting" derives a foam normal with no authored normal map: sample the white-foam value at two offsets with delta = 0.25·pixelZ·texel (the step scales with view distance so the gradient stays stable under minification), dfdx/dfdz = neighbor − center, then fN = normalize(N + _WaveFoamNormalStrength·(−dfdx, 0, −dfdz)). Lighting is diffuse = ambient + lightScale·sunColor·max(0, dot(fN, L)), plus an explicit foam specular pow(max(0, dot(reflect(−V, fN), L)), _SpecularFallOff)·_SpecularBoost — a soft wide gloss lobe, not the water's mirror ([OceanFoam.hlsl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wave-harmonic/crest/master/crest/Assets/Crest/Crest/Shaders/OceanFoam.hlsl)). The motivating bug report ([Crest issue #21](https://github.com/crest-ocean/crest/issues/21)) is instructive: uniform-lit foam "appears flat" and at sunset "looks overly saturated because the entire surface receives uniform lighting"; height-implied shading plus PBR roughness is the fix. [Horizon Forbidden West](https://advances.realtimerendering.com/s2022/SIGGRAPH2022-Advances-Water-Malan.pdf) adds the resolution caveat from the other direction: foam carried in vertex color "can't create features smaller than triangles," causing undersampling like foam popping on the front of a breaking wave — foam detail must live at fragment/texture rate.

For poseidon: foam is currently shaded on the water normal only; the lace/fbm fields modulate brightness (fA·0.55+0.78) but not direction, so a cap at sunset lights uniformly — exactly issue #21. The Crest trick ports cheaply because the composited coverage·tone scalar already exists per-fragment: two extra evaluations of the cheap layers (or the baked lace texture alone) at world-space offsets scaled by ~0.25·viewDist give a foam gradient normal for the diffuse term only; keep the water normal for Fresnel/reflection so the silhouette holds. A wide-lobe foam specular (falloff exponent ~8–32, small boost) on that same normal would give the wet-web layer its sheen. Poseidon is fragment-rate everywhere, so HFW's vertex-color trap is the argument for keeping it that way.

### Anti-aliasing I: filter the statistics, not the mask

Dupuy & Bruneton's headline result is that whitecap coverage can be anti-aliased analytically because it is computed from quantities that filter linearly: store the Jacobian's mean and second moment in mip-mapped textures (both linear in the underlying data, so hardware trilinear/anisotropic filtering is exact), then per pixel reconstruct variance and evaluate W = 0.5 + 0.5·erf((ε − μ)/(√2·σ)) ([Dupuy & Bruneton 2012](https://inria.hal.science/hal-00967078v1); [ocean.glsl](https://github.com/jdupuy/whitecaps/blob/master/ocean.glsl)). At close range σ collapses to per-texel and W is near-binary (crisp foam edges); under minification the filtered variance grows and W smoothly becomes the area fraction of foam in the pixel footprint — the correct filtered answer with zero shimmer, "plausible and anti-aliased images for scales ranging from centimetric to planetary," under 10 ms at 1280×720 on a GeForce 560 Ti. The general principle: never mip-filter a thresholded foam mask (thresholding and filtering do not commute); filter the driving field and its variance, and widen the threshold by the local standard deviation.

For poseidon: this is the strongest theoretical match to the existing architecture — the turbulence accumulator is per-texel and mipped, and coarse-mip neighbourhood reads (levels 1/2/3/5) already exist for core/streak/scud. The missing half is the variance: writing E[J²] (or E[turb²]) into a spare channel of the maps.js compute pass costs one MAD, after which every carve threshold (foamThreshold, fEdge, wEdge) can be widened by k·σ(lod) — distant lace then converges to its true grey coverage instead of strobing between white and dark as texels cross a fixed threshold. This attacks the fine-lace temporal shimmer at its root rather than masking it with blur.

### Anti-aliasing II: the per-fragment toolkit

The complementary tools: (1) fwidth-widened thresholds — replace hard smoothsteps with w = fwidth(v); smoothstep(t − w, t + w, v), making every carve edge exactly one pixel of gradient at any distance ([Ronja, tut. 46](https://www.ronja-tutorials.com/post/046-fwidth/)). (2) Band-limit the pattern itself — [Inigo Quilez](https://iquilezles.org/articles/filtering/) ([band-limiting](https://iquilezles.org/articles/bandlimiting/)): compute the pixel's texture-space footprint from derivatives and either analytically box-filter the procedural pattern or adaptively supersample (sample count = 1 + clamp(detail·length(duv), 0, N)); components whose period falls below the footprint should fade to their mean, not keep flickering. (3) Distance fades — [GodotOceanWaves](https://github.com/2Retr0/GodotOceanWaves) multiplies foam by exp(−dist·0.0075) and normal strength by exp(−dist·0.0175), and mixes bicubic/bilinear filtering by world-space pixel density; flattening normals with distance also kills specular shimmer feeding foam masks. (4) Sharper mips without shimmer — [Ben Golus](https://bgolus.medium.com/sharper-mipmapping-using-shader-based-supersampling-ed7aadb47bec): a conservative mip bias of about −0.5 sharpens with minimal aliasing; a 4-tap rotated-grid supersample in-shader at bias −1 gives sharp and temporally stable minified detail (4× fetches on the one texture that matters). (5) Stochastic dissolves — [Wyman & McGuire, Hashed Alpha Testing](https://cwyman.org/papers/i3d17_hashedAlpha.pdf) (I3D 2017) picks the comparison threshold from a stable spatial hash so geometry does not vanish as alpha-mapped content recedes, with "no more temporal flicker than traditional alpha testing" — the same idea applies to foam-fleck dissolves in TAA-less pipelines.

For poseidon: the lace carves are smoothstep(edge, edge + const, field) with fixed widths (0.16, 0.2) in texture-value space — under minification the field's fwidth exceeds these windows and the lace strobes. Port order: (a) add max(fixedWidth, k·fwidth(field)) to every carve window — near-free in TSL via dFdx/dFdy; (b) fade each lace scale toward its channel mean (the baked textures' TARGET_ means are documented in detailTexture.js) once its world period drops below ~2 pixel footprints, converting the 9 cm and 25 cm filament scales into smooth grey film at range instead of noise; (c) since poseidon has no TAA, the fleck gate (erode > 0.56 edge specks) is the one place hashed thresholds help — jitter the 0.56 gate by a world-anchored hash so specks fade by dropping count, not by blinking. The 4-tap RGSS supersample is the fallback for the lace texture alone if (a)+(b) leave residual shimmer in the 30–100 m band.

### HDR and tonemapping: foam below the knee, glints above it

Physics grants the headroom for free: Lambertian foam radiance = albedo·E_total/π with albedo ≤ ~0.55, so foam can never exceed the scene's diffuse-white level ([Koepke 1984](https://opg.optica.org/ao/abstract.cfm?uri=ao-23-11-1816)) — only mirror-path sun glints exceed it, by orders of magnitude. The tonemapper decides whether that separation survives. [Khronos PBR Neutral](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/ToneMapping/blob/main/PBR_Neutral/README.md) (three.js NeutralToneMapping) is exactly specified: identity below the knee at 0.8 (linear 0.8 = sRGB 231 — any baseColor with R,G,B below 231 is faithfully reproduced); above it, a 1/x compression maps linear 1.0 to ~sRGB 243 and infinity to 255, with a desaturation path-to-white (Kd = 0.15, Ks = 0.8 − 0.04). Consequences: foam whose lit value lands at 0.6–0.85 after exposure keeps full tonal separation between its layers, while everything above ~2–3× the knee — all sun glints — lands in the 243–255 bucket, so glints and the brightest foam become nearly indistinguishable near-whites on screen; their visible difference must be carried by area and structure (glints are subpixel chips, foam is connected lace), not display value. Filmic curves with an explicit white point ([Hable](http://filmicworlds.com/blog/filmic-tonemapping-operators/), Uncharted 2 operator, W = 11.2, whiteScale = 1/curve(W)) make the same trade tunably. And because foam is not emissive, it must stay below any bloom threshold: bloom belongs to glints (values ≫ 1), never the raft.

For poseidon: it ships NeutralToneMapping at exposure 1.2, and its own foamDebug comment records the predicted symptom — sun glitter clipping to white chips indistinguishable from foam in a still. Concretely: (1) budget the dry cap's final lit value to ~0.75–0.95 pre-tonemap (just under/at the knee at exposure 1.2) so the 1.0/0.85/0.8/0.58/0.5 tone ladder survives to the display — currently foamLight can reach 0.55 + 0.6 = 1.15 times an fbm max of 1.33, ≈ 1.5, pushing fresh caps well past the knee where Neutral flattens their texture; (2) keep the glint path free to exceed the knee (that is the physical separation) and let structure distinguish them, which the connected-lace textures already do; (3) if a preset re-enables ACES, expect the ~0.83/0.58 channel skew and cap desaturation to return (documented in main.js) — the tone ladder is calibrated for Neutral.

## Validating against reality

Ocean rendering papers historically validate by side-by-side screenshots. Whitecap oceanography, by contrast, has spent forty years turning foam photographs into numbers — coverage laws, patch-size histograms, fractal dimensions, decay-time fits — with published methods and downloadable datasets. Poseidon can be tested against all of it, offline, without touching the runtime renderer.

### Qualitative anchors: the Beaufort photo standards

The Beaufort scale is codified by WMO (Manual on Codes No. 306, Code table 3700) against a 10 m / 10-minute mean wind ([WMO Marine services FAQ](https://community.wmo.int/site/knowledge-hub/programmes-and-initiatives/marine-services/frequently-asked-questions)). Standard marine tables give per-force foam descriptions usable directly as pattern anchors ([NOAA NCEI PDF](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/sites/default/files/2021-09/Marine_Beaufort_Scale.pdf); [NWS reference](https://www.weather.gov/media/pqr/beaufort/beaufort.pdf)): Force 3 (3.4–5.4 m/s) scattered whitecaps begin; Force 4 (5.5–7.9 m/s) fairly frequent white horses; Force 5 (8.0–10.7 m/s) many white horses, chance of spray; Force 6 (10.8–13.8 m/s) extensive white foam crests; Force 7 (13.9–17.1 m/s) foam begins to blow in streaks along the wind; Force 8–9 dense wind-aligned streaks; Force 10+ sea surface largely white, great foam patches. A digitized reference photo set keyed to Beaufort force exists at the [Iowa Digital Library](https://digital.lib.uiowa.edu/node/593762).

For poseidon: the cheapest tuning loop — set U10 per Beaufort force, render at the capture rail framing, and compare side-by-side with the corresponding photo. The Force 7 threshold (~14 m/s) is a hard calibration point for when the wind-frame anisotropic carve and streak-film layer should transition from isotropic patches to wind-aligned streaks; below Force 7 real seas show whitecaps but not coherent streaks — a common CG over-stylization error.

### Binarizing the render the way field science binarizes photos

[Callaghan & White 2009](https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/atot/26/2/2008jtecho634_1.xml) (J. Atmos. Oceanic Tech. 26:383–394) is the standard automated whitecap extraction (AWE) method: for each grayscale image, compute the "percentage increase in pixels" (PIP) function over candidate brightness thresholds and pick the threshold from derivative/structure analysis of that curve — per-image adaptive, robust to changing illumination, no human analyst. [Schwendeman & Thomson 2015](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/2015JC011196) used a related criterion: threshold at 20% of the peak in the curvature of the pixel-intensity histogram. [Kleiss & Melville 2010](https://airsea.ucsd.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/10/2019/06/2010_Kleiss_Melville-Journal_of_Physical_Oceanography_vol_40.pdf) found a single strict threshold matches manual identification of active (bright) whitecaps well but misses dim residual foam: their thresholded coverage WT averaged only 1.5× their strictly-active WA, versus the classic WB/WA ~ 10 when residual foam is fully included — measured "coverage" depends strongly on which foam generations the threshold captures. [Mironov & Dulov 2008](https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0957-0233/19/1/015405) built the mast-video pipeline (background statistics plus physical criteria, patch-centroid tracking for breaking speeds); later systems add omnidirectional fisheye with IMU projection ([Al-Lashi et al. 2018](https://opg.optica.org/josaa/fulltext.cfm?uri=josaa-35-4-515&id=382300)), buoy cameras, and [optical-flow-trajectory detection](https://doi.org/10.3390/rs14225691).

For poseidon: binarize rendered frames the same way — render nadir/high-angle with flat lighting (or export the foam-alpha channel directly), grayscale, then apply a PIP/histogram-curvature adaptive threshold rather than a hand-picked constant, so the procedure is identical on render and reference photo. Crucially, run two thresholds mirroring poseidon's own layering: strict, isolating the fresh-cap band (compare to WA), and permissive, including trail/wet-web/streak layers (compare to WB/WT). The Kleiss WT/WA = 1.5 versus classic WB/WA ~ 10 spread warns that published coverage numbers are threshold-definition-dependent; the dry-cap/wet-web/streak-film tonal split maps naturally onto this two-threshold practice.

### Field campaigns and downloadable ground truth

HiWinGS (North Atlantic 2013): 600+ twenty-minute fisheye video recordings with IMU-based projection, sustained U10N to 25 m/s (gusts higher), waves 1–10 m — the first shipborne W estimates at 25 m/s, showing W leveling off at no more than ~10% as a 20-minute average ([Brumer et al. 2017](https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/phoc/47/9/jpo-d-17-0005.1.xml)). SO GasEx (Southern Ocean 2008) is the companion dataset; GOTEX (2004) provides airborne nadir video at 10–23 m/s, fetch-limited. Immediately downloadable, no author contact needed: (1) the Schwendeman & Thomson 2015 data — processed whitecap coverage plus wind stress, wave slope, and dissipation from two North Pacific cruises, a single 4.15 MB MATLAB file "DataForSchwendemanThomsonJGR2015.mat" at [UW ResearchWorks](http://hdl.handle.net/1773/42596); (2) the [Malila et al. 2022 data](https://digital.lib.washington.edu/researchworks/items/adadf2e3-e751-4ede-8014-191333f1a6d1/full) — W and WA time series plus stereo-video-derived spectra from the Ekofisk North Sea platform and a Station Papa cruise, a 17.67 MB zip of CSV/tar.gz; (3) [MU-SSiD on Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/umairatwork/mu-ssid) — 100,800 visual-range sea images labeled Beaufort classes 1–4 from Malaysian coastal sites, the first public sea-state image dataset ([paper](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/9689093)); (4) raw HiWinGS imagery by author contact (Brumer/Zappa, LDEO). For extreme winds: Saildrone/NOAA hurricane-eyewall videos (e.g., SD-1045 in Hurricane Sam) with in-situ wind measurements, and coastal webcams paired with nearby NDBC buoys for U10 ground truth.

For poseidon: these supply reference imagery AND ground-truth scalars at matched U10 — rendered coverage can be scattered onto the same W-vs-U10 axes as real data points, not just against a fitted curve. MU-SSiD covers the low-wind regime (Beaufort 1–4) where poseidon's foam should be nearly absent — a negative control that FFT-Jacobian pipelines often fail (spurious folding foam in light wind).

### Coverage targets with exact coefficients

The curves to hit: [Monahan & O'Muircheartaigh 1980](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2008GL036165) W = 3.84×10⁻⁶·U10^3.41 (fraction; ~1% at 10 m/s), and the [Callaghan et al. 2008](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2008GL036165) AWE-derived piecewise cubic (W in %): W = 3.18×10⁻³(U10 − 3.70)³ for 3.70 < U10 ≤ 11.25 m/s and W = 4.82×10⁻⁴(U10 + 1.98)³ for 9.25 < U10 ≤ 23.09 m/s — branches intersecting at 10.18 m/s, valid 3.70–23.09 m/s, with essentially zero whitecaps below ~3.7 m/s. [Brumer et al. 2017](https://doi.org/10.1175/JPO-D-17-0005.1) showed wind-only power laws vary greatly between datasets (order-of-magnitude scatter at low winds is normal) while wind-wave-Reynolds-number parameterizations collapse GasEx-98, SO GasEx, Knorr11, and HiWinGS onto closely matching laws, with W saturating near 10% at U10N ~ 25 m/s. [Albert et al. 2016](https://acp.copernicus.org/articles/16/13725/2016/acp-16-13725-2016.pdf) compiles dozens of W(U10) parameterizations including satellite ones ([Anguelova & Bettenhausen 2019](http://magde.info/main/texts/journals/2019_JGR_AnguelovaBettenhausen_whitecapAlgorithm.pdf)). [Scanlon & Ward 2016](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/2015JC011230): separating active WA from maturing WB matters — WA dominates at low winds; WB increasingly dominates total WT as wind rises, because foam persists longer than it is created.

For poseidon: tune the fresh-cap band so the strict-threshold mask hits Callaghan-2008 W at four anchor winds (6, 10, 15, 20 m/s → ~0.04%, 0.8%, 2.9%, 5.1% by the piecewise cubic), verify near-zero below 3.7 m/s, and cap total foam at ~10% even in storm presets. Because real data scatter an order of magnitude at fixed U10, landing inside the Brumer-2017 scatter cloud — plotted with the downloadable datasets — is the honest acceptance criterion, not exact curve-matching. The WA-vs-WB split says the trail band, not the cap band, should carry most of the coverage growth at high wind.

### Patch-size distributions

[Bondur & Sharkov 1982] — the foundational aerial-photography study (aircraft at ~100 m altitude, 10,000 m² footprint), quoted in [Kleiss & Melville 2010](https://airsea.ucsd.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/10/2019/06/2010_Kleiss_Melville-Journal_of_Physical_Oceanography_vol_40.pdf) — separated dynamic foam (fresh caps) from static striplike foam and found individual whitecap areas peaking in the 8–16 m² range. [Sharkov's monograph](https://books.google.com/books/about/Breaking_Ocean_Waves.html?id=6_-hMx_gVeYC) (Breaking Ocean Waves, Springer 2007) treats the full spatio-temporal statistical geometry: patch sizes and lifetimes follow exponential/lognormal-family distributions, and the field of breaking centers is treated as a Poisson field. [Callaghan 2024](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2023JC020193) (lab-vs-field) reports probability distributions of maximum foam patch area and growth/decay timescales, a systematic positive correlation between decay time and maximum patch area, and self-similar area evolution in normalized time t*. [Reul & Chapron 2003](https://archimer.ifremer.fr/doc/00000/10693/9320.pdf) model per-patch thickness evolution with a lognormal distribution, mean ~1.9 cm. [Landsat imagery](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0034425720305174) (15 m pixels) has probed large-scale breaking statistics.

For poseidon: connected-component the binarized mask and histogram patch areas. Targets: a unimodal, broad, heavy-tailed distribution with fresh-cap patches peaking near 8–16 m² at moderate-to-fresh winds — the 144 m cascade tile at N = 256 gives ~0.56 m texels, so such patches span 25–50 texels, comfortably resolvable. Larger patches must persist longer (decay time ~ max area), which the per-texel accumulator provides naturally IF recovery is not spatially uniform — consider scaling recovery weakly by the coarse-mip regional turbulence signal. Artifact check: the histogram must be smooth — spikes at the three Voronoi-lace domain-warp scales would reveal the baked texture imprinting fake characteristic patch sizes.

### Fractal dimension of foam boundaries

[Kerman & Szeto 1994](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/07055900.1994.9649511) ("Fractal properties of whitecaps," Atmosphere-Ocean 32(3):531–551; [ADS record](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1994AtO....32..531K/abstract)) analyzed aircraft line-scanner images: the estimated fractal dimension of the whitecap field decreases from ~2.25 at 10% area coverage to ~1.7 at 0.1% coverage, and the cumulative intensity distribution is self-similar for the brightest ~10% of the image, invariant under successive box-averaging. [Kerman 1994](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/94JC00590) showed the scattered-light field of foam is multifractal, not monofractal, with a crossover between actively entraining whitecaps and passively dissipating foam; Kerman also proposed a [multifractal equivalent of the Beaufort scale](https://www.academia.edu/47343241/A_multifractal_equivalent_of_the_Beaufort_scale_for_sea_state). Practical box-counting on single foam photos yields boundary dimensions between 1 and 2 ([worked example](https://ronshnapp.wordpress.com/2021/08/28/calculating-the-fractal-dimension-of-sea-foam-from-an-image/)).

For poseidon: this is the single best dial-check for the lace/carve stack — box-count the binarized mask at each preset U10 and demand D rise with coverage along the Kerman–Szeto line (~1.7 at W = 0.1% up to ~2.25 at W = 10%). Too-smooth Jacobian-band foam (no carve) reads D too low; over-cranked domain warp plus three-scale Voronoi lace reads D too high and scale-invariant in the wrong band. Because the real field is multifractal with an active/residual crossover, compute D separately for the cap and trail bands — the cap band should be smoother (lower D) than the lacy residual web, matching the dry-cap vs wet-web layering.

### Breaking-crest length Λ(c): the spectrum-to-foam link

Phillips' Λ(c) is the average length of breaking crest per unit sea area per unit breaking-speed increment. [Kleiss & Melville 2010](https://airsea.ucsd.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/10/2019/06/2010_Kleiss_Melville-Journal_of_Physical_Oceanography_vol_40.pdf) (GOTEX, airborne video, 10–23 m/s) measured Λ(c) in 0.5 m/s bins from actively-breaking perimeter segments (optical flow plus brightness/curvature/area-growth criteria): the ensemble is roughly consistent with Phillips' c⁻⁶ tail but is not a constant power law — Λ(c) is well described by a Rayleigh distribution in c at slow/intermediate speeds; its first moment correlates with breaking rate and its second with active whitecap coverage (if breaking duration scales with wave period via Froude scaling, τ ~ T = 2πc/g, then WA ~ the second moment of Λ). Directional Λ(c) is predominantly unimodal and better aligned with wind than with the dominant-wave direction, broadest (sometimes bimodal) at slow c; maxima of the 4th/5th moments (momentum flux, dissipation) fall at c = 5–6.8 m/s. [Melville & Matusov 2002](https://www.nature.com/articles/417058a) (Nature 417:58) found exponential Λ(c) scaling as U10³. Field event breaking-front speeds cluster in a narrow 2–3.5 m/s band, weakly wind dependent ([Hwang](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1906.11202); see also [Kleiss & Melville 2011](https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/atot/28/2/2010jtecho744_1.xml) and [Irisov 2016](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/2015GL067352)).

For poseidon: Λ(c) ties the foam pattern to the FFT spectrum. In a rendered top-down video, extract fresh-cap leading edges by frame-differencing the cap band, measure their length and advance speed, bin into Λ(c). Targets: a Rayleigh-ish shape peaking at modest c; most breaking crest length at scales well below the spectral peak — the 144 m and 24 m cascades should produce most cap-band edge length, not the 1024 m cascade; crest-edge orientations aligned with wind, directly validating the wind-frame anisotropic carve direction. If caps only appear on dominant-wavelength crests, Λ(c) peaks at too-high c — a visible signature of thresholded-Jacobian foam that real seas do not have.

### Groupiness: foam comes in bursts

[Malila et al. 2022](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/2021JC017938) (JGR Oceans 127:e2021JC017938; stereo video at Ekofisk plus Station Papa; [open archive](https://bora.uib.no/bora-xmlui/handle/11250/2998099); [data](https://digital.lib.washington.edu/researchworks/items/adadf2e3-e751-4ede-8014-191333f1a6d1/full)): passing wave groups enhance the probability distribution of total coverage W by 2–3× and active coverage WA by ~5× — breaking is strongly clustered on wave-group scales, not Poisson-uniform, and they quantify intermittency with the telegraph approximation of the W time series. Kleiss & Melville found crest orientations concentrated about the wind; Kerman's multifractal results imply clustering across scales; Sharkov treats breaking-center fields as clustered point processes with measured spacing statistics.

For poseidon: compute the frame-by-frame coverage series W(t) of the rendered mask and check that it is intermittent, with burst spacing at the group period (envelope of the 1024/144 m cascades) and conditional coverage during group passage 2–3× the mean (5× for the cap band). An FFT ocean gives wave groups for free, so the accumulator should inherit this — but if carve thresholds or accumulator recovery flatten the temporal variance (W(t) nearly constant), the pattern reads as artificial uniform sprinkle even at correct mean coverage. Also check the radially-averaged 2D spectrum of the mask: energy near the dominant wavenumber and group scale, plus wind-direction anisotropy — not white noise.

### Temporal statistics: decay fits, lifetimes, advance speeds

[Callaghan et al. 2012](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/2012JC008147) (JGR 117:C09015; 552 breaking waves, Martha's Vineyard Coastal Observatory, 3–6 fps video): individual decay times from the exponential model A(t) = A0·exp(a + bt) (decay time = 1/b) range 0.2–10.4 s; the area-weighted mean varied between observation periods from 1.4 to 4.8 s (factor 3.4, attributed to surfactants); decay time correlates positively with event-averaged breaking speed and maximum patch area. Lab benchmarks: Monahan & Zietlow 1969 give a 3.85 s decay constant (28 °C salt water); [Callaghan et al. 2013](https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/phoc/43/6/jpo-d-12-0148.1.pdf) identify the two decay regimes (bubble-plume-controlled vs slower surfactant-stabilized). Growth vs decay: growth is faster in 2D lab breakers; in the ocean, breaking initiates on a short crest segment and spreads laterally along the crest, so field foam area grows more slowly ([Callaghan 2024](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2023JC020193)); area evolution is self-similar in normalized time t* and collapses until area falls to ~3% of max. Lifetime: [Korinenko et al.](https://hydrophysics.spbrc.ru/jour/article/view/676?locale=en_US) (Black Sea platform video) find exponential lifetime distributions with mean lifetime / breaking-wave period = 0.3 across conditions; the whitecap forms at the crest shifted ~9.6° of phase onto the forward face, then migrates from leading toward trailing edge, with max coverage ~21.6° of phase after onset. Crest advance: lab c_breaking = (0.7–0.9)·c_phase (Rapp & Melville 1990; Stansell & MacFarlane 2002; Banner & Peirson 2007); field event speeds mostly 2–3.5 m/s regardless of wind ([Hwang](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1906.11202)); individual event speeds decay self-similarly from their initial value ([Kleiss & Melville 2011](https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/atot/28/2/2010jtecho744_1.xml)). Stage A vs B lifetimes follow Monahan & Lu 1990; [IR imagery resolves the stage transition](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/283974039_Whitecap_lifetime_stages_from_infrared_imagery_with_implications_for_microwave_radiometric_measurements_of_whitecap_fraction) (Potter et al.).

For poseidon: four direct animation-timing checks. (1) The recover rate should give trail-band e-folding of 2–5 s in calm/clean presets, stretchable toward 8–10 s in high-wind/surfactant presets — measured by rendering a video, tracking one patch's band area, and fitting the exponential exactly as Callaghan does. (2) Cap-band lifetime should be ~0.3× the local breaking wave's period — a 7 s dominant wave carries a ~2 s bright cap — coupling the accumulator threshold width to cascade wavelength and arguing for per-cascade rather than global fresh-band widths. (3) The cap's leading edge should advance at 0.7–0.9× local phase speed (2–3.5 m/s absolute for typical events) while the trail is deposited behind and migrates toward the trailing face — the flow-warped carve coordinates (0.35× horizontal displacement) can be checked against this advance-vs-trail split. (4) Foam area growth should be slower and crest-parallel (lateral spreading), not an instantaneous full-crest flash — a known artifact of thresholded-Jacobian foam that the strain-driven carve thresholds can counteract.

### What counts as credible evaluation in graphics

[Dupuy & Bruneton 2012](https://inria.hal.science/hal-00967078v1) generate whitecaps from the horizontal-displacement Jacobian like poseidon; their key contribution is the analytic, linearly pre-filterable coverage estimator — treating J as Gaussian within a filter footprint, W = P(J < ε) = 0.5 + 0.5·erf((ε − μ_J)/(√2·σ_J)), computed from mip-filtered mean and variance (in [ocean.glsl](https://github.com/jdupuy/whitecaps/blob/master/ocean.glsl): whitecapCoverage(epsilon, mu, sigma2) = 0.5·erf(0.5·√2·(epsilon−mu)·inversesqrt(sigma2)) + 0.5, with a jacobian_scale threshold uniform), giving scale-consistent, antialiased coverage from centimeters to planetary scale. Evaluation in that paper — and in [Horvath 2015](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2791261.2791267) (DigiPro), which introduced TMA spectra and directional spreading to graphics — is qualitative: side-by-sides against photographs and consistency with empirical curves, no formal metric. The strongest methodology in fluids graphics is [Um, Hu & Thuerey 2017](https://ge.in.tum.de/publications/2017-sig-um/) (SIGGRAPH, ToG 36(4); [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.10257)): crowd-sourced 2AFC user studies against a real-world reference video of a matched setup — the presence of the reference video is what makes judgments consistent — yielding a per-method "visual accuracy" score. Surveys ([Darles et al. 2011](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/228927824_A_Survey_of_Ocean_Simulation_and_Rendering_Techniques_in_Computer_Graphics)) confirm ocean papers historically validate by visual comparison and performance, rarely statistics — so a statistics-based tuning protocol would exceed current publication practice in the field.

For poseidon: two direct borrows. (1) The erf estimator is a free analytic cross-check — poseidon already does coarse-mip neighbourhood reads, so it can compute μ and σ² of the Jacobian (or turbulence accumulator) per region and predict what coverage should be at the current threshold; if the fragment-shader layered result diverges from the erf prediction, the carve/lace stack is adding or eating coverage unintentionally — a drift regression test that runs headless. (2) For perceptual sign-off, follow Um et al.: pick three reference clips at known Beaufort forces, render matched poseidon clips (same framing via the capture rail presets, same sun elevation), and run small 2AFC comparisons, always with the reference video visible. Also adopt Horvath's practice of validating the input spectrum against NDBC buoy data, so pattern errors are not chased into foam dials when the underlying sea is wrong.

### The end-to-end tuning protocol

Setup. Pick anchor winds U10 = 6, 10, 15, 20, 25 m/s (Beaufort 4, 5, 7, 8, 10); let the sea reach statistical steady state (accumulator warmed up > 60 s). Render two products per anchor: [A] a nadir orthographic "science pass" of one 144 m tile region (or a 200×200 m window spanning cascade overlap) at ≥ 1024², flat unlit albedo or direct foam-alpha export, 10 fps for 120 s; [B] a perspective "perceptual pass" using the existing rail/close framings for Beaufort-photo side-by-sides.

Binarize. Grayscale the science pass; threshold per-frame with a Callaghan–White-style adaptive rule (PIP/histogram-curvature) at two levels: strict → cap mask (WA), permissive (trail/wet-web/streak film included) → total mask (WT). If exporting foam-alpha directly, binarize at the alpha levels visually corresponding to "bright breaking" vs "any visible foam."

Metrics per anchor. (1) Coverage: mean WA and WT over 120 s; targets: Callaghan-2008 piecewise cubic for WT (0.04/0.8/2.9/5.1% at 6/10/15/20 m/s), near-zero below 3.7 m/s, ≤ 10% at 25 m/s; WT/WA between ~1.5 (strict) and ~10 (generous); acceptance = inside the Brumer-2017 scatter cloud plotted with the Schwendeman–Thomson .mat points. (2) Patch histogram: connected components of the cap mask; a smooth heavy-tailed area PDF, mode ~8–16 m² at 10–15 m/s, no spikes at the Voronoi-lace scales; larger patches must decay slower (positive slope in per-patch max area vs fitted decay time). (3) Spatial statistics: radially-averaged FFT power spectrum of the mean-removed total mask — a bump near the dominant wavenumber plus group-scale energy plus wind-direction anisotropy growing with U10; box-counting fractal dimension of mask boundaries — D ≈ 1.7 (W = 0.1%) rising to ~2.25 (W = 10%) per Kerman–Szeto, with the trail band lacier (higher D) than the cap band. (4) Temporal: from the 10 fps sequence, W(t) burstiness (2–3× total, ~5× cap enhancement at wave-group passages); per-patch exponential decay fits with area-weighted mean e-folding 1.4–4.8 s; cap lifetime ≈ 0.3× local wave period; cap leading-edge advance 0.7–0.9× local phase speed (2–3.5 m/s typical), trail deposited behind the crest and migrating to the trailing face. (5) Analytic regression: erf-based coverage from Jacobian mip mean/variance versus actual rendered coverage (the Dupuy–Bruneton estimator) at every anchor — flags carve-stack drift headlessly. (6) Perceptual: 2AFC side-by-sides of pass [B] against Beaufort-matched reference clips (Um et al. protocol), verifying the qualitative gates: streaks absent below Force 7, present and wind-aligned above; scud/spray only Force 8+.

Order of tuning. Jacobian threshold plus accumulator gain first (hit the WA curve); then the recovery constant (decay e-folding plus WT/WA); then carve/lace/warp dials (patch histogram plus fractal D); then strain/flow-warp (advance speed plus groupiness) — each later stage re-checks stage-1 coverage via the erf regression.

For poseidon: every metric maps onto an actual dial — Jacobian threshold and accumulator gain (coverage), the min(J, recover) recovery constant (decay e-folding, WT/WA ratio), fresh-cap vs trail band widths (WA vs WB, lifetime/period = 0.3), Voronoi-lace scales plus domain warp (patch-histogram smoothness, fractal D), the wind-frame anisotropic carve (streak onset at Force 7, mask-spectrum anisotropy), the 0.35× flow-warped carve coordinates (leading-edge advance vs trail deposition), and the strain-driven carve thresholds (convergence merging, groupiness contrast). Every metric is computable offline from rendered frames with numpy/scipy (label, radial FFT, box counting, exponential fits) — no runtime changes needed beyond an optional foam-alpha debug output and the erf cross-check, which reuses existing coarse-mip reads ([Callaghan & White 2009](https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/atot/26/2/2008jtecho634_1.xml); [Callaghan et al. 2008](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2008GL036165); [Kerman & Szeto 1994](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/07055900.1994.9649511); [Callaghan et al. 2012](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/2012JC008147); [Malila et al. 2022](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/2021JC017938); [Schwendeman & Thomson dataset](http://hdl.handle.net/1773/42596); [Dupuy & Bruneton estimator](https://github.com/jdupuy/whitecaps/blob/master/ocean.glsl); [Um et al. 2017](https://ge.in.tum.de/publications/2017-sig-um/)).


## How shipped games do foam

### The consensus architecture

Every documented FFT ocean in a shipped game converges on the machinery poseidon already runs: a persistent per-texel turbulence buffer fed by the displacement Jacobian, decaying over time. WaveWorks/War Thunder's "turbulent energy" (inject where J < M ≈ 0.3–0.5; foam intensity = energy) and the foam sims of Crest and GodotOceanWaves are the same design — no shipped game does anything fundamentally different for open-ocean whitecaps without particles. Against that baseline, the survey's deltas reduce to a short list. First, **spatial dissipation**: War Thunder and ATLAS blur the energy texture as it fades (dissipation in time *and* space) so foam patches spread and soften as they age; Sea of Thieves goes further and makes progressive feedback-blur the entire dispersion model. A tiny blur in the accumulator pass, or age-weighted blending toward coarser mips at composite time, closes this gap for poseidon. Second, **strain feedback**: War Thunder modulates foam textures by both turbulent energy and current stretching (J > 1 thins, J < 1 thickens) — poseidon's strain-driven carve thresholds are precisely this technique, validated; the fresh cap band should stay keyed to raw instantaneous J (dense foam on actively-breaking areas) rather than the accumulator. Third, **anti-aliased distance foam** via Dupuy-Bruneton: store J and J² so mips carry mean and variance, then coverage = 0.5 + 0.5·erf(0.5·√2·(threshold − mean)/σ); ATLAS adds the complementary near-field fix of lerping variance to zero by clamp(0.25·mip) to undo bilinear-magnification bias. Fourth, **anti-stretch advection**: Naughty Dog's two-phase flow sampling — two coordinate sets offset by half an advection cycle, blended with abs(2·frac(t)−1), with spatially varying phase to hide the reset pulse. Fifth, **lifecycle constants that read right**: linear (or event-driven) growth with exponential decay (GodotOceanWaves' grow/decay rates; Crest's per-tick fade at a fixed 30 Hz sim rate for framerate-independent aging), and weather-coupled lifetime — AC3 made foam decay a per-Beaufort parameter interpolated between keyframes at levels 0/3/7/12. Sixth, **"one mask, artist-controlled decode" texturing**: AC3 packs three foam densities into RGB and decodes with a single artist ramp; Sea of Thieves blends its blurred mask with hand-authored textures; War Thunder's 2026 update adds a micro-relief normal map so specular glides across bubbles — the ramp-decode and foam micro-normal are the two cheap refinements worth stealing on top of poseidon's 3-scale domain-warped Voronoi lace.
