Seventh, **foam feeds back into shading, not just albedo**: ATLAS raises roughness under foam, War Thunder adds energy-modulated "milkiness" to refraction, Uncharted uses foam to modulate apparent water depth — poseidon's submerged-grey band should act in the water-shading terms. Finally, Horizon Forbidden West drives breaking-wave foam purely by wave age past the break point, independently confirming poseidon's accumulator-recovery-as-age trail band; and the extension paths — splatting local events into the turbulence texture (World of Warships' deformation particles; Crest's RegisterFoamInput) and depth-threshold shoreline deposit (Crest; War Thunder's sawtooth Gerstner shore foam) — all reuse the existing accumulator.

### War Thunder and the WaveWorks lineage: turbulent energy with dual dissipation

[Ocean simulation and rendering in War Thunder (Tcheblokov, CGDC 2015)](https://developer.download.nvidia.com/assets/gameworks/downloads/regular/events/cgdc15/CGDC2015_ocean_simulation_en.pdf) is the definitive Jacobian-foam pipeline. The spectrum is split into 4 cascades (tile sizes ~5 m to ~1 km), faded and excluded with distance. Basic foam: J is the Jacobian of the flat→displaced transform; J > 1 is stretched, J < 1 squeezed, J < 0 self-overlap (breaking). They threshold at M ≈ 0.3..0.5 (not 0) and modulate foam textures by saturate(k·(−J+M)) — with the stated problem that "Foam disappears!" the instant J recovers. Advanced foam fixes this: breaking areas inject turbulent energy into per-cascade energy textures; energy dissipates over time (exponential fade) *and* in space (blur), simulated per cascade in a pixel-shader pass and summed at render. Turbulent energy *is* foam intensity, and foam textures are modulated by both energy and instantaneous stretching (stretched thins the layer, squeezed thickens it). Two extra layers: dense opaque foam on actively-breaking areas (J < M right now), and "milkiness" — mixed-in bubbles — added to the refraction color, modulated by energy. Shore foam uses analytic Gerstner waves with a sawtooth profile directly as the foam mask, scaled by depth from a distance-field texture (RGBA8: depth, distance-to-shore, DF gradient; 4k×4k for a 65 km world), group speed = phase speed / 2, plus a downwind "openness" texture that automatically kills ocean foam in lakes, rivers, and the lee of islands. The 2026 ["Ninth Wave" update](https://warthunder.com/en/news/9957-development-ninth-wave-new-water-and-naval-battle-effects-en) adds foam generated in turbulent zones where wavefronts collide (vortex/resonance physics rather than a random mask) and a micro-relief overlay normal map on foam, giving a slowly settling 3D-suspension look (see also [NVIDIA WaveWorks](https://developer.nvidia.com/waveworks)).

For poseidon: this is the closest published ancestor and validates the architecture — the persistent per-texel min(J, recover) accumulator *is* the turbulent-energy buffer, and the strain-driven carve thresholds *are* stretch modulation (exactly the divergence merge/thin rule). Three concrete upgrades: (1) add the spatial half of dissipation — a cheap 3×3 blur or mip-bounce in the accumulator compute pass so trails diffuse outward while fading; (2) keep the two-term split explicit: dense "currently breaking" from instantaneous J < M layered over the decaying energy term — fresh cap and trail bands map 1:1, with the fresh band sourced from raw J, not the accumulator; (3) apply energy-modulated milkiness into the refracted/scattered water color under foam — the submerged-grey layer acting in water shading, not only foam albedo. The Ninth Wave micro-normal is a cheap sparkle win: reuse the lace texture's gradient as a normal perturbation in the specular term.

### ATLAS: per-band energy, moments-based filtering, foam-driven roughness

The GPUOpen slides for [Wakes, Explosions and Lighting: Interactive Water Simulation in ATLAS (Mihelich & Tcheblokov, GDC 2019)](https://gpuopen.com/gdc-presentations/2019/gdc-2019-agtd6-interactive-water-simulation-in-atlas.pdf) give the full production pipeline. Spectrum: dual fetch-limited JONSWAP (local wind sea + swell) split into 4 frequency bands, each a small FFT recombined in shaders; bands fade out starting ~30 world-space periods from camera. Per-step texture layout per band: slice1 = (Dx, Dy, Dz); slice2 = (E[x-slope], E[y-slope], foam intensity, displacement Jacobian); slice3 = second moments (E[x²], E[y²], E[xy]) for LEADR-style specular. The foam algorithm, verbatim from the slide: "Calculate Jacobian of displacements per frequency band; if above threshold we are on a wave top; inject some amount of turbulent energy; dissipate it over time (blur + fade); sum up turbulent energy from all bands on rendering; modulate foam texture by turbulent energy." Shading lerps between water radiance and foam color by foam density *and* increases roughness in foam-covered areas for the sun integral. Anti-aliasing: because bilinear magnification isn't linear, they lerp second-order moments toward squares of first-order moments by clamp(0.25·mip, 0, 1) (variance → 0 up close), and lerp bilinear→bicubic filtering for the most detailed band. Spray: sprite particles are emitted everywhere in the camera frustum, then each particle samples the world-space foam/whitecap texture; if foam_wave_hats ≤ WaveHatThreshold the particle sets LifeTime = −1 and never renders — GPU-side culling instead of GPU spawning (a UE4 Cascade limitation). An interactive-wakes prototype used Tessendorf's eWave solver, with foam injected and evolved in the wake sim with the "same math as wind waves" then combined with wind-wave foam (see also the [GDC session video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Dqld965-Vv0) and [NVIDIA's WaveWorks 2.0 in ATLAS post](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-waveworks-2-0-debuts-in-grapeshot-games-atlas/)).

For poseidon: three transplants. (1) Per-cascade foam — poseidon accumulates one turbulence value from the combined Jacobian; ATLAS/WaveWorks accumulate per band and sum at render, letting small-cascade foam flicker fast while large-cascade foam persists. With 3 cascades poseidon could store 3 accumulators in the RGB of one texture at negligible cost, giving natural multi-scale foam lifetimes. (2) The roughness boost under foam is missing from most hobby renderers and nearly free: drive GGX roughness up by foam coverage before the specular term. (3) The variance-fix pattern (lerp toward the unfiltered value by the 0.25·mip clamp) is the same trick poseidon should apply to its coarse-mip regional reads to avoid double-filtering artifacts when carving.

### Dupuy & Bruneton 2012: statistically correct coverage at any distance

[Real-time Animation and Rendering of Ocean Whitecaps (Dupuy & Bruneton, SIGGRAPH Asia 2012)](https://hal.science/hal-00967078) observes that the Jacobian breaking criterion is linear in wave-spectrum products, so J and J² can be stored per cascade and prefiltered by ordinary mipmapping. At shade time, sum per-cascade means (jm = jm1+jm2+jm3+jm4 across 4 grid sizes), compute variance σ² = max(E[J²] − Σ jm_i², 0), and whitecap coverage becomes a closed-form Gaussian CDF: W = 0.5·erf(0.5·√2·(ε − μ)/√σ²) + 0.5, with ε the artist Jacobian threshold ("jacobian_scale"). Foam radiance is then W · ((Lsun·NdotL + Esky)/π) · 0.4 added on top. Because the criterion prefilters linearly, distant pixels containing thousands of wavelets get statistically correct fractional coverage with zero shimmer, from centimeters to planetary scale. Reference GLSL is public in [jdupuy/whitecaps ocean.glsl](https://github.com/jdupuy/whitecaps/blob/master/ocean.glsl) (presentation: [PDF](https://inria.hal.science/hal-00967078/file/Whitecaps-presentation.pdf)).

For poseidon: the single highest-leverage technique for horizon quality. Upgrading the existing coarse-mip neighbourhood reads to (mean, variance) of the Jacobian — writing J and J² into the derivatives map or accumulator alpha and letting WebGPU mipmap them — turns distance foam from a thresholded lookup into analytically anti-aliased coverage. The erf can be a smoothstep approximation. It also gives a principled fade for the carve: as variance grows with distance, collapse the carved lace toward flat coverage W. Fully fragment-shader-only, using mip generation poseidon already has.

### Sea of Thieves: feedback blur as the whole dispersion model

Rare's [The Technical Art of Sea of Thieves (SIGGRAPH 2018)](https://history.siggraph.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2018-Talks-Ang_The-Technical-Art-of-Sea-of-Thieves.pdf) confirms a straight Tessendorf FFT ocean. Foam is generated (1) at wave peaks "using the method described in the reference paper" (Tessendorf's Jacobian folding criterion) and (2) around objects intersecting the surface, via depth-buffer comparisons within a camera-centered window. The foam signal is written to a buffer that is progressively blurred *with feedback* each frame — the blur-accumulate loop is itself the dissipation model, spreading and softening foam over time into a deliberately softer, stylized mask, which is then blended with artist-authored foam textures (the mask decides where, the texture decides what foam looks like). Sea state (calm/normal/storm) modulates all three stages — generation amount, dispersion speed, and texture blending — and calm water shows only object-intersection foam. Water color adds a wave-peak mask from FFT choppiness offsets that boosts subsurface color at crests, so peaks read brighter and greener before foam even appears ([ACM page](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3214745.3214820), [talk video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y9BOz2dFZzs)).

For poseidon: the persistent min(J, recover) accumulator already plays the role of SoT's feedback buffer, but SoT adds spatial spreading — blurring the accumulator, or intentionally sampling it at a coarser mip and blending toward it as foam ages, makes trails grow outward and soften as they decay instead of just fading in place; poseidon's coarse-mip neighbourhood reads can emulate this for free by weighting the trail band toward coarser mips with accumulator age. The wave-peak subsurface mask is a cheap pre-foam tonal cue under the fresh cap band. Object foam is screen-space and out of scope by design.

### Assassin's Creed III / Black Flag: Beaufort-keyed decay and the ramp-decoded texture

AC3's ocean ([GDC 2013, Rendering Assassin's Creed III, J-F St-Amour](https://gdcvault.com/play/1017710/Rendering-Assassin-s-Creed); detailed by [fxguide](https://www.fxguide.com/fxfeatured/assassins-creed-iii-the-tech-behind-or-beneath-the-action/); video mirror on [archive.org](https://archive.org/details/GDC2013StAmour)) keys everything to the Beaufort scale 0–12 with keyframes at levels 0/3/7/12 and interpolation between them; each level defines surface scale, height scale, choppiness, *and foam decay* — foam lifetime is a weather parameter, not a constant. Foam levels are precomputed at wave edges each frame from the precomputed tiling/cycling FFT displacement set, then modified temporally (dispersal rate). Texturing: one RGB texture holds three grayscale foam densities — coarse (R), sparse (G), medium (B) — and a 1D artist color ramp decides the mix as intensity rises: at ~0.1 on the ramp, mostly coarse; at ~0.8, all coarse + all sparse + ~50% medium. Artists only ever edit the ramp. Coastal foam is baked offline: terrain topology sampled at 512×512 for a 4×4 km map (~8 m precision), Gaussian-blurred with Perlin noise added to feather and expand the shore band. The water composite layers diffuse, spec, normal, reflection, depth/tint, refraction, faked SSS on backlit wave undersides, plus the foam layers. Skull & Bones is the same lineage (AC3 → AC Origins → S&B per [Ubisoft's Q&A](https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/water-water-everywhere-a-q-a-with-ubisoft-s-i-skull-and-bones-i-team)) with wind-aligned spray and a dedicated full-time water artist; no algorithmic details published.

For poseidon: two directly liftable ideas. (1) The 3-density-channels + ramp scheme is a cleaner formalization of the tonal layers — bake the Voronoi lace at three densities (or treat the 3 domain-warped scales as pseudo-channels) and drive the mix with a single ramp indexed by accumulator value, so dry cap / wet web / streak film become ramp stops an artist tunes without touching shader logic. (2) Make the "recover" constant a function of the wind/sea-state uniform, AC3-style: heavier seas keep trails alive longer, calm seas eat them fast — one uniform buys weather coherence for the whole foam system.

### Uncharted: the flow/advection anti-stretch canon

Naughty Dog's flow shader (invented for Drake's Fortune, formalized in [Water Technology of Uncharted, GDC 2012](https://www.slideshare.net/agebreak/water-technologyofunchartedgdc2012); [PDF mirror](https://cgzoo.files.wordpress.com/2012/04/water-technology-of-uncharted-gdc-2012.pdf); [GDC Vault](https://gdcvault.com/play/1015309/Water-Technology-of)) advects texture UVs along a flow field but samples *twice* with phases offset by half a cycle, blending with a triangle wave. Pseudo-code from the [Rendering Rapids in Uncharted 4 deck (SIGGRAPH 2016)](http://advances.realtimerendering.com/s2016/Rendering%20rapids%20in%20Uncharted%204.pptx): `fTime = frac(vec2(t, t*0.5)); posA = pos.xz - flowDir*fTime.x...; posB = pos.xz - flowDir*fTime.y...; result = blend(sampleA, sampleB, abs(2*frac(t)-1))`. Each sample resets before it distorts too far; maximum blend weight lands exactly when the other layer is at maximum distortion. Refinements: offset the UV starting position and vary the phase offset spatially (breaking the global "pulse"), optional texture-feedback ping-pong, and UVs must scroll *opposite* the intended direction. Foam (2012): modulated by wave amplitude (multipliers painted into the flow grid via Maya tools), advected with the same flow as the normal maps, appearance via a threshold on a gradient field (their ramp trick), and the foam texture also modulates apparent water depth for a pseudo-volumetric effect. Uncharted 3/4 geometry: 4 Gerstner swells + 4 wave-particle grids (one particle set sampled at 4 octaves/scales), each grid advected at different speeds along the flow map, amplitude-controlled by an artist RGBA map. U4 control maps: flow map (direction+magnitude, 2 channels), 16-bit height packed in 2 channels of DXT5 (x + y/256), alpha cull mask, normals — flow maps generated from Houdini FLIP sims plus artist-drawn direction curves. PS4 timings for fullscreen ocean: wave particles ~3 ms, mesh gen <4 ms, render ~0.2 ms components. They flag TAA as an unsolved pain: foam/flow appearance changes phase per frame, so even correct motion vectors blur foam.

For poseidon: the flow-warped carve coordinates (single warp at 0.35x horizontal displacement) accumulate distortion indefinitely for stationary foam patches; the two-phase blend is the exact fix — sample the Voronoi lace at two phase-offset advected coordinate sets, blend with abs(2·frac(t)−1), add per-texel spatial phase offset (hash of wind-frame coords) to hide the reset pulse. Cost: one extra texture sample per carve layer. Also reusable: foam-modulates-perceived-depth (darken water under thick foam to fake submerged bubble columns, complementing the submerged-grey band); and their threshold-on-gradient-field foam is the same family as poseidon's strain-driven carve thresholds.

### Horizon Forbidden West: foam as wave age — and a warning about vertex color

Hugh Malan's [Rendering Water in Horizon Forbidden West (SIGGRAPH 2022 Advances)](https://advances.realtimerendering.com/s2022/SIGGRAPH2022-Advances-Water-Malan.pdf) bakes breaking waves as a single animated cross-section (Houdini sim → hand-cleaned curve) stored as a 2D texture — each animation frame is one row of XYZ offsets as RGB, with a companion texture of partial derivatives for tangent frames and a UV-compensation map, because the deformation squashes vertices together at the curl (explicit anti-stretch correction baked offline). A compute shader deforms grid vertices inside artist-authored wavefront quads; U = back-to-front position, V = animation parameter along the wavefront. One cross-section animation serves every breaking wave in the game. Wavefront shape and timing come from artist "shape curves", "guide curves", and "animation curves" (Coons-patch interpolation baked to a grid, streamed with world tiles). Foam appears where the animation parameter passes the break point (a bright green curve in tools) — coverage is a direct function of wave age past breaking, passed to the water shader *through vertex color* along with relative height and deformation strength; a per-wavefront variation texture (one row per wavefront) scales deformation strength to create natural gaps where the wave doesn't break. Admitted weaknesses: vertex-color foam can't create sub-triangle features, causing undersampling and popping on the breaker's front face; surface foam overall (beach interaction, entity wakes, flow around rocks) is what they most want to improve, citing Weta's "Guided Bubbles and Wet Foam" as the aspirational model. The [2024 SIGGRAPH follow-up (Lopatin, Vossers, Malan)](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3641233.3664308) extends the representation to approximation curves handling overhangs and topology changes within strict budgets (course index: [SIGGRAPH 2022 Advances](https://www.advances.realtimerendering.com/s2022/index.html)).

For poseidon: two lessons. (1) HFW derives foam purely from "how long past breaking" — the same semantics as accumulator-recovery age, independently validating age-driven tonal banding (fresh cap → trail). (2) A warning poseidon already avoids: carrying foam in vertex data undersamples badly — HFW's popping foam is the argument *for* the per-texel accumulator with fragment-shader compositing. Their baked UV-compensation map is the offline analogue of poseidon's anti-stretch problem: where displacement compresses the surface, adjust sampling coordinates — approximable at runtime by scaling carve UVs by the local Jacobian stretch term so lace features stay metric.

### Crest: fixed-rate persistence and two-threshold layering

[Crest](https://crest.readthedocs.io/en/4.12/user/ocean-simulation.html) (Unity, Wave Harmonic) runs a dedicated persistent foam simulation over its LOD-data cascade textures at a configurable frequency — default 30 updates/s, decoupled from frame rate, so dissipation is framerate-independent. Deposit: foam is added where wave crests are "pinched" (determinant of the displacement Jacobian) scaled by Wave Foam Strength, with Wave Foam Coverage raising or lowering the detection threshold; a second deposit source adds foam in shallow water (below Shoreline Foam Max Depth, scaled by Shoreline Foam Strength) to fake shore splash. Decay: every sim update multiplicatively reduces foam by Foam Fade Rate. Arbitrary geometry, textures, or vertex colors can inject foam through RegisterFoamInput (boat wakes, etc.). Rendering pulls *two* visual layers from different thresholds of the same scalar with black-point fade blending — a bright surface whitecap layer on top and a submerged bubble layer beneath — and the foam texture is world-space mapped at power-of-2 scales so floating-origin shifts don't pop (see also the [USERGUIDE](https://github.com/ajweeks/crest-oceanrender/blob/master/USERGUIDE.md) and [water-resources hub](https://github.com/wave-harmonic/water-resources)).

For poseidon: the two-threshold/black-point-fade layering is the cleanest published match for the layered tonal system — one scalar, multiple bands via thresholds with soft knees, which poseidon already does (cap vs trail). Crest's addition is running decay at a fixed sim rate so trail age is framerate-independent — directly relevant to a browser renderer swinging 30–120 Hz: scale "recover" by real dt, or tick the accumulator pass at fixed Hz. The shallow-water deposit is a cheap future shoreline feature: add foam wherever ocean depth < threshold.

### GodotOceanWaves: the browser-scale peer

[GodotOceanWaves (2Retr0)](https://github.com/2Retr0/GodotOceanWaves) is an open Godot 4 FFT ocean with near-identical architecture to poseidon: multiple cascades sharing compute pipelines, a TMA (JONSWAP × depth attenuation) spectrum with Hasselmann directional spread plus a swell-elongation parameter, and a small-wave suppression term exp(−k²(1−δ)²). Foam is generated where wave peaks curl into themselves (negative displacement Jacobian); "foam accumulates linearly and dissipates exponentially on a texture over multiple wave updates," controlled by explicit "foam grow rate" and "foam decay rate" parameters. Cascade start times are auto-offset to decorrelate interference. Sea spray uses GPUParticles distributed evenly over the surface and culled by sampling foam amount (only particles on foamy texels live), rendered as billboards that scale and displace over lifetime with a dissolve for atomization — with the acknowledged weakness that raising particle count barely raises density because most get culled. A shading detail worth noting: normal maps mix bicubic and bilinear filtering based on world-space pixel density to fight aliasing (comparable implementation: [godot4-oceanfft](https://github.com/tessarakkt/godot4-oceanfft)).

For poseidon: direct peer validation of the compute-accumulator design at hobby/browser scale. The asymmetric response curve — *linear* accumulation, *exponential* decay — is worth copying exactly: poseidon's min(J, recover) is effectively linear decay, and switching recovery to exponential (value *= exp(−k·dt)) gives long low-intensity tails that read naturally as scud/streak film, matching the outermost tonal band. The bicubic/bilinear mix-by-pixel-density also applies to derivative-map sampling at grazing angles.

### World of Warships and Call of Duty: WWII: splat it or bake it

[Sea Surface Visualization in World of Warships (Kryachko, SIGGRAPH 2016)](https://history.siggraph.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2016-Talks-Kryachko_Sea-Surface-Visualization-in-World-of-Warships.pdf) superposes height maps (GPU Gems 2 lineage) on a projected grid, corrected per-pixel with Newton-iteration ray casting for stability; water deformations (shell splashes, wakes) are "special particles" that render *both* the surface deformation and its foam into the water's data maps — foam is a byproduct of the deformation particle, giving high-resolution local foam without a global sim. Full quality costs 4.2 ms GPU on an HD 7970 at 1080p (follow-up: [WoWs GDC 2018, Rendering High-Quality Sea 'Till Horizon](https://www.gdcvault.com/play/1025312/)). [Creating Real-Time Oceans for Call of Duty: WWII (Vitalone, GDC 2018)](https://player.vimeo.com/video/261901539) bakes a looping Houdini Ocean Toolkit + FLIP sim driving real-time surfaces at 60 fps, with foam masks from the offline sim data (talk exists only as video; summary at [80.lv](https://80.lv/articles/creating-real-time-oceans-for-call-of-duty-wwii)). Both sit at the "bake or splat it" end of the spectrum, opposite the Jacobian-energy end.

For poseidon: mostly context, but the WoWs pattern — a splat that writes deformation *and* foam into the same data maps — is the minimal-machinery way to later add local events (boat wake, impact) without particles or history: render a quad into the turbulence accumulator, and the entire existing carve/tonal pipeline applies for free.

### The baseline without a foam sim, and two verified negatives

UE5's built-in Water plugin uses Gerstner waves and provides only material-driven, depth-based shoreline foam (scene depth vs water depth drives a foam texture near shores, several textures layered at different scales) — no Jacobian, no persistence, no dynamic whitecaps, the most common community complaint; shipped UE oceans get real foam from custom compute (as ATLAS did on UE4 with WaveWorks) or marketplace FFT/Niagara systems where "the wave Jacobian detects areas of wave convergence... foam trails persist for several seconds and dissipate naturally" ([StraySpark UE5 guide](https://www.strayspark.studio/blog/ocean-water-simulation-ue5-guide); [Epic forums thread](https://forums.unrealengine.com/t/whitecaps-and-foam-for-a-dynamic-ocean/56746)). For poseidon: confirmation it is already past the engine baseline — slope/depth material foam alone reads static — while the depth-difference shoreline recipe remains the standard cheap coastal treatment if coasts arrive.

God of War and Ghost of Tsushima have no published ocean-foam deep dives — verified by exhaustive search of GDC Vault, SIGGRAPH archives, and studio blogs. Santa Monica's public 2019/2023 talks cover [wind simulation (Rupert Renard)](https://gdcvault.com/play/1026404/Wind-Simulation-in-God-of), vegetation, lighting, and [Rendering 'God of War Ragnarok'](https://gdcvault.com/play/1029298/Rendering-God-of-War-Ragnarok) — none document the Lake of Nine water/foam pipeline. Sucker Punch's material ([Samurai Landscapes, GDC 2021](https://gdcvault.com/play/1027352/Samurai-Landscapes-Building-and-Rendering), the Blowing from the West wind talk, Samurai Shading SIGGRAPH 2020, Real-Time Samurai Cinema 2021, and the [Ghost of Yotei 2025 tech deep dive](https://blog.playstation.com/2025/10/23/ghost-of-yotei-tech-deep-dive/)) covers terrain, wind, shading, sky, and GPU particles; water appears only as particle interactions — leaves, blood, lanterns riding currents ([PlayStation Blog VFX piece](https://blog.playstation.com/2021/01/12/how-stunning-visual-effects-bring-ghost-of-tsushima-to-life/)). For poseidon: don't hunt these as references — the documented state of the art for FFT-ocean foam is the War Thunder/ATLAS/Dupuy-Bruneton lineage plus Sea of Thieves' stylization pass; Ghost of Tsushima's admired water is visually a Gerstner/heightmap sea with strong shading and particles, not a published foam algorithm.

## How film VFX does whitewater

### Four signals and an energy multiplier

Film emission criteria reduce to four signals poseidon can already compute per-fragment: deformation eigenvalues of the displacement Jacobian (λmin = onset-of-folding, per Tessendorf; stretch/squish = Houdini's deformation source); crest convexity gated by velocity-normal alignment (Ihmsen's v̂·n̂ ≥ 0.6); acceleration/velocity-fluctuation versus a low-pass (Weta's aeration = Reynolds stress / surface tension — poseidon's coarse-mip reads *are* the low-pass); and a kinetic-energy *multiplier* on everything (Ihmsen's n_d = I_k·(k_ta·I_ta + k_wc·I_wc); Moana birthed bubbles by particle energy in VEX). The headline upgrades: accumulate the minimum eigenvalue λmin = ½(Jxx+Jyy) − ½√((Jxx−Jyy)²+4Jxy²) instead of det J — Tessendorf calls it "the actual signal of the onset of folding" (fires earlier, no false negatives in mixed strain), and its eigenvector ê− gives a free per-pixel anisotropy frame, since foam folds align perpendicular to ê−. Poseidon's persistent turbulence accumulator is exactly Tessendorf 2022's published whitecap map O (boost to 1 when λmin < λT, exponential decay with half-life 1–8 s), and that paper supplies the missing calibration: histogram λmin → CDF, then solve W(1−α)/(1−Wα) = CDF(λT) with Monahan coverage W = 3.84e-6·U^3.41, so the cap threshold follows wind-speed presets automatically (published thresholds ranged 0.034 → 0.534 from calm to 25 m/s — a fixed threshold can't serve multiple sea states). The foam/spray/bubble classification (Ihmsen: <6 fluid neighbors = spray, >20 = bubble, else foam; soft 0–1 states in Houdini) maps 1:1 onto poseidon's tonal layers, and each class advects differently — spray ballistic (scud should out-run the surface downwind), foam position-advected with weak drag (Weta's χΦ = 0.05–0.5 s⁻¹ window vindicates the mild 0.35x flow-warp; fully locked foam looks "stringy"), bubbles buoyant and lagging (submerged grey trails everything). Foam lifetime in film is probabilistic, not fixed: Houdini computes a per-frame death chance from age plus local density (erosion kills sparse foam, preserves dense patches — poseidon's coverage-riding dissolve threshold is this rule); Weta bursts wet foam on a normal distribution (mean 1.5–2 s, variance 0.5 s²); Ihmsen scales lifetime by emission potential so energetic breaks leave longer trails. The cellular foam-patch look is *manufactured*, not simulated, at every studio — Houdini seeds "repellent" particles, Disney's Moana used Voronoi patterns outright — poseidon's 3-scale domain-warped F2−F1 lace is the shader-space equivalent, and should fade to solid in the fresh cap band and gain contrast and coarseness with age (Weta's cohesion clumping grows clump size over time). Sub-pixel foam becomes surface texture through a mask-then-layer chain poseidon already implements at the final rung, and the scale anchors say the lace must carry it: foam clump structure lives at 5 mm–12 cm (Weta bubble radii 0.5–5 mm, cohesion radius 5–12 radii), far below FFT texel size. Target screen coverage from Monahan: ≈1% at 10 m/s wind, ≈10% at 20 m/s, ≈22% at 25 m/s, with an e^(0.0861·ΔT) air-sea temperature factor from Premoze-Ashikhmin as a free climate control. One archival note: no SIGGRAPH talk titled "Foundation of the Sea" exists — the Moana material is spread across the Palmer/Frost/Byun 2017 Wet-and-Wild session talks plus "Rigging the Oceans" (SA 2016).

### Houdini's Whitewater Source: the emission criteria stack

Houdini's [Whitewater Source](https://www.sidefx.com/docs/houdini/nodes/sop/whitewatersource.html) computes several independent per-voxel/per-point emission signals, each linearly remapped to a (0,1) emission probability between a user min/max range with an optional custom remap ramp ("Compute Range from Data" auto-fits the range to the current frame's min/max). The signals: (1) **Curvature** — SDF curvature of the (smoothed) fluid surface, gated by "Max Velocity Angle", the angle between fluid velocity and surface normal; emission only where velocity is roughly along the normal, isolating the leading edge/lip of breaking waves (high-res sims need surface smoothing first or spurious curvature emits everywhere). (2) **Acceleration** — Eulerian acceleration at fixed points; catches impacts, rejoining splashes, and trapped-air events that curvature misses. (3) **Vorticity** — magnitude of curl of velocity; churning regions that "generally occur deeper below the surface" (a bubble source, not a cap source). (4) **Deformation** — principal strain eigenvalues of the surface deformation: "Stretch" = max expansion eigenvalue along one direction, "Squish" = max compression eigenvalue, "Surface Scale" = expansion/compression across all directions, each with its own scale, range, and remap. (5) A **Speed gate** — below min speed no emission, above max always emit. (6) **Splash** — relative particle density with a negative mapping, so loosely packed (ballistic) particles emit. (7) **Pressure** — pressure-gradient alignment. The final emission is a probability field seeded stochastically, optionally limited by a depth band ("Limit by Depth") (context overview: [Whitewater SOP](https://www.sidefx.com/docs/houdini/fluid/sopwhitewater.html)).

For poseidon: the derivatives maps already carry the raw inputs for four of these — the displacement Jacobian gives the deformation eigenvalues exactly (stretch = λmax, squish = λmin, surface scale = det J or trace), and the strain-driven carve threshold is precisely Houdini's stretch/squish pair; keep them as two separate signals rather than one scalar (compression accumulates foam into ridges, stretch thins and dissolves it, matching the merge/thin carve behavior). The "Max Velocity Angle" gate has a shader analog: emit fresh cap only where the crest moves into the wind-frame forward direction (sign of the horizontal displacement derivative along wind), suppressing false caps on wave backs. And Houdini's practice of auto-fitting remap ranges to each frame's min/max suggests normalizing the accumulator bands against a coarse-mip regional min/max so foam thresholds self-adapt to sea state.

### Houdini's Whitewater Solver: probabilistic death, erosion, and repellents

The [Whitewater Solver](https://www.sidefx.com/docs/houdini/nodes/dop/whitewatersolver.html) gives whitewater particles no prescribed lifetime — a "death chance" is computed per particle per frame from (a) real age versus the statistical "Lifespan" parameter, (b) per-class "Aging Rates" (separate Bubbles/Foam/Spray rates multiplying death probability without touching the real age attribute), and (c) with "Enable Erosion", local neighborhood density: erosion "preserves foam in denser areas and erodes it in sparser regions" (Erosion Strength = faster death in sparse foam; Preservation Strength = a density range immune to erosion; both within a Depth Range of the surface). Classification is soft: "Add State Attributes" writes bubble/foam/spray floats in 0–1 "signalling how strongly each particle is of the respective state". Forces are depth-ramped: buoyancy (Base Buoyancy × a Buoyancy-by-Depth ramp), advection strength by depth, plus a "Foam Location" offset raising or lowering the foam layer. Depth Control is an adhesion constraint keeping foam on the surface ("Upper Surface Only", stiffness by depth — lower stiffness = thicker foam layer; disabled when particle velocity deviates from the normal by more than "Off Velocity Angle"). Density Control is a PBF-style constraint projection (Neighborhood Size target, Constraint Stiffness, Tensile Radius/Strength for inter-particle repulsion) producing foam clumping. And the cellular machine: the solver seeds and advects a second particle system of **repellants** that push whitewater away "and give rise to a cellular foam structure" — the classic bald-patch look of real sea foam. Each repellent has a radius (Feature Size Range), magnitude (Strength Range), noise (0 = circular hole, 1 = maximally noisy shape), pulse (evolution rate of the noisy shape), optional life range, and is only seeded where whitewater density exceeds a threshold; repellent force is attenuated by liquid speed and acceleration ramps so active breaking regions stay solid white and only calm, aging foam opens into cells (context: [Whitewater DOP overview](https://www.sidefx.com/docs/houdini/fluid/whitewater.html)).

For poseidon: this is the strongest validation of the architecture — the Voronoi-edge (F2−F1) lace texture is a closed-form stand-in for repellents: repellent "radius" = Voronoi cell scale (poseidon's 3 scales = the repellent size distribution), "noise" = domain-warp amplitude, "pulse" = warp animation rate. Two behaviors worth copying into the shader: (1) repellent strength attenuates where the liquid is fast or accelerating — so the lace carve should fade to solid white in the fresh cap band and open up only in the trail band (gate carve strength by accumulator age and a coarse-mip "activity" read); (2) erosion kills sparse foam faster than dense foam — poseidon's dissolve-threshold-riding-coverage (commit 6bee2b3) is exactly this rule, with the suggested refinement of also *preserving* foam wherever regional coarse-mip coverage exceeds a threshold, not just biasing the dissolve. The per-class aging rates justify different recovery rates per tonal layer: spray/cap dies fastest, submerged grey slowest.

### Ihmsen et al. 2012: the unified spray/foam/bubbles model Houdini descends from

[Unified Spray, Foam and Bubbles for Particle-Based Fluids (Ihmsen, Akinci, Akinci, Teschner, CGI 2012)](https://cg.informatik.uni-freiburg.de/publications/2012_CGI_sprayFoamBubbles.pdf) clamps all emission potentials with Φ(I, τmin, τmax) = (min(I,τmax) − min(I,τmin)) / (τmax − τmin) — a pure linear remap to [0,1]. (1) **Trapped air**: v_diff_i = Σ_j |v_ij| · (1 − v̂_ij·x̂_ij) · W(x_ij,h), where (1 − v̂·x̂) is 0 for separating and 2 for approaching pairs and W is a linear tent kernel; I_ta = Φ(v_diff) — chosen over curl because curl is large in turbulence but small at impacts. (2) **Wave crest**: curvature κ_i = Σ_j (1 − n̂_i·n̂_j)W counted only for convex neighbor pairs (x̂_ji·n̂_i < 0), gated by velocity-normal alignment δ = 1 only if v̂_i·n̂_i ≥ 0.6 (≈53° cone); I_wc = Φ(κ̃·δ). (3) **Energy**: E_k = ½mv², I_k = Φ(E_k) — a stand-in for the Weber number (they cite Mihalef's Weber-number splash criterion and Bagar's real-time Weber foam classification). Diffuse particles emitted per fluid particle per step: n_d = I_k · (k_ta·I_ta + k_wc·I_wc) · Δt — energy multiplies, crest and trapped-air add. Working thresholds across all scenes: τ_wc = 2..8, τ_ta = 5..20, τ_k = 5..50; emission rates up to 30 (trapped air) and 50 (crest) particles/frame/fluid-particle. **Classification** by fluid-neighbor count: <6 → spray, >20 → bubble, else foam. **Advection** per class: spray ballistic (gravity + external only); foam position-only advected by the SPH-averaged fluid velocity (velocity never stored — foam is a passenger of the surface); bubbles get v += Δt(−k_b·g + k_d·(ṽ_fluid − v)/Δt) with user buoyancy k_b and drag k_d (k_d = 1 snaps to flow). **Dissolution**: only foam ages — spray dies by falling in, bubbles by surfacing — and foam lifetime is not constant: it is set between user min and max in proportion to the generation potentials, so foam born of energetic events (in large clusters) lives longer, mimicking the real stability of large patches. **Rendering**: volumetric raycast with binary density (1 inside the particle volume radius, 0 outside), spray given a smaller radius than foam so it reads sharper; diffuse particle radius = 1/10 of fluid particle radius; 2.7M–15M diffuse particles for 220k–3.5M fluid particles ([Springer version](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00371-012-0697-9)).

For poseidon: three direct transfers. (1) The multiplicative-energy form — the accumulator injection should be energy-scaled: multiply the Jacobian-threshold trigger by a wave-energy proxy (cascade-0 displacement magnitude or crest speed at coarse mip) so big sea states inject more foam per fold event and small chop barely registers even when it folds. (2) "Lifetime proportional to emission potential" is a one-line change: instead of clamping the accumulator at a fixed cap, let stronger folds push it further above the cap-band threshold so recovery naturally takes longer for violent breaks — trail length then encodes break energy for free. (3) The crest gate v̂·n̂ ≥ 0.6 and the convexity test are shader-computable: convexity ≈ negative surface Laplacian of height (cheap from neighbouring derivative texels), velocity-normal alignment ≈ a vertical-velocity proxy from the time derivative of height at coarse mip. The neighbor-count classification maps to the tonal layers by density: dry cap = "dense foam", scud/streak film = "spray" (advecting ballistically downwind, faster than the surface — justifying a stronger flow-warp for scud than the 0.35x used for foam), submerged grey = "bubbles" (lagging the surface, fading with buoyancy time).

### Tessendorf's eigen-decomposition: accumulate λmin, not det J

The choppy-wave section of [Simulating Ocean Water (Tessendorf, SIGGRAPH course notes 2004, §Choppy Waves, eqs. 45–49)](https://people.computing.clemson.edu/~jtessen/reports/papers_files/coursenotes2004.pdf) defines, for the displacement map x → x + λD(x,t), the Jacobian J = Jxx·Jyy − Jxy·Jyx with Jxx = 1 + λ∂Dx/∂x, Jyy = 1 + λ∂Dy/∂y, Jxy = Jyx = λ∂Dx/∂y. J = 1 with no displacement; J < 0 signals the surface passing through itself — "a useful effect to signal the production of spray, foam and/or breaking waves". The refinement most implementations skip: write Jab = J−·ê−_a ê−_b + J+·ê+_a ê+_b with eigenvalues J− ≤ J+, so J = J−·J+. Folding (J < 0) means J− < 0 while J+ > 0 — "the minimum eigenvalue is the actual signal of the onset of folding", and it goes negative *before* det J does in mixed-strain regions. The eigenvector ê− "points in the horizontal direction in which the folding is taking place": whitecap streaks and folds align perpendicular to ê−, parallel to the crest line. Closed forms: J± = ½(Jxx+Jyy) ± ½√((Jxx−Jyy)² + 4J²xy); ê± = (1, q±)/√(1+q±²) with q± = (J± − Jxx)/Jxy — two lines of shader code from data poseidon already has. His 2022 talk restates it: λmin < 1 near sharp peaks, ≈1 in broad troughs, "a sensitive measure of steep peaks" ([2002 version of the notes](https://jtessen.people.clemson.edu/reports/papers_files/coursenotes2002.pdf)).

For poseidon: two upgrades fall straight out. (1) Accumulate the minimum eigenvalue λmin instead of det J — it is the physically meaningful onset signal, fires earlier and more selectively (det can stay positive when one axis compresses while the other stretches, exactly the crest-line case), and it is monotone where det is quadratic; the closed form needs only the three derivative-map channels the compute passes already produce. (2) ê− gives a per-pixel anisotropy frame *better* than the global wind frame for carve sampling: stretch the lace perpendicular to ê− so foam streaks follow actual crest geometry — curved crests get curved streaks — blending toward the wind frame at coarse mips where ê− is noisy. Both computable in the existing compute pass and packable into a spare texel channel.

### Tessendorf, Reinhardt & Gao 2022: the calibrated whitecap map

[Visualization of Simulated Ocean Scenes Employing Whitecap Fraction Phenomenology (Tessendorf, Gao, Reinhardt, Ocean Sciences 2022)](https://jtessen.people.clemson.edu/reports/papers_files/Os2022_tessendorf_reinhardt_gao.pdf) maintains a dynamically updated whitecap map O(x,t) ∈ [0,1] on the FFT surface. Growth: O is set to 1 wherever λmin(x, t+Δt) < λT (threshold on the minimum Jacobian eigenvalue). Decay: elsewhere O decays exponentially, O(x,t+Δt) = O(x,t)·e^(−Δt/T) with half-life T. Compact form: O(t+Δt) = O·e^(−Δt/T) + Θ(λT − λmin)·(1 − O·e^(−Δt/T)), Θ the Heaviside function. They used T ∈ {1, 8} s across 105 simulation runs (TMA spectrum, wind 4–25 m/s, fetch 25–200 km, patch 400–4000 m at 2048², cusp scale 0.01–0.95). The key contribution is **calibration**: the whitecap fraction W = ⟨O⟩ (spatial mean of the map) should match oceanographic phenomenology via Monahan & O'Muircheartaigh 1983, W = 3.84×10⁻⁶·U^3.41 (U in m/s → W ≈ 0.0007 at 4.5 m/s, ≈0.01 at 10 m/s, ≈0.07–0.2 at 24 m/s). Assuming stationarity, the update model averages to W(1−α)/(1−Wα) = CDF(λT) with α = e^(−Δt/T), where CDF is the cumulative distribution of λmin measured by histogramming a few simulated frames. Procedure: pick the desired W from wind speed → invert to the needed CDF value → read λT off the measured CDF. Example thresholds from their renders: λT = 0.034 (U = 4.54 m/s, actual W 0.0014) and λT = 0.534 (U = 24.1 m/s, actual W 0.076); their arbitrary-threshold examples show W = 0.011 at λT = 0.71 versus W = 0.15 at λT = 0.81 — coverage is extremely sensitive to the threshold, hence the need for calibration. Rendering: the map is a thresheld parameter in a Monte Carlo path tracer (whitecap regions swap the Fresnel water BRDF for a diffuse whitecap response). The talk credits its lineage: Jacobian-determinant shaders (Dupuy & Bruneton 2012), grow+decay game tools (Crest, SIGGRAPH 2017), and a min-eigenvalue-with-history clip from Superman Returns R&D (2005) (whitecap parameterization cited therein: [Albert et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.5194/acp-16-13725-2016)).

For poseidon: structurally identical to the persistent per-texel accumulator, so everything transfers. (1) Recovery should be an exponential half-life of 1–8 s — if the linear "recover" constant produces trails shorter than ~1 s or longer than ~10 s of visible decay, it is outside the published envelope. (2) The calibration recipe is directly implementable: a tiny compute reduction histogramming J (or λmin) over the cascade-0 tile for a few frames gives the CDF; solving W(1−α)/(1−Wα) = CDF(λT) with W = 3.84e-6·U^3.41 from the preset wind speed makes the cap threshold follow the weather presets automatically — the capture presets from commit ece7279 could each carry a Monahan-consistent coverage. (3) The extreme threshold sensitivity (W 0.011 → 0.15 for λT 0.71 → 0.81) explains why foam tuning feels brittle — calibrate to coverage, not threshold. (4) The exponential decay value is a natural age coordinate: age = −T·ln(O), so tonal layers can sit at fixed seconds-since-break rather than accumulator values.

### Moana: energy-birthed whitewater over a compositing ocean

In [The Ocean and Water Pipeline of Disney's Moana (Palmer et al., SIGGRAPH 2017)](https://history.siggraph.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2017-Talks-Palmer_The-Ocean-and-Water-Pipeline-of-Disneys-Moana.pdf) ([DOI](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3084363.3085067)) the ocean is a lightweight implicit representation — a compositing node graph of height fields, level sets, and operators — with the base ocean a procedural expression built on Horvath's empirical directional-spectra extension of Tessendorf waves (principled wind speed / fetch / depth controls) so FX sims match the base surface. Simulation regions are cut out with bounding boxes, run in the proprietary APIC solver Splash (Houdini-hosted), and stitched back with a blend node that dampens simulation toward region borders. The expression is split into low/high frequency bands: low frequencies go into the meshed surface, high frequencies are deferred to render-time displacement in the shader (a published filter setting acts as a high-pass), so lighting could amplify or filter near-field versus far-field detail without remeshing. Meshing shoreline-to-horizon in Hyperion took ~30 min/frame median; caches ran 1–10 GB/frame; the largest sim exceeded 1 billion particles and 20+ TB. Whitewater — bubbles, foam, and spray — used a Houdini POP solver as a secondary particle pass over the cached surface, with automated rigs running boat-wake + whitewater sims from published layout metadata with no artist intervention in many shots; artists "used VEX to efficiently isolate ocean particles with enough energy to birth bubbles" — a kinetic-energy emission criterion in production. [Moana: Crashing Waves (Byun & Stomakhin)](https://alexey.stomakhin.com/research/siggraph2017_waves.pdf) adds that the procedural wave deformer "stored the peak area of wave geometry and we used it as an emitter for white-water simulation" with proper initial velocity computed by the deformer — and, notably, "Voronoi patterns were used to enhance the scale of very large running waves, allowing us to cover a wide range of scales" on the procedural whitewater; hero breaks used FAB-guided Stokes-wave APIC sims. [Moana: Performing Water (Frost, Stomakhin, Narita)](https://history.siggraph.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2017-Talks-Frost_Moana-Performing-Water.pdf) added "secondary effects such as surface foam, drips and bubbles" to the sentient-water character, and shipped wall-of-water panels "with accompanying whitewater and sand churn elements", instanced, time-offset, and mirrored. On the rendering side ([Yining Karl Li's Hyperion notes](https://blog.yiningkarlli.com/2016/11/moana.html)), all water forms unify through SDF compositing into one watertight mesh containing a homogeneous scattering volume, with real photon-mapped sun-water caustics using adaptive photon distribution. Archival note: no published Moana talk is titled "Foundation of the Sea" — the material lives across this Wet-and-Wild session set plus "Rigging the Oceans of Disney's Moana" (SA 2016) (production story: [SideFX](https://www.sidefx.com/community/walt-disney-animation-studios-moana/)).

For poseidon: three precedents that legitimize the design. (1) Disney explicitly used Voronoi patterns to give procedural whitewater large-scale structure — the baked F2−F1 lace at 3 domain-warped scales is the same trick, published, and the "cover a wide range of scales" purpose supports multi-scale sampling over a single lace frequency. (2) "Peak area as emitter with stored initial velocity" equals the fresh cap band seeded from the Jacobian fold, and argues the fresh band should be advected slightly forward along the crest-velocity direction — a small forward offset along the wind frame mimics whitewater outrunning its crest. (3) The low/high frequency split with near/far-field filtering is the offline mirror of the 3-cascade split and coarse-mip regional reads — including letting the *shading* stage re-filter high frequencies per distance, which poseidon can do by fading carve scales with mip/distance. The VEX energy-birth reinforces Ihmsen's energy-multiplier emission form.

### Weta's wet foam: aeration, cohesion, and bursting

[Guided Bubbles and Wet Foam for Realistic Whitewater Simulation (Wretborn, Flynn & Stomakhin, ACM TOG 41(4), SIGGRAPH 2022)](https://alexey.stomakhin.com/research/siggraph2022_whitewater.pdf) ([DOI](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3528223.3530059); [summary](https://history.siggraph.org/learning/guided-bubbles-and-wet-foam-for-realistic-whitewater-simulation-by-wretborn-flynn-and-stomakhin/)) — the whitewater system behind Avatar 2, alongside the [Pahi/Loki pipeline (DigiPro 2023)](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3603521.3604291) — replaces the traditional velocity+curvature+vorticity stack with a single dimensionless **aeration** metric: A = 2Haρw·||[u]⊗[u]||_F / (πγ), the ratio of instantaneous Reynolds stress (from the velocity fluctuation [u] = u − ū, where ū is a box low-pass in space and time) to surface-tension pressure (γ = surface tension, H = mean curvature from the SDF, a = (Δx)² characteristic area). A ≳ 1 marks the onset of air entrainment; artists remap [Amin, Amax] (typically within [1,100]) to a target bubble volume fraction up to φmax ∈ [0.3, 0.7]; emission occurs only within 2Δx of the surface. They note pointedly that any liquid-only heuristic is incomplete for ocean whitecaps because local *wind* also matters. Bubble radii are sampled from Deike et al. 2016's inverse-cubic distribution Q(r) = 1/r³ (analytic CDF inversion), radii 0.5–5 mm. Bubbles reaching the surface convert to **wet foam**: observed sea foam has near-spherical, similar-size bubbles → yield stress σy ≈ 0, so foam is a Newtonian viscous fluid in SPH, constrained to the moving water surface by a manifold-advection constraint (Φ(x,t) = 0 enforced via Newton iterations, 2–3 iterations to within 0.1 mm; correction capped at ε = 0.1 m to avoid tunneling through overturning waves). Forces: pressure with clamp P = max(κ(ρ−ρ0), 0) (κ = 0.5 m²/s²; no negative pressure — wet foam separates freely instead of stretching); artificial viscosity μ = 0.05–5 m/s (higher = smaller-bubble foam); a **cohesion** force (the "cheerios effect" — meniscus attraction clusters surface bubbles; strength C = 10–100 m/s², cohesion radius βc = 5–12 particle radii; increasing C clumps faster, increasing βc makes larger clumps); and linear surface drag toward the liquid velocity a = χΦ(u − v) with χΦ = 0.05–0.5 s⁻¹ — too high locks foam into surface vortices (a "stringy look"), too low makes foam slide off waves. Transitions: particles within their own radius of the surface, or crossing it, become foam (projected onto the surface, keeping ζ = 0.7 of tangential momentum); particles inside the SDF become bubbles; others are deleted; new foam is stochastically pruned where the surface is already saturated (perfect-packing density from an analytic hex-lattice analysis; ρf = 1 kg/m³, kernel support β = 4r). Lifecycle: foam death is "bursting" — each particle's age is tested against a user probability distribution; a normal distribution works well, with lifespan mean E(τ) = 1.5–2 s and variance 0.5 s² in their production-scale examples. Demonstrated at 40 m × 40 m on a purely procedural Horvath-spectrum ocean — the foam solver runs fine on FFT oceans with no bulk sim.

For poseidon: (1) Aeration-as-fluctuation — Weta's emission signal is velocity minus its space-time low-pass, and poseidon's coarse-mip neighbourhood reads *are* a spatial low-pass: (fine displacement-derivative − coarse-mip displacement-derivative) is a legitimate shader-side Reynolds-stress proxy, and the ⊗ outer product → Frobenius norm says the signal should enter quadratically, not linearly — high-frequency cascade energy relative to the regional mean is an emission term with published pedigree. (2) The drag window χΦ = 0.05–0.5 s⁻¹ quantifies how loosely foam follows the water: over one second foam relaxes only 5–40% toward the local flow — the mild 0.35x flow-warp is squarely inside this behavior, and it argues *against* full-strength advection of the lace (fully locked foam looks "stringy", per the paper). (3) Cohesion-driven clumping increases with age: fresh foam is uniform, aged foam gathers into clumps — implementable as lace contrast/gamma increasing with accumulator age and blending toward the coarser Voronoi scales (larger effective βc) later in life. (4) Bursting as a normal distribution over age maps to the dissolve threshold: make the carve threshold a smooth function of age centered ~1.75 s with ~0.7 s sigma rather than a linear ramp, and the trail edge reads as stochastic bursting. (5) Weta's own caveat — liquid-only heuristics under-represent wind — endorses poseidon's wind-frame terms as physically motivated, not just aesthetic.

### From sub-pixel particles to shaded surface: the three-rung chain

The production chain from particles to shading has three published rungs. (1) **Particles → field**: Houdini's [Whitewater post-process](https://www.sidefx.com/docs/houdini/fluid/sopwhitewater.html) offers raw particles (fine splashy detail), a fog volume with a velocity field ("to get light absorption through the whitewater"), or a mesh ("sharp, defined boundaries between foamed and clear regions"); "Flatten Outside Bounding Box" projects whitewater particles back onto the procedural ocean surface offset by their depth attribute so a particle sim blends seamlessly into a shader-only far field. [Ihmsen et al. (§3.3)](https://cg.informatik.uni-freiburg.de/publications/2012_CGI_sprayFoamBubbles.pdf) render diffuse particles as a raycast volume with *binary* density thresholding (1 within the particle's volume radius, else 0 — found to beat Gaussian falloff), spray with a smaller radius than foam so it stays sharp while foam reads soft. (2) **Field → surface mask**: Houdini's [Ocean Evaluate](https://www.sidefx.com/docs/houdini/nodes/sop/oceanevaluate-.html) runs a "Foam Solver" — a per-frame simulation on the FFT tile where the "cusp" attribute (Jacobian-based wave-peak sharpness, < 0 stretched to > 1 inverted, with a "cuspdir" vector toward the peak) accumulates into a foam value with per-frame "Decay", gated by Min/Max Cusp and Min/Max Velocity, then is exported to a texture used as the "Foam Mask" in the Ocean Surface shader — foam becomes pure shading data, no render-time particles. (3) **Mask → BRDF**: the [Ocean Surface shader](https://www.sidefx.com/docs/houdini/gallery/shop/vopmaterial/oceansurface.html) accumulates any remaining foam particles at each shading point by radius (a shade-time splat), applies a particle-alpha ramp over lifespan (age-faded opacity), and composes foam as a separate shading layer with: two diffuse components — "streak" intensity/color and "whitecap" intensity/color, the whitecap driven by an intensity ramp on the cusp value that clamps low values to zero ("preventing whitecaps on smaller waves"); its own reflection intensity/color/blur scaled by foam visibility (foam is rough-specular as well as diffuse — the wet layer); directional streak controls (direction, frequency, bias) that stretch foam anisotropically; and optional foam displacement or bump-only normal perturbation. For fully procedural offline oceans, [Premoze & Ashikhmin, Rendering Natural Waters (PG 2000)](http://graphics.stanford.edu/courses/cs348b-competition/cs348b-01/ocean_scenes/ocean.pdf) shade whitecaps as a coverage fraction that "modifies optical properties on the water's surface", with coverage from Monahan's empirical formula f = 1.59×10⁻⁵·U^2.55·exp(0.0861(Tw − Ta)) (U in m/s; Tw−Ta the water-air temperature difference in °C — cold air over warm water increases foam). Tessendorf 2022 does the same in a path tracer via the thresheld whitecap map. At Moana scale, whitewater particles fed the same level-set/volume compositing as the water so foam participated in the homogeneous scattering volume; Weta's [Pahi (DigiPro 2023)](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3603521.3604291) renders through Loki compositing graphs "per sample requested by the renderer" so particle and volume foam composite losslessly with the ocean surface.

For poseidon: it lives entirely at rung (3), and the Houdini Ocean Surface shader is effectively its published blueprint, term by term: (a) age-ramped alpha over lifespan = the trail band's tonal decay (validated); (b) two diffuse foam populations — cusp-gated "whitecap" clamping small waves to zero, and anisotropically stretched "streak" — = the fresh cap band versus the streak-film layer, with the clamp-low-cusps ramp endorsing a hard floor on the cap threshold so small chop never caps; (c) foam carries its *own* specular lobe — the wet web and streak film layers should perturb roughness and keep some specular rather than going pure diffuse white, with only the dry cap (1.0) approaching Lambertian; (d) bump-only foam displacement suggests a cheap normal perturbation from the lace texture to break up water specular inside foam regions; (e) Ihmsen's binary-threshold volume and the mesh mode's "sharp boundary between foamed and clear" translate to a hard-ish edge on the fresh cap (step-like remap) with soft falloff reserved for the aged trail — film foam is not uniformly soft. The Monahan temperature term is a free climate control: one exp() factor scaling overall coverage for warm/cold presets.

### The numbers to target

A cross-source tuning card ([Tessendorf/Reinhardt/Gao 2022](https://jtessen.people.clemson.edu/reports/papers_files/Os2022_tessendorf_reinhardt_gao.pdf); [Wretborn et al. 2022, Table 3](https://alexey.stomakhin.com/research/siggraph2022_whitewater.pdf); [Ihmsen et al. 2012](https://cg.informatik.uni-freiburg.de/publications/2012_CGI_sprayFoamBubbles.pdf); [Premoze & Ashikhmin 2000](http://graphics.stanford.edu/courses/cs348b-competition/cs348b-01/ocean_scenes/ocean.pdf); [Byun & Stomakhin, Moana: Crashing Waves](https://alexey.stomakhin.com/research/siggraph2017_waves.pdf)). **Coverage**: Monahan/O'Muircheartaigh 1983 (used by Tessendorf 2022), W = 3.84×10⁻⁶·U^3.41 → U = 5 m/s: W ≈ 0.0009; U = 10: ≈ 0.0099; U = 15: ≈ 0.039; U = 20: ≈ 0.104; U = 25: ≈ 0.22; the Monahan 1971 variant with temperature (used by Premoze-Ashikhmin) is f = 1.59×10⁻⁵·U^2.55·e^(0.0861(Tw−Ta)). **Decay**: Tessendorf's production-tested half-life T ∈ [1, 8] s (α = e^(−Δt/T); the 105-run study used α = 0.861 per step); Weta's wet-foam bursting on a normal-distributed age with mean 1.5–2 s and variance 0.5 s² (close-up foam); Houdini defaults think in "Lifespan" seconds modulated per class by aging rates and density-based erosion. Together they suggest a two-stage decay: the bright cap dies on a ~1.5–2 s bursting curve, and the residual trail/streak decays exponentially with a 4–8 s half-life. **Emission threshold**: Tessendorf's calibrated λmin thresholds ran 0.034 (light wind) to 0.534 (25 m/s storm) — the threshold must move with sea state by an order of magnitude; fixed thresholds cannot serve multiple weather presets. **Classification**: Ihmsen's neighbor counts (<6 spray / 6–20 foam / >20 bubble), crest-gate cosine 0.6, and Houdini's soft 0–1 state attributes. **Scale structure**: Weta's cohesion radius of 5–12 particle radii with bubble radii 0.5–5 mm puts physical foam clump features between ~5 mm and ~12 cm — below any FFT texel — so structure at this scale must come from texture (poseidon's lace), not from displacement maps; Disney used Voronoi patterns precisely to synthesize this band procedurally.

For poseidon, concretely: (1) pick wind speed per preset → Monahan W gives the target screen-average foam coverage; verify by averaging the foam output at coarse mip (a debug reduction) rather than eyeballing. (2) Split the accumulator decay into the two published stages: a fast bursting envelope on the fresh cap (smoothstep of age centered ~1.75 s) and a slow exponential on the trail (half-life 4–8 s at high wind, 1–2 s in calm presets — stormier seas keep foam longer). (3) Make the cap threshold preset-dependent across roughly a 10x range, or better, auto-calibrate from a J histogram. (4) The 5 mm–12 cm clump band confirms the lace carries physically-scaled detail no cascade can: keep the finest domain-warped lace scale at ~5–20 cm in world units and let the two coarser scales cover ~0.5–3 m (repellent feature sizes) — matching Houdini's repellent Feature Size Range concept.

## The airborne phase: spray and spume

### The shape of the gap

Nobody in real time renders the airborne phase from the surface shader. The two shipped patterns are (1) ATLAS: emit a fixed particle budget everywhere in the frustum and kill any particle not on a whitecap by sampling the foam/Jacobian texture — effectively a history-free spawn poseidon can drive from its accumulator's fresh-cap band — and (2) GodotOceanWaves: fully stateless billboards with closed-form arcs (foam > 0.9 activation, exp_impulse/log scale curves, parabolic fall, an unshaded sprite with dissolve noise) — a complete numeric recipe that ports to one instanced TSL draw with zero new compute passes. Film pipelines — The Perfect Storm's spray/crest-mist/crest-foam/splash classes, Weta Loki's bulk→spray(SPH)→mist(ballistic+air-drag) state machine, Moana's energy-thresholded bubbles/foam/spray — all converge on a two-phase look target: discrete ballistic streaks at the crest that relax into a translucent wind-following haze downwind; in poseidon the blend parameter between the two is the accumulator age (trail band) it already computes. The fragment-only implementation that covers the visually dominant phase is an analytic exponential height-fog spray layer (Wenzel's SIGGRAPH 2006 closed-form transmittance, iq sun-tinting): density ~ k1·U10 + k2·U10³·capCoverage, scale height ~0.3·Hs (log-profile decay per Ortiz-Suslow 2016, visible matter to ~2·Hs), evaluated in the ocean and horizon-sky fragments — yielding near-surface haze, spindrift veiling, horizon dimming, and storm visibility loss with no particles, history, or screen-space passes. Physical dials with sources: spume-stripping onset at U10 ~7–11 m/s (~9 m/s midpoint; Veron 2015/Andreas); spume drops r0 10–500 µm with peak ~100 µm, launched at roughly the wind speed at the crest and falling back in <~1 s; jet-drop fizz reaching only 10–20 cm above fresh foam; spray mass growing ~U10³ (NOAA PSL). Storm-preset structure from Holthuijsen et al. 2012: whitecap coverage saturates at ~4% even in hurricanes — extra whiteness above B9 must come from wind-parallel foam/spray *streaks*, which merge into total whiteout above 40 m/s. So poseidon should cap fresh-cap coverage near 4% and let scud/streak-film layers plus airborne haze carry the escalation, with the Beaufort ladder (B9 "spray may affect visibility" → B12 "air filled with foam and spray... visibility very seriously affected") fixing the per-preset visibility budget. War Thunder and Sea of Thieves confirm the gap — no airborne pass in either deck — but supply the surface-side levers poseidon already mirrors.

### ATLAS: frustum-emit, band-cull — the canonical history-free spawn

The full [ATLAS deck (Mihelich & Tcheblokov, GDC 2019)](https://gpuopen.com/gdc-presentations/2019/gdc-2019-agtd6-interactive-water-simulation-in-atlas.pdf) computes foam per frequency band: Jacobian of displacement per band; if above threshold "we are on a wave top", inject "turbulent energy", dissipate it over time (blur + fade), sum energy from all bands at render, and modulate a foam texture by it (slide 56) — the same accumulator idea as poseidon's min(J, recover). Spray ("Wave top sprays", slides 61–64): they wanted particles only in camera view and only on whitecaps, inside UE4's Cascade system with *no* GPU spawning; the particle sim runs in a pixel shader over Position/Time/Velocity textures. The trick: a custom emitter emits particles *everywhere* in the camera frustum, without simulating or rendering them; each particle samples the world-space foam/whitecap texture at its location — pseudocode: `if (Surf.foam_wave_hats > Simulation.WaveHatThreshold) { Particle.Pos += Vert.Displacement; Particle.LifeTime = 0.0 } else { Particle.LifeTime = -1.0; return; }` — invalid particles are killed before simulation starts, valid ones get the surface displacement applied and begin ballistic life. Explosions are "currently done with spray particles & sprites", wakes with foam sprites (slide 66). Sprite shading and lighting details are *not* in the deck — rendering is stock UE4 Cascade camera-facing sprites; the [NVIDIA WaveWorks 2.0 blog](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-waveworks-2-0-debuts-in-grapeshot-games-atlas/) adds that spray "drift[s] off into the wind", doubling as a gameplay wind cue. Timings: wind-wave sim 0.5 ms on an RTX 2080/Radeon VII at max quality ([GDC Vault session](https://www.gdcvault.com/play/1025819/Advanced-Graphics-Techniques-Tutorial-Wakes); [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Dqld965-Vv0)).

For poseidon: the ATLAS spawn is effectively stateless — emit a fixed budget uniformly in view, cull against the instantaneous whitecap band — and poseidon already owns the cull signal: the fresh-cap band of the turbulence accumulator (a superset of ATLAS's per-band energy). A minimal WebGPU port needs no compute pass and no history: one instanced draw of N quads whose vertex shader hashes instance ID → (xz in frustum, phase), samples the accumulator and displacement maps (the same fetches the water vertex stage already does), and collapses the quad to zero size when freshCap < threshold. That is ATLAS's kill-invalid-particles trick with poseidon's existing textures.

### GodotOceanWaves: a complete numeric recipe for stateless billboards

The two spray shaders in [GodotOceanWaves](https://github.com/2Retr0/GodotOceanWaves) are public and small, read verbatim from the repo. The particle sim shader ([sea_spray_particle.gdshader](https://github.com/2Retr0/GodotOceanWaves/blob/main/assets/shaders/spatial/sea_spray_particle.gdshader)): particles sit on a fixed √N×√N grid in the emitter AABB; activation is `ACTIVE = normal_factor in [0,1] && foam > 0.9`, foam sampled from the accumulated-Jacobian texture at the particle's world UV; start times are staggered by hash (`START_TIME = TIME + rand.z*(LIFETIME - PARTICLE_LIFETIME)`); lifetime is 3 s with 0–25% randomization. Scale over normalized age t: vertical `exp_impulse(t, 3.0)` (fast pop, slow decay), horizontal `log(1.0 + t)` spread. Position: horizontal follows the ocean displacement map ×0.75 (to damp jitter); vertical follows the parabola `-5.0*pow(2.5*t - 0.45, 2.0) + 0.5` (rise then fall) — a closed-form ballistic arc, no integration, no history. The sprite shader ([sea_spray.gdshader](https://github.com/2Retr0/GodotOceanWaves/blob/main/assets/shaders/spatial/sea_spray.gdshader)): camera-facing billboard, unshaded, shadows off; albedo = texture × foam color × vec3(1.65, 1.75, 1.65) brightness push; alpha = texture.a × 0.666 × near-fade `1.0 - exp(-length(VERTEX.xz)*0.04)` × a dissolve term mixing per-instance fade with a noise texture scrolling at TIME×0.35. The author's own header comment concedes it is "not a great shader since it doesn't apply any lighting".

For poseidon: this is the smallest shipped implementation that matches its architecture — every input it needs (foam accumulator, displacement map, hash, time) poseidon already has, and its "sim" is closed-form, so it ports as a pure vertex-shader instanced draw in TSL with zero new passes. Improvements poseidon can make over it: light the sprite with the same sun/ambient terms as the foam layers (Godot's admitted weakness); stretch quads along the wind frame (poseidon has the wind basis) so puffs read as spindrift streaks rather than isotropic splashes; and drive dissolve with the existing Voronoi lace texture instead of a second noise.

### War Thunder and Sea of Thieves: the gap confirmed, the surface-side levers supplied

Contrary to folklore, there is *no* dedicated airborne spray pass in [Ocean simulation and rendering in War Thunder (Tcheblokov, CGDC 2015)](https://developer.download.nvidia.com/assets/gameworks/downloads/regular/events/cgdc15/CGDC2015_ocean_simulation_en.pdf) — "Wakes & splashes" appear only as a quality-scaling row (full / normals-only by distance). What the deck does document: foam from J < M with M ≈ 0.3..0.5, foam texture modulated by saturate(k·(−J+M)); breaking waves injecting turbulent energy per cascade, dissipated over time (exponential fade) and space (blur), simulated per cascade in a pixel shader and combined; surface stretching explicitly modulating foam-layer thickness ("stretched - thinner, squeezed - thicker"); and, as the closest thing to an airborne phase, a refraction-side effect: "turbulent energy = foam intensity ... and mixed-in bubbles! Add milkiness modulated by energy to refraction color" — a *sub*-surface bubble haze rather than an above-surface one. Sim cost ~0.5 ms on a GTX 770. [The Technical Art of Sea of Thieves (SIGGRAPH 2018)](https://history.siggraph.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2018-Talks-Ang_The-Technical-Art-of-Sea-of-Thieves.pdf) ([DOI](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3214745.3214820); [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y9BOz2dFZzs)) likewise documents only surface foam: peak foam per Tessendorf plus depth-buffer object foam in a camera-centered window, a foam buffer "progressively blur[red] ... with feedback" to model dispersal, blending with artist-authored textures — and, critically for presets, "foam generation, dispersion and blending with the artist-authored textures is modified based on whether the water is calm, normal or stormy" (stormy raises foam for churn; calm shows only object-interaction foam). A wave-peak mask from FFT choppiness offsets drives extra subsurface color at crests (thin-crest translucency). The ship-bow splash/spray sprites seen in game are conventional UE4 particle VFX not covered by any published talk — the SIGGRAPH talk documents only surface foam, clouds, ropes, and deck-water sims (Mei et al. 2007 GPU shallow water).

For poseidon: these two confirm that even the storm-heavy shipped FFT titles stop at the surface — putting matter *above* the interface from the fragment side is genuinely new ground. Their transplants are surface-side: War Thunder's "milkiness added to refraction color, modulated by energy" is the exact mirror of poseidon's submerged-grey tonal layer (the below-surface half is already covered), and the stretch-thickness rule matches the strain carve. Sea of Thieves' calm/normal/stormy single-scalar modulation of foam generation and dispersion is the cleanest precedent for wiring poseidon's storm presets to foam *and* spray amount through one weather scalar, and its crest translucency from choppiness offsets endorses keying wet-web/streak-film tones off horizontal-displacement magnitude at coarse mip — a signal poseidon already reads for flow-warped carve coordinates.

### Film look target I — The Perfect Storm: spray versus crest mist

For The Perfect Storm, ILM wrote new software over ~6 months for the water surface and "extremely complex particle simulations ... to model elements such as spray, crest mist, crest foam, and splashes" — establishing the split film pipelines still use: a coarse, fast-falling **spray** class (discrete blobs, ballistic, sun-lit like the foam) and a fine **crest mist** class (semi-transparent haze torn off the crest, streaming downwind, lit by scattering — reading as a soft veil, not droplets). Habib Zargarpour and John Anderson explicitly researched "how wind and water and solid objects interact" and "how light affected the appearance of the water and mist"; the work was presented as the SIGGRAPH 2000 panel "Industrial Light + Magic: the making of The Perfect Storm" ([befores & afters retrospective](https://beforesandafters.com/2023/04/06/heres-why-the-fluid-sims-on-the-perfect-storm-were-so-hard-to-do/); [ILM project page](https://www.ilm.com/vfx/the-perfect-storm/); [Zargarpour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habib_Zargarpour)).

For poseidon: the two-class split is the design contract for the storm look — the airborne phase is not one effect but two: (1) discrete crest spray (sparse, bright, short-lived; the billboard/impostor layer) and (2) crest mist (continuous, translucent, wind-sheared; the volumetric haze layer). Visually, whitecaps at Beaufort 7+ are "inseparable" from the mist class more than from individual droplets — so if poseidon builds only one of the two, it should be the haze.

### Film look target II — Weta's Loki state machine: bulk → spray → mist as a continuum

Loki (SIGGRAPH 2022 Technical Paper, "Loki: a unified multiphysics simulation framework for production", Wētā FX) runs solvers per water *state* and blends between them: bulk water is FLIP/Eulerian; when Reynolds stress and surface tension shatter it at the air interface it becomes **spray**, simulated with SPH; spray transitions to **mist** — "ballistic particles but fully coupled with the surrounding air via a drag force" ([Unity blog description](https://unity.com/blog/industry/technology-behind-avatar-the-way-of-water)). Whitewater combines "a grid-based fluid solver coupled with bubbles, and an SPH solver for foam constrained to the water surface" ([80.lv](https://80.lv/articles/a-behind-the-scenes-look-at-avatar-2-s-water-technology)). Joe Letteri, via [befores & afters](https://beforesandafters.com/2022/12/21/why-the-cg-water-in-the-way-of-water-looks-so-good/): "water exists in all these different states, so we wrote a suite of solvers in Loki, each one tuned for the optimal state ... [Loki] parses the simulation and assigns the correct solver to the correct state, before allowing room to blend in between", with artist-controlled blend points; "Bulk water will react to air drag differently to small particles because you're changing the shape and the scale." Rendered in Manuka; Loki's RenderGraph composites "spray, mist, bubbles, volumes" without degrading individual elements.

For poseidon: the transferable idea is the *continuum*, not the solvers — airborne water starts as directed, ballistic, opaque streaks at the crest and relaxes into wind-following translucent volume downwind. In a fragment-only pipeline that maps to a single blend parameter: near the fresh-cap source, spray should be anisotropic (streaked along wind, high contrast, moving at crest speed); with distance-from-source — and poseidon's accumulator age / trail band *is* that distance-in-time — it should decay into an isotropic haze contribution that only dims and brightens. The accumulator recovery gives the age signal film pipelines get from particle lifetime, for free.

### Film look target III — Moana: energy-gated emission and the occlusion warning

Disney's Moana pipeline ([The Ocean and Water Pipeline of Disney's Moana, SIGGRAPH 2017](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3084363.3085067); [PDF](https://history.siggraph.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2017-Talks-Palmer_The-Ocean-and-Water-Pipeline-of-Disneys-Moana.pdf)) composites simulations over a lightweight implicit/levelset ocean at render time via a levelset-graph procedural in Hyperion (1–10 GB/frame caches). Whitewater — "bubbles, foam and spray" — was simulated with a Houdini POP solver on top of the Splash (APIC) main sim, with emission gated by *energy* thresholds: artists "used VEX to efficiently isolate ocean particles with enough energy to birth bubbles" and "directed how sheeting particles flowed over a collision surface and broke off as drips when they passed a parameterized density or velocity threshold" ([SideFX interview, Alex Moaveni](https://www.sidefx.com/community/walt-disney-animation-studios-moana/)). Per-class rendering specifics (points versus volumes) were not published; the levelset-compositing talk covers the surface only. [Moana: Performing Water (Frost, Stomakhin, Narita, SIGGRAPH 2017)](https://alexey.stomakhin.com/research/siggraph2017_gretchen.pdf) adds the FAB seeding method for perpetual birth and sinking of particles on a moving surface.

For poseidon: this reinforces energy-gated emission — every serious pipeline spawns airborne matter from an energy/turbulence threshold, never uniformly, and poseidon's Jacobian accumulator is precisely that energy proxy, so any spray/haze layer should inherit its bands rather than introduce a new trigger. Also a scope warning: Moana's spray reads correctly only because it is composited with correct occlusion against the surface — poseidon's haze layer must be occluded by wave geometry (evaluate it in the ocean fragment shader behind/above the surface point, not as a screen overlay), or crests will glow through each other.

### History-free foundations: stateless particles and analytic height fog

Two building blocks a fragment-only pipeline can afford. (1) [Building a Million Particle System (Latta, GDC 2004)](https://media.gdcvault.com/gdc04/slides/building_a_million.pdf) ([project page](http://www.2ld.de/gdc2004/)) formalizes *stateless* particles: position as a closed-form function of age, p(t) = p0 + v0·t + ½g·t², attributes derived from a per-particle hash — no read-back, no history buffer, no integration pass; suited to short-lived effects. Combined with ATLAS-style cull-by-foam-band this yields spray with zero persistent state. (2) [Real-time Atmospheric Effects in Games (Wenzel, SIGGRAPH 2006 Advances course, Crytek)](https://advances.realtimerendering.com/s2006/Wenzel-Real-time_Atmospheric_Effects_in_Games.pdf) gives the closed-form transmittance through an exponential height-density medium ρ(h) = ρ0·e^(−h/H): the integral along a view ray from camera to surface point has an analytic solution (his height-fog equation), evaluated per fragment with no marching. [Iñigo Quilez's fog article](https://iquilezles.org/articles/fog/) adds the standard sun-tinting — lerp fog color toward sun color by pow(max(dot(rayDir,sunDir),0),k) — which makes a spray haze read as backlit when looking upwind into the sun. The negative control: [Rendering Water in Horizon Forbidden West (Malan, SIGGRAPH 2022 Advances)](https://advances.realtimerendering.com/s2022/SIGGRAPH2022-Advances-Water-Malan.pdf) — even Guerrilla shipped breaking waves with foam via vertex color, lists surface foam and splashes as unsolved or toned down ("sims with high splashes ... had to get toned down"), and has no airborne layer — corroborating that a cheap non-particle airborne treatment is an open niche.

For poseidon, the concrete design, all fragment/vertex-only: **Layer A** (spume streaks, B7–9): stateless instanced quads — instance hash → frustum xz + phase; the vertex shader samples the accumulator fresh-cap at coarse mip, collapses the quad if below threshold, else places it at the displaced surface plus a closed-form arc; launch velocity ≈ wind speed at the crest (Andreas), stretched along the wind frame; lit with the foam layers' sun/ambient terms. **Layer B** (spray haze, B8+): in the ocean fragment shader (and the sky shader near the horizon), analytic Wenzel transmittance for a layer hugging z ≈ sea level with scale height H ≈ 0.2–0.5·Hs; density ρ0 ∝ (U10/U_ref)³ × a coarse-mip regional foam signal; color = scattered sky/sun with iq's sun-lerp.
