This simultaneously delivers near-surface haze, horizon dimming, and storm visibility loss with no particles, no history, no screen-space pass — and the flow-warped carve coordinates poseidon already computes can advect Layer B's streak modulation downwind so haze streams off crests.

### What the ocean actually does: onset, droplet classes, heights

From [Veron's Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics survey (Ocean Spray, 2015, 47:507–538)](https://sites.udel.edu/fveron/files/2020/12/Veron-2015-spray-annurev.pdf) (DOI: 10.1146/annurev-fluid-010814-014651): spume drops are "mechanically torn off from the crest of a breaking wave", and "a wind speed higher than approximately 7-11 m/s is typically necessary to generate spume droplets" (Andreas et al. 1995, Andreas 2002) — the ~9 m/s figure is the midpoint. Droplet classes: **film** drops at r80 0.01–2 µm, ejected at 20–30 m/s (invisible haze/aerosol, irrelevant to rendering except as long-range atmosphere); **jet** drops at r0 2–100 µm, peak ~10 µm, ejection up to 8 m/s, reaching only 10–20 cm height (the fizz above fresh foam); **spume** drops at r0 10–500 µm with peak ~100 µm (lab observations up to 2–6 mm), swept *downwind* of the crest after ejection, with initial ejection velocity inferred to "scale with the value of the wind speed at the wave crest" (Andreas et al. 2010; see also [Veron et al. 2012, GRL](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2012GL052603)). Large spume is "likely to fall back within a fraction of a second, except in the most extreme winds"; larger droplets overall stay airborne "from fractions of a second to several minutes". Vertical structure from [Ortiz-Suslow, Haus, Mehta & Laxague (Sea Spray Generation in Very High Winds, J. Atmos. Sci. 73(10):3975–3995, 2016)](https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/atsc/73/10/jas-d-15-0249.1.xml), lab data at U10-equivalent 36–54 m/s: spume radii observed 80–1400 µm; concentration profiles imaged from 2 to 6× the local significant wave height follow a *logarithmic* decay with height (not the power law assumed by older source models); and size spectra fall off as r⁻³ — far shallower, i.e. more large visible drops, than the r⁻⁸ of typical models. [NOAA PSL](https://psl.noaa.gov/spotlight/2013/measuring_seaspray.html) adds that the whole spray layer lives "within 100 m of the ocean surface" with dense concentrations within tens of meters.

For poseidon, direct parameterizations: switch the spray layer on at U10 ≈ 9 m/s (between the fresh-breeze and gale presets); streak launch speed = wind speed sampled at crest height (use the preset's U10 directly); billboard arcs should live ≲1 s before dissolving (spume fallback time); the haze scale height H for the Wenzel layer is physically a fraction of Hs with log-profile decay — practically H ≈ 0.3·Hs, with visible content up to ~2·Hs above crests in storm presets and essentially nothing above that until hurricane strength; and the jet-drop fizz (10–20 cm) justifies a thin bright halo hugging fresh foam patches, renderable as a slight upward bias of the fresh-cap tone rather than geometry.

### How much to show: coverage laws, streaks, whiteout, visibility

Amount scaling: whitecap coverage W = 3.84×10⁻⁶·U10^3.41 ([Monahan & O'Muircheartaigh 1980, the canonical law, J. Phys. Oceanogr. 10:2094](https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/phoc/10/12/1520-0485_1980_010_2094_opldoo_2_0_co_2.xml): ~0.15% at 10 m/s, ~1% at 17 m/s, ~4% at 25 m/s); total spray *mass* "increases roughly as wind speed to the 3rd power" ([NOAA PSL](https://psl.noaa.gov/spotlight/2013/measuring_seaspray.html)). Storm-state structure from [Holthuijsen, Powell & Pietrzak (Wind and waves in extreme hurricanes, JGR 117:C09003, 2012)](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/2012JC007983), from hurricane aerial reconnaissance: whitecap coverage *saturates* near 4% (never exceeding ~10%) even in hurricanes; above that, the surface whitens through wind-parallel *streaks* of foam and spray, which grow until "at wind speeds above 40 m/s the streaks merge into a whiteout with complete coverage" — i.e., ~96% of a hurricane sea's whiteness is streak/spray matter, not whitecaps. The visibility ladder from the [NOAA NCEI Marine Beaufort Scale](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/sites/default/files/2021-09/Marine_Beaufort_Scale.pdf): B7 — foam "begins to be blown in streaks"; B8 — "edges of crests begin to break into spindrift", well-marked streaks; B9 — dense foam streaks, "spray may affect visibility"; B10 — sea "takes on a white appearance ... visibility affected"; B11 — long white patches of foam everywhere, visibility affected; B12 — "air filled with foam and spray; sea completely white with driving spray; visibility very seriously affected". Quantitative optics: spaceborne lidar shows marine-aerosol extinction at 532 nm in the lowest ~300 m rising with a positive linear relationship to wind speed (R² = 0.57) ([ACP 24, 2024](https://acp.copernicus.org/articles/24/4389/2024/)) — haze density can be modeled as monotonic in U10 on top of the U³ burst term near the surface.

For poseidon, a preset table: (a) cap the fresh whitecap band's areal coverage near 4% even in the hurricane preset — past B9 the extra whiteness must come from the streak-film/scud tonal layers and the airborne haze, *not* from more caps (matching Holthuijsen, and keeping storms from looking like uniform foam soup); (b) drive haze optical depth as k1·U10 + k2·U10³·freshCoverage, with the whiteout blend forcing horizon-level transmittance toward zero as U10 → 40 m/s; (c) tie the scud/streak band's coverage to the gap between total whiteness (Beaufort ladder) and the capped 4% whitecaps; (d) set a visibility budget per preset — B7 clear horizon, B9 horizon softened, B10–11 horizon veiled, B12 horizon gone within a few hundred meters of eye height — implemented entirely by the analytic haze layer's density, delivering the previously missing "visibility loss in storm presets" from measured anchors.

### Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag — the lit-particle precedent

AC4's updated Anvil particle system renders "ocean spray from splashing or waves ... individually-simulated, physically-tracked, and individually-lit liquid particles", responding "independently with the scene's light sources, wind, materials, and object collision events"; foam particles ride wave crests, and dynamic weather escalates to tropical storms with rain and spray hitting the camera ([AC4 Graphics Tech Explained, GamersNexus quoting Ubisoft](https://gamersnexus.net/gg/1205-assassins-creed-4-black-flag-graphics-analysis); background on the AC3 lineage at [fxguide](https://www.fxguide.com/fxfeatured/assassins-creed-iii-the-tech-behind-or-beneath-the-action/)). The details are marketing-level — no GDC deep-dive was published on the spray specifically — but it is the earliest big-ship title to treat crest spray as a lit particle pass driven by wind, and it established the storm-legibility convention: spray plus camera droplets as the storm-intensity readout.

For poseidon: two cheap perception wins, both compatible with its constraints. (1) Individually-lit matters — even a haze layer should take the sun term (iq's sun-lerp) so upwind and downwind views differ. (2) At B9+ a first-person or rail camera reads storm intensity from droplets *on the camera* as much as from the sea — a screen-corner droplet streak texture keyed to U10 sits outside the ocean shader entirely and costs almost nothing, if poseidon's capture framings ever want it.


## The academic record

The academic literature on real-time whitecaps divides into four questions: a *criterion* (where does foam appear), a *persistence model* (how long does it stay), a *calibration* (how much of the sea should it cover), and an *appearance model* (what does it look like once it exists). Two papers anchor the field — [Dupuy & Bruneton 2012](https://inria.hal.science/hal-00967078v1) solved the criterion-plus-filtering problem, and [Tessendorf, Reinhard & Gao 2023](https://jtessen.people.clemson.edu/reports/papers_files/whitecap_fraction.pdf) solved persistence and calibration. Everything else in this chapter either feeds those two or supplies a complementary signal.

### Dupuy & Bruneton 2012: the pre-filterable whitecap closure

The canonical whitecaps paper, [Dupuy & Bruneton 2012](https://inria.hal.science/hal-00967078v1) ("Real-time Animation and Rendering of Ocean Whitecaps", SIGGRAPH Asia 2012 Technical Brief; [ACM DOI](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2407746.2407761)), marks a surface point as whitecapped when the determinant of the horizontal-displacement Jacobian `J = det(I + lambda*grad D)` falls below a user threshold `epsilon` — Tessendorf's folding criterion (`J <= 0` means self-intersection) generalized to `J < epsilon` so foam appears slightly before folding.

The paper's actual contribution is not the test but the *closure*: `J` over a pixel footprint is treated as a Gaussian random variable whose first two moments ride the ordinary texture pipeline. In the author's [reference implementation](https://github.com/jdupuy/whitecaps) (`whitecap_precompute.glsl`), each of the 4 FFT cascades gets a per-texel partial Jacobian `res_c = 0.25 + Jxx + Jyy + Jxx*Jyy - Jxy^2` — the identity's 1 split as 0.25 per cascade, with choppiness-scaled derivatives from dedicated FFT layers `LAYER_JACOBIAN_XX/YY/XY` — and *both* `res` and `res^2` are written to textures. Mean and second moment are linear quantities, so ordinary hardware mip-mapping and anisotropic filtering yield exact footprint averages `E[J_c]` and `E[J_c^2]` at any scale: a "wave deformation criterion that can be pre-filtered linearly." At shading time (`ocean.glsl`): `mu = sum_c E[J_c]`; `sigma^2 = sum_c (E[J_c^2] - E[J_c]^2)` (cascades assumed statistically independent, cross-cascade covariance dropped); coverage `W = P(J < epsilon) = 0.5*erf((epsilon - mu)/(sqrt(2)*sigma)) + 0.5`. Rendering adds a Lambertian foam term `R_f = W * (L_sun*max(N.L,0) + E_sky)/pi * 0.4` (effective whitecap albedo 0.4) onto the water BRDF. Near the camera `sigma -> 0` and `W` approaches a crisp binary cap; far away it becomes fractional coverage — anti-aliased "from centimetric to planetary" scale. Reported performance: under 10 ms/frame at 1280x720 on a GeForce 560 Ti with 4 cascades of 256^2 FFTs.

Critically, there is *no history or accumulator anywhere* — `foam.glsl` and `ocean.glsl` are pure per-frame functions of the current Jacobian moments. Temporal coherence is emergent (the FFT displacement evolves continuously; the erf gives partial coverage instead of popping binary pixels), and LOD/camera coherence comes from the linear prefiltering. The documented weakness, stated by Tessendorf et al. 2023 who cite it as their [5]: no persistence — the whitecap vanishes as soon as `J` recovers, whereas real foam lingers seconds to minutes — and coverage is fixed by a threshold rather than by observed whitecap-fraction phenomenology.

For poseidon: the criterion is already there (the `min(J, recover)` accumulator) but the paper's real contribution — the variance closure — is not. Storing `J` and `J^2` (or accumulator and accumulator^2) in the cascade compute passes and letting mip generation average both would let the fragment shader compute `sigma^2` at its footprint and replace hard band thresholds with `erf((threshold - mu)/sigma)`, giving analytically anti-aliased foam coverage at distance; the coarse-mip neighbourhood reads poseidon does for "regional signals" are a manual approximation of exactly this. The per-cascade moment sum with the independence assumption maps 1:1 onto poseidon's 3 cascades (1024/144/24 m): sum the 3 means, sum the 3 variances, split the identity 1/3 per cascade instead of 0.25 — and adopt the per-cascade `Jxx*Jyy - Jxy^2` determinant term if poseidon currently sums only trace terms.

### Tessendorf, Reinhard & Gao 2023: minimum eigenvalue, half-life, and wind-speed calibration

The direct academic successor, [Tessendorf et al. 2023](https://jtessen.people.clemson.edu/reports/papers_files/whitecap_fraction.pdf) ("Whitecap Phenomenology for Ocean Surface Simulation"; [companion Ocean Sciences 2022 poster](https://jtessen.people.clemson.edu/reports/papers_files/Os2022_tessendorf_reinhardt_gao.pdf)), makes three upgrades.

**Criterion.** Replace `det J` with the *minimum eigenvalue* `lambda_min` of `J = I_2D + f_cusp*grad D`: 1 for flat water, approaching 0 at a cusp, negative when the surface self-intersects. It is "a more sensitive measure of peak sharpness" than the determinant (`det = lambda_min*lambda_max` can be masked by the other eigenvalue), and its eigenvector gives the horizontal direction the wave is trying to break along.

**Persistence.** A whitecap opacity map `O(x,t)` in [0,1] updated as `O(t+dt) = 1` where `lambda_min < lambda_T`, else `O(t)*exp(-dt/T)` — reset-to-one on generation, exponential decay with half-life `T`, recharge when a new wave passes. This formalizes what Crest and games already did. Frame whitecap fraction `W(t) = (1/NxNy)*sum O` reaches statistical steady state after 2–3 half-lives.

**Calibration.** Ensemble-averaging the update (with the separation-of-timescales factorization `<W*Theta> ~= <W><Theta>`) gives `<W> = <Theta> / (1 - alpha(1 - <Theta>))` with `alpha = exp(-dt/T)`, and `<Theta(lambda_T - lambda_min)> = CDF(lambda_T)`. Unlike Dupuy & Bruneton they do *not* assume Gaussian statistics — measured PDFs of `lambda_min` from TMA-spectrum simulations show strong non-Gaussian tails and wildly different widths at the same wind speed — so they histogram `lambda_min` from one frame of the actual realization and invert the empirical CDF. The algorithm: pick a phenomenological whitecap-fraction model, e.g. MOM80 `W = 3.84e-6 * U^3.41` (general family `W = a(U-U0)^b`, sourced from [Albert et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.5194/acp-16-13725-2016)); compute `W_reduced = W(1-alpha)/(1-alpha*W)`; solve `CDF(lambda_T) = W_reduced` by a monotone bounds test. Concrete numbers: `alpha = 0.861` (effective `dt = 0.15*T`), half-life `T` in {4, 8} s, `f_cusp` 0.05–0.95, wind 4–25 m/s, fetch 25–200 km, patch 400–4000 m at 2048^2; example thresholds `lambda_T = 0.71 -> W = 0.011` and `lambda_T = 0.81 -> W = 0.15`. Rendering uses `O` as an opacity that "pulls through" a separately authored dynamic foam pattern — explicitly described as standard film/games practice — shaded as white Lambertian.

For poseidon: three drop-in upgrades. (1) Swap `det J` for `lambda_min = 0.5*(Jxx+Jyy) - sqrt(0.25*(Jxx-Jyy)^2 + Jxy^2)` — cheap, the derivative maps already exist; more sensitive cap detection, and the eigenvector supplies a physically derived per-wave breaking direction that could replace or modulate the global wind-frame anisotropic carve (foam streaks aligned per-wave rather than per-wind). (2) Poseidon's "accumulator recovery = age" is exactly `O(t)*exp(-dt/T)` with reset; adopting an explicit half-life of 4–8 s makes the trail band physically parameterized. (3) The calibration recipe kills the magic-threshold problem: histogram `lambda_min` (or `J`) over one frame of the 3 cascades on the GPU (or offline per preset), pick the target `W` from MOM80 for the preset's wind speed, invert the CDF — the foam threshold then tracks spectrum/wind/choppiness changes automatically. Together the two anchors also validate poseidon's core design: Dupuy & Bruneton's lack of persistence is the documented weakness that later work — [Crest 2017](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3084363.3085028) in engineering, Tessendorf et al. 2023 academically — fixed with exactly poseidon's reset-on-generation plus exponential-decay-with-recharge pattern. The `min(J, recover)` accumulator is the published state of the art, not a hack.

### Crest: the engineering form of the persistence model

[Bowles 2017](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3084363.3085028) ("Crest: Novel Ocean Rendering Techniques in an Open Source Framework", SIGGRAPH Advances talk; [docs](https://crest.readthedocs.io/en/4.14/user/ocean-simulation.html), [source](https://github.com/wave-harmonic/crest)) runs foam as a small persistent simulation texture, LOD-chained like its displacement data. Each update (default simulation frequency 30 updates/s) injects foam where the displacement-texture Jacobian determinant indicates pinched waves (a Wave Foam Coverage parameter moves the `J` threshold; Wave Foam Strength scales injection) and in shallow water below Shoreline Foam Max Depth (scaled by Shoreline Foam Strength); all texels are then multiplied down by a Foam Fade Rate — exponential dissipation, i.e. exactly the reset/recharge + `exp(-dt/T)` model Tessendorf et al. 2023 cite (their ref [2] is this talk) and calibrate. Rendering derives two looks from the sim texture: a whitecap layer and a sub-surface "bubble" layer offset/parallaxed under the surface. The foam sim runs at fixed Hz decoupled from frame rate (lower Hz is cheaper but jitters), and foam LOD data follows the camera like displacement LODs.

For poseidon: Crest is the closest existing system to poseidon's architecture and confirms the core choices. Deltas worth stealing: fixed 30 Hz foam updates make trail age wall-clock-stable across devices (important in-browser where frame rate varies wildly); depth-based shoreline injection is a two-line addition if bathymetry ever exists; the parallaxed sub-surface bubble layer is a cheap depth cue the "submerged grey" tonal layer could adopt (sample the lace texture with a small view-vector offset scaled by a fake depth). Conversely poseidon's carve machinery — Voronoi lace, strain-driven thresholds, wind-frame anisotropy — is ahead of Crest's texturing.

### Complementary generation signals: vertical acceleration and limiting steepness

[Chen, Jin & Yin 2017](https://hrcak.srce.hr/file/264243) ("Ocean Wave Rendering with Whitecap in the Visual System of a Maritime Simulator", CIT 25(1):63–76, DOI 10.20532/cit.2017.1003327) critiques the Jacobian route — it needs 3 extra IFFTs (Jxx, Jyy, Jxy), "lacks theoretic support in marine engineering" and "suffers from temporal instability" — and uses the criterion standard in ocean engineering: breaking when downward vertical acceleration `a_z <= -beta*g` with `beta = 0.388 ~ 0.39` (the limit-steepness equivalent). Since `a_z` has Fourier coefficient `-omega^2 * h_tilde`, *one* extra IFFT yields the whole field. The statistics are exact: `a_z` is Gaussian with mean 0 and variance `m4` (the 4th spectral moment, integrable directly from the spectrum), so instantaneous coverage is `W_az = 1 - Phi(beta*g / sqrt(m4))` in closed form — the analogue of Dupuy's erf but with a physically calibrated threshold and analytically known variance. Rendering blends `C = (1-W_R)*C_F + W_R*C_W` with a continuous ramp: `W_R = 0` for `a_z >= -alpha1*g`, `W_R = 1` for `a_z <= -alpha2*g`, and between them `W_R = beta1*[exp(-(a_z+alpha1*g)/sqrt(m4)) - 1]/2`. The temporal trick: a point's `a_z` time-series rises monotonically from crest to trough, so the ramp width `(alpha2 - alpha1)` acts as the whitecap *lifetime* control ("the smaller alpha1, the longer the lifetime"). `alpha2, beta1` are fitted by a genetic algorithm so `E[W_R]` equals the stochastic coverage, keeping rendered coverage on the empirical wind curves (they cite `W = 4.4e-4*U10^2`, `2.96e-6*U10^3.75`, `1.90e-6*U10^3.51`). Example fits at `beta = 0.39`: `U19.5 = 10 m/s, alpha1 = 0.25 -> alpha2 = 0.685`; `U = 20, alpha1 = 0.25 -> alpha2 = 0.507`. Validated against Beaufort 5–7 descriptions; 71 fps on a GTX 660 with 35x35 tiles of 512 m at up to 256^2 verts.

For poseidon: `-omega^2*h` is one more spectral multiply in the existing FFT compute pass (no new transforms if packed into a spare channel), and `m4` is a scalar CPU integral per preset. Two uses: (a) gate the *fresh cap* band by `a_z < -0.39g` so caps appear at physically breaking crests — crest-phase-locked, slightly *leading* the Jacobian pinch, which peaks after the crest passes — while the Jacobian accumulator keeps driving the trail band; (b) the closed-form `W = 1 - Phi(0.39g/sqrt(m4))` is a free analytic calibration target to normalize thresholds across wind presets without the Tessendorf histogram pass. The monotone-ramp-as-lifetime idea is also a zero-storage alternative for the cap-to-trail transition.

[Jeschke & Wojtan 2017](https://research-explorer.ista.ac.at/download/470/7359/wavepackets_final.pdf) ("Water Wave Packets", SIGGRAPH 2017; [project](https://visualcomputing.ist.ac.at/publications/2017/WWP/), [code](https://github.com/jeschke/water-wave-packets)) contributes the steepness limit. Lagrangian particles carry packets of wave energy with representative wavenumber `k = 2*pi/lambda` and amplitude `a`, travelling at group speed while the internal train moves at phase speed; amplitude obeys the discrete energy-conservation law `a(t+1) = a(t) * sqrt((rho*g + sigma*k_n^2)*A_n / ((rho*g + sigma*k_{n+1}^2)*A_{n+1}))` as packet area `A` stretches (discrete — not discretized — conservation gives unconditional stability). Damping: viscosity `da/dt = -2*nu*k^2*a` and surface contamination `da/dt = -(1/2)*nu'*sqrt(omega/2nu')*k*a`. Since Airy theory cannot represent breaking, they adopt the Dean & Dalrymple deep-water observation that waves break when amplitude exceeds 7% of wavelength: `a` is clamped to `<= 0.07*lambda` every step, the energy removed at the clamp *is* the breaking event, and foam/spray particles are seeded at packet fronts that hit the clamp. Packets below a minimum steepness are deleted; real-time for hundreds of thousands of packets in an open-source DX11 sandbox.

For poseidon: the 7% law is the transferable nugget — a breaking predictor independent of the Jacobian. Per-cascade steepness is `k*a`, and locally `2*a/lambda ~ |grad h|/pi` at the dominant wavenumber, so slope magnitude at the crest exceeding ~0.22 (= 0.07*pi; practically a `|grad h|` threshold tuned near 0.2–0.3) flags physically breaking crests. A steepness gate on the fresh-cap band ties cap injection to actual limiting steepness rather than only area compression — the two disagree exactly where it matters visually (long swell pinches without breaking = no cap; short steep chop breaks = cap) — and gives the smallest cascade (24 m tile) a principled way to contribute breaking events the big cascades cannot see.

### The particle heritage: generation potentials and clumpy dissipation

[Ihmsen et al. 2012](https://cg.informatik.uni-freiburg.de/publications/2012_CGI_sprayFoamBubbles.pdf) ("Unified Spray, Foam and Bubbles for Particle-Based Fluids", CGI / The Visual Computer 28:669; [Springer](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00371-012-0697-9)) is the canonical foam-generation model: three potentials, each mapped to [0,1] by the clamp `Phi(I, tmin, tmax) = (min(I,tmax) - min(I,tmin))/(tmax - tmin)`. (1) Trapped air: `v_diff_i = sum_j ||v_ij|| * (1 - v_hat_ij . x_hat_ij) * W(x_ij,h)` — relative speed weighted by "moving towards each other" (factor 0 receding, 2 approaching), with a *linear* kernel `W = 1 - ||x||/h` chosen over cubic splines for free-surface robustness. (2) Wave crest: curvature `kappa_i = sum_j (1 - n_hat_i . n_hat_j) W(x_ij,h)` counted only where `x_hat_ji . n_hat_i < 0` (convex), gated by motion alignment `delta_i = 1` only if `v_hat_i . n_hat_i >= 0.6` — the surface must be moving outward along its normal, killing false positives on static sharp edges. (3) Kinetic energy `I_k = Phi(0.5*m*v^2)`. Spawn count per particle per step: `n_d = I_k * (k_ta*I_ta + k_wc*I_wc) * dt` — energy multiplies, the two causes add. New diffuse particles are sampled in a cylinder along the velocity with tangential initial components, then classified by fluid-neighbor count: fewer than 6 neighbors = spray (ballistic), more than 20 = bubble (buoyancy `k_b` vs drag `k_d` toward local fluid velocity), 6..20 = foam, advected exactly with the interpolated surface velocity. Only foam ages; lifetime is initialized *proportional to the generation potential* between user min/max — strong events make longer-lived foam — while spray and bubbles are reclassified instead of dying. Scale: 2.7M diffuse particles on a 220k-particle wave.

For poseidon: every potential has a texture-space analogue that refines the strain-driven carve. Trapped air maps to negative surface divergence (compression) *weighted by horizontal speed* — multiplying the divergence signal by `|horizontal velocity|` (from the displacement time-derivative or choppy displacement at coarse mip) concentrates foam where water both converges and moves, suppressing static pinches. The velocity-alignment gate translates to injecting fresh cap only where `dh/dt > 0` (crest rising) — a one-channel gate stopping foam on the backs of already-passed waves. Lifetime-proportional-to-potential means seeding the accumulator not to a constant but scaled by how far `J` undershot the threshold, so deeper pinches leave longer-lived trails, enriching the recovery-equals-age tonal ramp. The multiplicative structure — energy times the sum of causes — validates a global wind/sea-state factor multiplying local event signals.

[Yingst, Alford & Parberry 2011](https://ianparberry.com/pubs/GAMEON-NA_GRAPH_04.pdf) ("Very Fast Real-Time Ocean Wave Foam Rendering Using Halftoning", GAMEON-NA) attacks dissipation: real foam does not fade to transparent — discrete bubble clusters pop away, and uniform alpha decay looks wrong. A precomputed halftone mask `m(u,v)` tiled over the ocean thresholds a smooth time-varying saturation function `f(x,z)`: foam pixel on iff `f > m`; as saturation decays, successively higher mask values are crossed and foam disappears in discrete clumps. The mask design is the whole trick: Gaussian-filtered white noise (Alford & Sheppard 2010), analyzed via the radially averaged power spectrum — a wide filter `sigma = 24` suppresses high-frequency mask energy and produces naturally clumped dot patterns matching foam's surface-tension clustering, while `sigma = 1.5` gives blue-noise-like isolated dots (the wrong look). Anti-popping refinement: fade term `g = clamp(f/2 - m, 0, 1)` multiplies the foam so each clump dims briefly before popping; final `j = g * foamTexture` where `f > m`, else 0. Their saturation is analytic (`f = e^(-tan(theta/2 + pi/2))/C`, `C ~ 4`, locked to Gerstner fronts so foam sits on the forward face), but the halftoning layer is agnostic to where saturation comes from. Cost: one texture fetch plus a compare.

For poseidon: this is the academic statement of the dissolve-threshold-riding-coverage pattern in poseidon's newest commit, with two upgrades. (1) The dissolve texture's *spectrum* is the knob controlling perceived bubble clumping — the Voronoi F2−F1 lace is high-frequency/edge-like; layering a low-pass clump mask (Gaussian-filtered noise, effective sigma large relative to texel) underneath makes trail decay proceed in patch-wise pops rather than uniform thinning, especially where accumulator recovery plays the role of decaying saturation. (2) The pre-pop fade `clamp(f/2 - m)` is a one-liner that softens carve edges just before they disappear — applicable to the wet-web and streak-film layers to avoid shimmering hard edges as the accumulator recovers.

### Foam appearance: thickness, occlusion, and tint

[Akinci et al. 2013](https://cg.informatik.uni-freiburg.de/publications/2013_WSCG_screenSpaceFoamRendering.pdf) ("Screen Space Foam Rendering", WSCG) renders millions of diffuse particles in a multi-pass screen-space pipeline: (1) accumulate per-pixel foam *thickness* by additive splatting and map thickness to intensity/opacity exactly as volume ray-casters map optical depth (more bubble layers = more scattering = whiter and more opaque); (2) screen-space ambient occlusion over the foam depth buffer attenuates intensity in crevices; (3) approximate per-pixel environment irradiance *tints* the foam — foam is not pure white, it takes sky and sun color; (4) composite. The stated physics: foam looks white because many thin water films reflect all incident light before it penetrates. They position against [Bagar et al. 2010](https://www.cg.tuwien.ac.at/research/publications/2010/bagar-2010-ppb/) ("Physically Based Real-Time Rendering of SPH Fluids"), which classifies fluid vs foam by a Weber-number threshold `We = rho*v^2*L/sigma` and renders layered foam back-to-front, lerping between two user foam colors by thickness — Akinci adds the occlusion and environment lighting Bagar lacks.

For poseidon: the shading model transfers wholesale despite the absence of screen-space passes. Treat the layered foam value as a *thickness*, not an albedo mask: (a) `opacity = 1 - exp(-tau * thickness)` instead of linear banding — the dry-cap-1.0 / wet-web / streak-film tonal ladder is a hand-made version an exponential thickness law would unify with one parameter; (b) tint foam by sky irradiance plus a sun term rather than constant white (Dupuy's `(L_sun*N.L + E_sky)/pi * 0.4` is the same idea; the "submerged grey" layer is Bagar's two-color thickness lerp, with the wet color being the water-attenuated foam color); (c) Bagar's speed-squared Weber gate supports weighting fresh caps by per-cascade wave phase speed — big-cascade caps whiter and denser than capillary scud.

### Advection, wakes, wavelets, and aperiodicity

[Ojeda & Susín 2013](https://web.mat.upc.edu/toni.susin/files/hybrid_lbmsw_rend_new.pdf) ("Real-time Rendering of Enhanced Shallow Water Fluid Simulations", Computers & Graphics) is the cleanest published statement of history-buffer foam advection on a heightfield: a single-channel floating-point texture over the surface; wherever a splash particle re-enters, the texel is initialized to a maximum time-to-live; every frame the texture is advected along the horizontal velocity by semi-Lagrangian backtracing (Stam-style: sample the previous frame's foam at `x - dt*v`) and decremented by `dt` until 0; TTL times a foam color blends onto the surface. They warn that foam-texture texel size must match the injection footprint or events are lost or blurred, and they simplify from [Chentanez & Müller 2010](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/1833349.1778830)'s advected diffuse foam disks. Cost is one fullscreen pass, negligible.

For poseidon: this is the missing flow-map-history branch poseidon deliberately avoids — the reference design if it ever changes its mind. The per-texel accumulator decays *in place* while real foam is transported by orbital/drift velocity; the fix costs one ping-pong: in the existing turbulence compute pass, read the previous accumulator at `uv - dt*v_horizontal` (v from the displacement maps' time derivative or the coarse-mip horizontal displacement — the same field already used for the 0.35x flow-warped carve coordinates) before applying `min(J, recover)`. That single semi-Lagrangian read makes trails stream downwind instead of ghosting — the difference between foam painted on the sea and foam riding it. The texel-size warning maps to choosing which cascade hosts the accumulator: the 144 m / N=256 middle cascade at ~0.56 m texels bounds the smallest persistable foam feature.

[Jeschke et al. 2018](https://pub.ista.ac.at/group_wojtan/projects/2018_Jeschke_WaterSurfaceWavelets/WaterSurfaceWavelets.pdf) ("Water Surface Wavelets", SIGGRAPH 2018; [ACM](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3197517.3201336)) simulates amplitude density `A(x, theta, k)` over space, direction, and wavenumber on a coarse Eulerian grid (e.g. 4096^2 spatial x 16 wave-vector samples for a 4x4 km scene), reconstructing arbitrarily high-resolution displacement via Gabor-like synthesis — boats, reflections, diffraction in real time. Foam: none native. The dynamics are linear in `A`, "there is no direct way for it to handle complex non-linear phenomena like breaking waves," and for look development they "evaluate a Fourier ocean spectrum and a simple foam shader on top." The [2020 boundary-aware follow-up](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/cgf.14100) makes procedural waves boundary-aware via precomputed direction/phase fields around obstacles. For poseidon: reassurance — even the most sophisticated real-time wave papers punt foam to "a simple foam shader" over a Fourier spectrum, so poseidon's fragment-only layered foam is already beyond this branch's published state. If spatially varying seas are ever wanted, the WSW idea maps to a low-res wave-energy texture modulating cascade amplitudes regionally, with the *time derivative* of that regional energy (energy loss = breaking) as an extra regional foam signal feeding the existing coarse-mip reads.

For ship wakes, [Huang et al. 2021](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2108.05481) ("Ships, Splashes, and Waves on a Vast Ocean", SIGGRAPH Asia; [ACM](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3478513.3480495)) couples a surface-only BEM ocean with localized FLIP domains (three 50x3.5x50 m boxes on a 100 m-radius tank; speedboats at 10 m/s); whitewater is *not* part of the solver — the BEM mesh becomes an SDF with a narrow-band velocity field, and an off-the-shelf whitewater simulator (Houdini's, essentially Ihmsen 2012's potentials) runs over it as a separate composited pass, at ~42 s/frame. Wake geometry is validated against [Rabaud & Moisy 2013](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.110.214503)'s airborne measurements (wake angle falls below the classical 19.47 deg at high Froude number). The real-time ancestor is [Thuerey et al. 2007](https://dl.acm.org/citation.cfm?id=1272690.1272716) (SWE heightfield, steepness/velocity breaking criteria, foam particles advected with the SWE velocity); older empirical systems shape bow/stern foam to the [38.94-degree Kelvin envelope](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-642-38460-8_95). For poseidon: the unanimous pattern is that foam is driven by a surface velocity field plus an injection mask, never by the wake solver itself. A ship would just stamp turbulence into the existing accumulator (propeller wash = trapped-air analogue; hull line = Kelvin-arm mask at 19.47 deg, narrower at high speed per Rabaud–Moisy) and the existing carve/tonal machinery renders it — the research gap is purely the injection field.

Finally, [Lutz, Schoentgen & Gilet 2024](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3675388) ("Fast Orientable Aperiodic Ocean Synthesis Using Tiling and Blending", HPG 2024 / PACMCGIT 7(3); [Ubisoft La Forge write-up](https://www.ubisoft.com/en-us/studio/laforge/news/5WHMK3tLGMGsqhxmWls1Jw/making-waves-in-ocean-surface-rendering-using-tiling-and-blending)) applies histogram/covariance-preserving tiling-and-blending (the Heitz–Neyret by-example noise family) to the FFT displacement and derivative maps: a hexagonal tiling blends exemplar content of 3 hexes per texel with variance-preserving normalization, so the synthesized displacement is aperiodic yet statistically indistinguishable from the FFT original — and because the blend is covariance-preserving, the Jacobian and foam masks computed from it keep coherent statistics; Jacobian-thresholded foam continues to work without retuning. A flow map sampled at hexagon centers rotates each hex's exemplar lookup (with compensating rotation of displacement vectors), giving spatially varying wave direction with zero precomputation — one FFT set serves all directions, cheaper than multiple IFFTs. For poseidon: this attacks the two artifacts the 3-cascade design exists to hide — visible 1024/144/24 m periodicity and the single global wind frame. One hex-blend layer over the cascade textures would kill tile repetition at grazing heights and let a coarse flow map bend wave (and foam-carve) direction regionally, with carve coordinates rotated by the same per-hex angle. Caveat: blending must be applied to the *input* displacement/derivative maps, with `J` and the accumulator computed from blended values — min/history operations do not commute with variance-preserving blending. Pure texture-space math, WebGPU-friendly.

## Texture advection without destruction

The entire texture-advection field is one idea with variants: advection distorts a texture at a rate set by the *velocity gradient*, not the velocity, so transport must be periodically reset and the reset hidden. The design axes are: how many copies (phases), the phase weight function, the reset period (latency), what de-synchronizes the pulse, and what metric adapts or triggers regeneration. Two artifacts recur, with independent causes and independent fixes. Temporal synchrony (the whole surface breathing in lockstep) is fixed by a per-pixel phase offset from a noise channel at roughly half the range's amplitude, plus per-cycle UV "jump" offsets that stretch the loop to hundreds of cycles. Blend-induced variance loss (the mid-blend "muddy" moment) is fixed by variance-preserving blending — dividing the weighted deviation-from-mean by `sqrt(sum w^2)` — or, for opacity compositing, exponential optical-depth weights. And one rule governs everything: never blend through a nonlinearity — crossfade the raw field (noise octaves, Voronoi distance, height) and apply thresholds and shading once on the blended result. For poseidon's dissolve-threshold foam this is the difference between two lace webs merging plausibly and double-exposure ghosting.

Two architectures fit poseidon without particles: (a) stateless fragment-only two/three-phase advection of the carve coordinates by the coarse-mip displacement flow — zero history, about one extra texture fetch per lace scale, direction-safe for the isotropic Voronoi lace provided the wind-frame stretch is applied to coordinates; (b) one-tap semi-Lagrangian accumulation in the existing compute ping-pong (the IBFV pattern): `foam' = (1-alpha)*sample(foam, uv - flow*dt) + alpha*freshLace`, `alpha ~ dt/latency` — true transport, merge, and dilution with no pulse, at the cost of one history channel and a known contrast loss (~77% of standard deviation at `alpha = 0.1`, recoverable with the variance trick).

### Max & Becker 1995: the root — advect, reset, crossfade

[Max & Becker 1995](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/6472w2f4) ("Flow Visualization Using Moving Textures", LLNL) originates the family. Texture coordinates at triangle-grid vertices are advected *backward* along the flow (`F^-t(P)`); hardware interpolates per pixel; the texture is periodic (wraparound addressing) so streamlines leaving the domain still fetch valid texels. "During the animation this distortion continues to build up... therefore we periodically restart the texture coordinates back at their original positions in the regular grid. To avoid the sudden jump... we gradually fade up the new texture and fade down the old one" — overlapping weight curves with `f1 + f2 = 1` at all times (their Figure 2 shows three staggered cycles). Two technical notes matter. For unsteady flows the inverse map `G_t` is integrated incrementally with the Jacobian estimated by central differences between adjacent grid vertices — errors in those partials compound *exponentially* frame to frame, an independent reason the periodic reset is mandatory rather than optional. And when the crossfade is done in *opacity* (alpha compositing of semi-transparent layers), naive weights pulse: compositing opacities `a1 = b*f1, a2 = b*f2` yields total `C = b - b^2*f1*f2`, dipping every mid-blend. Their fix: exponential optical-depth weights `a_i = 1 - exp(-f_i * rho)`, because transparencies multiply — `(e^-f1r)(e^-f2r) = e^-r`, constant across the cycle. The distortion insight underneath it all: stretching comes from the velocity gradient, not the velocity — a fast uniform flow does not distort at all.

For poseidon: two direct lessons. The exponential-opacity identity is the correct way to crossfade the tonal foam layers (dry cap over wet web over streak film composite like alpha layers): if two advected phases of a coverage mask are combined as opacity, use `w_i -> 1 - exp(-f_i*rho)` so total coverage does not breathe at mid-blend — equivalently, crossfade in an optical-depth/density domain and convert to coverage once. And the velocity-gradient insight says the reset period should be tied to poseidon's already-computed surface strain (divergence), not flow speed: uniform drift is harmless and could run long cycles; only convergence zones where foam merges need short ones.

### Valve flow maps: the canonical two-phase crossfade

[Vlachos 2010](https://alex.vlachos.com/graphics/Vlachos-SIGGRAPH10-WaterFlow.pdf) ("Water Flow", SIGGRAPH 2010, in the [Advances course](https://advances.realtimerendering.com/s2010/index.html); L4D2 / Portal 2) is pixel-shader-only flow: an artist-authored flow map (~4 texels/meter, painted as a combed vector field in Houdini) gives a 2D flow vector per point; a tiling detail texture is offset along it, scaled by time. The algorithm: (1) building on Max & Becker, distortion "looks reasonable for the first 1/3 of UV space," so each animation segment distorts only a little before restarting; (2) the restart is hidden by running the same short segment in two layers offset by half a phase, crossfaded so each layer's weight is zero at its own reset instant; (3) the "repetition" artifact (identical normals recurring every cycle) is solved by offsetting each phase's sample interval per cycle; (4) the "pulsing" artifact (the surface breathing between sharp single-texture and muddy 50/50 moments) is solved by adding a per-pixel noise value to time, de-synchronizing every pixel's cycle. A subtle distinction: for flowing *normals* the distortion interval runs 0..fraction with the blend peak at half distortion, but for flowing *color* (Portal 2 debris) the interval is re-centered to −fraction..+fraction so each layer's full-weight moment coincides with *zero* distortion — stretched color is far more visible than stretched normals. Normal strength is scaled down by flow speed. Cost versus two scrolled normal maps: +2 texture fetches (flow, noise), +21 ALU instructions — shippable on ps2.0b / Xbox 360.

For poseidon: directly implementable under the fragment-only constraint — zero history, just a time uniform, a flow vector, and a noise channel. The flow vector already exists (the flow-warped carve coordinates read horizontal displacement at coarse mip); today that warp is a static 0.35x offset that oscillates with orbital motion but never truly transports. Replacing it with `flowVec * frac(t/T)` in two half-period phases gives genuine downwind transport of the lace/carve texture with bounded shear (distortion capped at `T * |flow|`). Per-pixel phase noise can come free from an existing baked Voronoi/fbm channel or the turbulence accumulator itself. And Vlachos' color-vs-normal lesson maps onto foam: foam albedo is "color," so center the distortion interval so each phase peaks at its least-distorted moment.

### The exact two-phase math: Catlike Coding, mtnphil, three.js Water2

[Catlike Coding](https://catlikecoding.com/unity/tutorials/flow/texture-distortion/) ("Texture Distortion") gives the full reference implementation:

```hlsl
float3 FlowUVW(uv, flowVector, jump, flowOffset, tiling, time, flowB) {
  float phaseOffset = flowB ? 0.5 : 0;
  float progress = frac(time + phaseOffset);
  uvw.xy = uv - flowVector * (progress + flowOffset);
  uvw.xy *= tiling;  uvw.xy += phaseOffset;
  uvw.xy += (time - progress) * jump;
  uvw.z = 1 - abs(1 - 2*progress);
  return uvw;
}
```

The blend weight is the triangle wave `w = 1 - |1 - 2*progress|` — zero at each phase's reset, peaking at progress 0.5 — and the two phases (offset 0.5) have complementary weights: `final = texA*wA + texB*wB`. The jump term shifts the sampled region by a constant per cycle (`time - progress` is the integer cycle count): `jump = 0.25` would loop the whole animation after 4 cycles, so they use near-quarter values `uJump = 0.24` (= 6/25, repeats after 25 cycles) and `vJump = 0.2083` (~5/24, 24 cycles), for a combined loop of hundreds of cycles. Per-pixel time offset comes from the flow map's alpha noise channel: `time = _Time.y*_Speed + noise`. [mtnphil 2012](https://mtnphil.wordpress.com/2012/08/25/water-flow-shader/) ("Water flow shader") documents the same with a sawtooth weight (`blend = 2*|phase0 - 0.5|`) and phases `phase_i = (NormalPhase01_i + noiseSample * PULSE_REDUCTION) % 1`, and quantifies the tradeoffs: the pulsing is really *contrast loss* (averaging two unrelated normal samples is "muddy"); noise de-phasing fixes it, but (a) no pixel is ever fully invisible so the free random re-offset at end-of-cycle is lost, and (b) using the noise's full 0..1 range makes regions visibly advect at different speeds — he limits it to half the dynamic range (`PULSE_REDUCTION = 0.5`). [three.js Water2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrdoob/three.js/dev/examples/jsm/objects/Water2.js) ships this in poseidon's own ecosystem: `cycle = 0.15`, `halfCycle = 0.075`, `flowSpeed = 0.03/s`; two offsets advance by `flowSpeed*delta`, wrap at `cycle`, and stay exactly `halfCycle` apart; `uv_i = uv*scale + flow*offset_i`; weight `flowLerp = abs(halfCycle - flowMapOffset0)/halfCycle`; `normal = mix(n0, n1, flowLerp)`.

For poseidon: the drop-in recipe, trivially portable to TSL nodes. Concretely for the carve texture: `progress = fract(t/T + phaseNoise)`; `carveUv_i = windFrameUv - flowUv * progress_i * gain`; `w = 1 - |1 - 2*progress|`; per-pixel `phaseNoise` from an existing domain-warp fbm channel at ~0.3–0.5 amplitude (mtnphil's half-range rule). The jump trick matters for the 3 domain-warped lace scales: give each scale different sub-quarter jumps so the composite never visibly loops. mtnphil's caveat: the technique wants direction-free texture content — poseidon's Voronoi F2−F1 lace is isotropic and qualifies, but the wind-frame anisotropic stretch must be applied to the *coordinates* before advection (stretch and advect commute) rather than baked into the texture.

### Neyret 2003: three phases, multi-latency layers, and blend-before-nonlinearity

[Neyret 2003](https://inria.hal.science/inria-00537472) ("Advected Textures", SCA 2003; [PDF mirror](https://evasion.inrialpes.fr/Publications/2003/Ney03/neyret161.pdf)) generalizes to N layers `{T^i}`, each built from *three* regenerated texture parameterizations `{(u_j, v_j), j = 1..3}` phase-shifted by `tau_i/3`, where regeneration means resetting texture coordinates to window coordinates after latency `tau_i`. Phase weights are raised cosines `alpha_ij = (1/3)(1 - cos(2*pi*(t - t0_ij)/tau_i))`, which sum to 1 for a seamless rolling crossfade: `T^i = sum_j alpha_ij * T(u_ij, v_ij)`. Three phases cost one extra fetch over two but give a much flatter blend — there is never a pure-single-texture moment, hence no detail pulse. The latency tuning rule: neither too high (stretch) nor too low (breaks the motion illusion — a fading spot is perceptually re-identified with neighbors unless it travels more than a pseudo-period before reset; "consider a factor of 10 in practice"). The distortion metric: instantaneous deformation is the strain tensor `epsilon = (G + G^T)/2` (G the velocity gradient; symmetrizing cancels solid rotation, which does not distort), scalar `sigma = sqrt(sum epsilon_ij^2)`; each texture maintains an *accumulated* deformation `d_j`, advected with the fluid and updated `d_j += sigma*dt`; a layer's accumulation `d^i` is the sum over its three phases (quasi-constant on steady flow). Selection: the user sets a target deformation `d*`; find bracketing layers `d^i < d* < d^(i+1)`; fractional layer `l = i + (d* - d^i)/(d^(i+1) - d^i)`; blend layers i and i+1 with weights (1−f, f) — "temporal MIP-mapping." Six textures (2 layers x 3 phases) blend per point. The blending fix: linear blends of a nonlinearly-shaded procedural texture ghost and lose contrast; since Perlin base functions share pseudo-period and are uncorrelated, blend the *raw* base noise octaves across the 6 parameterizations first (`b_k = sum alpha*b(2^k u)`), then apply the nonlinearity once — `t(x) = sum (1/2^k) f(b_k)` with `f(b) = |2b-1|`, then the final shader `shad(t())` — one shader evaluation per pixel instead of six, and no ghosting. Results: 3 layers (9 textures), 64x64 sim grid, 512x512 output, real-time with hardware texture layers. [Yu et al. 2011](https://maverick.inria.fr/Publications/2010/YNBH10/IEEE_TVCG.pdf) later measured the endpoints of the latency tradeoff on the basic single-latency scheme: 0.6 s latency = echoed texture and *wrong* optical flow but near-preserved Fourier spectrum; 4.0 s = correct optical flow but stretched texture and distorted spectrum — hence multi-latency layers or local adaptation instead of one global period.

For poseidon: the deepest match. (1) The persistent per-texel turbulence accumulator `min(J, recover)` *is* Neyret's advected accumulated-deformation field `d` — already computed in the compute pass. It can select between two carve-advection layers with different periods (e.g. `tau = 6 s` calm / `1.5 s` churned) exactly like his temporal MIP-mapping, with the fractional-layer crossfade guaranteeing continuity; strain (divergence) is already available as the instantaneous `sigma`. (2) Blend-before-nonlinearity is the single most important transfer: poseidon's foam is a dissolve *threshold* riding fbm/Voronoi coverage, and thresholding is exactly the nonlinearity that ghosts — crossfade the two phases of the raw lace/erosion field first, apply the strain-driven carve threshold once to the blended field, and two coincident lace webs merge into one plausible web instead of double-exposed foam. (3) The 10-pseudo-period rule sizes T: with lace features ~0.5 m and flow ~1 m/s, `T >= ~5 s` or the reset reads as foam swimming in place.

### Yu et al. 2011: the distortion metric and variance-preserving blending

[Yu, Neyret, Bruneton & Holzschuch 2011](https://maverick.inria.fr/Publications/2010/YNBH10/IEEE_TVCG.pdf) ("Lagrangian Texture Advection: Preserving both Spectrum and Velocity Field", TVCG; [HAL](https://hal.science/inria-00536064/)) attach deformable 8x8-vertex grids to Poisson-disk particles (spacing d, maintained per-frame by boundary sampling; killed if closer than `(1-delta)d` with `delta = 0.25`; grid width `(2+eps)d` with `eps = 0.6` so grids outlive kernel coverage), each mapping a random window of the reference texture. The core distortion metric: per triangle, take singular values `sigma_min, sigma_max` of the Jacobian between original and advected triangle; distortion `delta_t = max(sigma_max, 1/sigma_min)`; triangle quality `Q_t = max((delta_max - delta_t)/(delta_max - 1), 0)` (1 undistorted, 0 at max acceptable); vertex quality `Q_V` = mean of incident triangles; *kill* the particle when any `Q_V < 1/2` — the margin reserved for fade-out. Weights `w_V(t) = K_s(V) * K_t(t)`: temporal `K_t` a linear fade-in over `tau`, hold at 1, linear fade-out over `tau` after kill; spatial `K_s = (1 - |V-p|/d) * d_V * Q_V` with `d_V = 0` on the grid boundary, guaranteeing zero weight at every patch edge. Their second key result: the naive weighted average `R' = sum(w_i R_i)/sum(w_i)` preserves the mean but *shrinks the variance* wherever patches overlap — contrast loss and visible heterogeneity. Their Eq. 4: `R'(x) = [sum_i w_i(x)*(R(u_i(x)) - Rbar)] / sqrt(sum_i w_i(x)^2) + Rbar`, with `Rbar` the reference texture's mean — restoring the reference variance exactly (proof in their appendix). Blending happens on linear channels (noise octaves, height); the nonlinear appearance function is applied after. Rendering is either direct splatting into an intermediate texture (accumulating `w*a` and `w^2`) or an indirection grid storing covering-sprite IDs with constant cost under zoom (10 ms at 4096x4096-equivalent vs 410 ms direct). Performance: 300 grids of 8x8 vertices at 512x512 output = 9 ms total (6.5 ms CPU particles + 5.5 ms GPU) on a 2010 GTX 275. They also define the quality metrics any scheme should pass: measured optical flow (Lucas–Kanade, window 1/20 of image) must match the input field, and the Fourier spectrum must match the exemplar's.

For poseidon: two pieces transfer verbatim to the fragment shader. (1) The variance-preserving blend is a two-line change wherever two phase samples are mixed: `out = (wA*(sA-m) + wB*(sB-m)) / sqrt(wA^2 + wB^2) + m`, with `m` the lace texture's known mean, bakeable as a constant per mip. This kills the mid-blend muddy-foam pulse at its root instead of hiding it with noise — and composes with the noise de-phasing. (2) `delta_t = max(sigma_max, 1/sigma_min)` of the UV Jacobian is the principled distortion metric: the advected carve UV's screen-space derivatives (dFdx/dFdy versus the underived UV) give that Jacobian for free, so poseidon can locally *shorten* the effective cycle (or clamp warp gain) exactly where stretching exceeds a threshold — a per-pixel version of what the paper does per-triangle.

### Wave sprites: regenerate where sampling density matters

The same group's [Yu et al. 2009](https://maverick.inria.fr/Publications/2009/YNBH09/riversEG09.pdf) ("Scalable Real-Time Animation of Rivers", Eurographics 2009) carries small-scale wave detail on sprites over particles kept as a Poisson-disk distribution in *screen space* (spacing d, sprite radius `r = d` guaranteeing gap-free coverage), advected in world space by a procedurally evaluated steady velocity field (stream-function based, computed locally from distance to banks and obstacles — no global simulation). Per frame: advect; delete out-of-frustum or over-dense particles (fading first: active -> inactive -> dead); insert new particles via incremental boundary sampling (O(N)), recovering world positions by rendering world position to a buffer and reading back. Each sprite maps a random window of a tileable wave texture, window size recomputed per frame proportional to viewer distance so screen-space wavelength stays constant. Reconstruction weights `w(x,t) = w_x(x)*w_t(t)`: `w_x` linear falloff to 0 at radius r; fade-in `w_in(t) = min(t - t0, T)/T` and fade-out `w_out(t) = w_in(t1) * max(t1 - t + T, 0)/T` with user fading period T — fade-out starts from the weight reached at inactivation, so a still-fading sprite dies without a pop. The fragment shader accumulates `w*z` and `w` from a screen-space indirection texture of covering sprites; `z_avg = sum(w*z)/sum(w)`; *then* normals and Fresnel are computed from the blended heights — blending physical parameters before shading avoids lighting artifacts. Cost is proportional to projected river area, independent of world size; real-time at full-window coverage on 2009 hardware. Noted limitation: at very close views the sprite is smaller than the texture's longest wavelength, so the lowest frequencies must be carried separately per sprite (a scalar from a low-passed version).

For poseidon: the architectural lesson is "regenerate in the space where sampling density matters" — the coarse-mip regional reads already implement a rough analog. Two specifics transfer: crossfade advected lace *fields* then apply tonal layering (mirroring their z-then-normal order), and the fade-out-from-current-weight formula is the correct popless way to retire any transient foam element (e.g. discrete scud patches spawned from the accumulator): never restart the envelope, decay from wherever it was.

### IBFV: the stateful one-tap alternative

[van Wijk 2002](https://vanwijk.win.tue.nl/ibfv/ibfv.pdf) ("Image Based Flow Visualization", SIGGRAPH 2002; [source code page](https://vanwijk.win.tue.nl/ibfv/)) replaces N discrete phases with one image advected every frame plus continuous injection: `F(p_k; k) = (1-alpha) * F(p_{k-1}; k-1) + alpha * G(p_k; k)`. The history term is a single backward/forward warp of the previous frame (mesh warping originally; a single semi-Lagrangian fetch in shader form); G is a *periodic* sequence of low-pass-filtered noise frames — each texel a "particle" glowing with profile `w(t)` at a random per-texel phase `phi in [0,1)`: `G_i(k) = w((k*dt + phi_i) mod 1)`. Profiles tested: raised cosine (too soft), square wave (crisp, high contrast), exponential decay `t^-beta` (particle-like heads and tails but poor dynamic range), sawtooth `w(t) = 1 - t` (best compromise). Typical parameters: 512^2 image, 64^2 noise tiles, M = 32 noise frames, 100^2 warp mesh, `alpha ~ 0.1` — quantified: `alpha = 0.1` shrinks texture standard deviation ~77%, so contrast must be budgeted — with `alpha = 0.01–0.02` for soft long-trail looks; 50 fps on a GeForce2Go in 2002. The inflow-boundary artifact (black leaking in) is fixed by *not clearing*: texels with no valid history keep their previous value and are refreshed only by the alpha blend (their Eq. 22). The exponential-decay view — `F = alpha * sum_i (1-alpha)^i G(k-i)` — shows the effective latency is `1/alpha` frames and the crossfade is continuous rather than periodic, so there is no pulse at all; the price is a persistent history texture and progressive blur, since each resample low-passes.

For poseidon: it deliberately has no flow-map history in the fragment path — but it already owns a persistent per-texel compute texture, the ping-ponged turbulence accumulator. IBFV shows that the same ping-pong slot extended by one channel gives foam-texture advection for one fetch per frame: `newFoamTex = (1-alpha)*sample(oldFoamTex, uv - flowUv*dt) + alpha*laceField(uv, t)`, `alpha ~= dt/latency`. That is a compute-pass, not screen-space, so it respects the pipeline's constraints (per-cascade, camera-independent), and it makes foam features genuinely travel, merge and dilute with zero pulsing. Costs to budget: the ~77% contrast loss at `alpha = 0.1` (fixable with the Yu variance trick or a contrast curve after the read) and resampling blur (fixable by injecting high-frequency lace in G every frame — which the baked Voronoi already provides).

### Tiled directional flow: regenerate in space, not time

[van Hoesel 2011](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2037715.2037738) ("Tiled Directional Flow", SIGGRAPH 2011 poster; [full commented shader source](https://github.com/Scrawk/Tiled-Directional-Flow/blob/master/Assets/TiledDirectionalFlow/Shaders/TiledDirectinalFlow.shader); modern reconstruction at [Catlike Coding "Directional Flow"](https://catlikecoding.com/unity/tutorials/flow/directional-flow/)) is the main alternative to time-phase crossfading. The flow domain is cut into a tile lattice (flow sampled with `floor(uv*texScale)/texScale`, constant per tile); the water normal map is *rotated* and scaled per tile by a 2x2 matrix built from the tile's flow vector (`rotmat = [fx, -fy; fy, fx]`, flowdir premultiplied by a wavelength channel), then translated by a global scroll `_offset = time*speed`. Seams are hidden by *four* overlapping lattices (A, B, C, D) offset by half a tile in x, y, and xy; every point blends 4 samples. Blend factor per axis: `ff = abs(2*frac(uv) - 1) - 0.5`, sharpened `ff = 0.5 - 4*ff^3` (the cubic widens the plateau where both tiles contribute equally); `NormalTAB = ff.x*A + (1-ff.x)*B` etc., then `ff.y` across pairs. Each lattice scrolls at a slightly different speed (multipliers 1.0, 1.06, 1.33, 1.24 plus arbitrary constant offsets 0.62, 0.27) so the four copies decorrelate and the water "animates" rather than slides. Contrast restoration: averaging normals pulls them toward the mean, so the blended deviation is rescaled by `ffscale = sqrt(ff^2 + (1-ff)^2)`: `NormalT = (NormalT - 0.5)/(ffscale.y*ffscale.x)` — the same variance-preserving normalization as Yu et al.'s Eq. 4 (`w/sqrt(sum w^2)` for weights w and 1−w), discovered independently. Because no tile ever resets in time, there is *no temporal pulse*; the artifact moves to space instead (detail softening along tile edges — per mtnphil's analysis, bright specular features dim as they cross a seam), and sharp per-pixel direction changes are lost since flow is constant per tile. Cost: 4 normal fetches + 4 flow fetches.

For poseidon: attractive precisely because the foam texture is *directional* (the wind-frame anisotropic carve). The plain two-phase Valve scheme assumes direction-free content, while van Hoesel rotates the texture into the local flow frame per tile — what poseidon's wind-frame sampling already does globally. The natural hybrid: keep the global wind frame, but let tile-level flow (coarse-mip horizontal displacement, floored to a ~10–20 m lattice in the 144 m cascade frame) modulate rotation and speed per tile with 4-tap half-offset blending. And the `ffscale` contrast restoration is usable *today* on the existing 3-scale domain-warped lace combination — poseidon already averages multiple texture reads and pays the same normals-toward-mean contrast tax; the seam-band softening artifact is exactly the variance loss this normalization repairs.

### The Pixar patent: film-grade confirmation plus shear dampening

[US 9177419 B2](https://patents.google.com/patent/US9177419B2/en) (O'Brien & Hemberger, assigned Pixar, filed 2013, granted 2015; [USPTO PDF](https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/9177419)), "Advection of UV texture maps in fluid flows," is the production codification of advect-reset-crossfade for surface detail (foam displacement) on simulated water. UV displacements are advected with the fluid mesh; because mesh points move at different velocities the map distorts, so each UV set is periodically reset to the current geometry ("re-pinned" to the identity mapping). Two overlapping UV sets run on staggered cycles — in the patent's example both advect for 50 frames between resets, with the second set's resets at the midpoints between the first's (N/2 = 25-frame stagger) — and a smooth sine-like periodic mix weights them so that at each reset instant of set 1 the mix is at an extreme where set 2 contributes 100% and set 1 contributes 0%: the reset discontinuity is completely hidden because the resetting map has zero weight at that moment. The extra idea: a *dampening* function suppresses the advected displacement in high-shear regions, with shear measured as a function of `du x dv` — the cross of the UV derivatives, i.e. the area/skew change of the advected parameterization — so fast water sliding past slow water does not shred the texture; detail gracefully reverts toward un-advected exactly where advection would destroy it.

For poseidon: independent confirmation from film production of the identical recipe (2 sets, half-period stagger, weight hitting 1/0 exactly at resets) — with one idea poseidon lacks in advection form. It already damps its carve warp under compression (0.35 -> 0.12 with squeeze) using strain; the patent suggests the complementary metric: measure the Jacobian area/skew of the advected carve coordinates themselves (in TSL: the cross of the analytic derivatives of the warped uv, or dFdx/dFdy) and fade advection strength toward zero where it exceeds a threshold, self-limiting shear in exactly the divergence bands where the strain-driven thresholds are simultaneously thinning foam. The two mechanisms reinforce: dampened advection + strain-thinned coverage = foam separating without smearing.

### The offline regeneration branch: re-synthesize instead of reset

The offline literature answers distortion not by resetting coordinates but by *re-synthesizing* texture wherever it degraded. [Kwatra et al. 2007](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17622678/) ("Texturing Fluids", TVCG; [project](https://www.cc.gatech.edu/gvu/perception/projects/textureoptimization/)) transports texture information — color *and* local orientation — between free surfaces by extending it into the 3D fluid volume, advecting one step, interpolating back, then runs surface texture optimization (their SIGGRAPH 2005 EM-like energy: sum over surface neighborhoods of squared distance to the nearest exemplar neighborhood) with the transported texture as the temporal-coherence soft constraint — the optimizer keeps whatever advection left intact and regenerates (snaps back to exemplar statistics) exactly where stretching, shearing, or topology change corrupted it; orientation advection lets anisotropic patterns follow rotation. [Gagnon et al. 2016](https://profs.etsmtl.ca/epaquette/Research/Papers/Gagnon.2016/) ("Dynamic Lapped Texture for Fluid Simulations", The Visual Computer) scatters particle trackers on the surface, advected and rotated coherently with the flow; overlapping lapped patches anchored to trackers fill a texture atlas; per frame, patches whose deformation or coverage fails are retired, uncovered atlas texels spawn new trackers, unused trackers are removed — patch layering plus this birth/death process suppresses popping with "controllable texture distortion." The follow-ups sharpen the trigger: [Patch Erosion (CGF 2021)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/cgf.142639) combines an explicit distortion metric with a feature map and *erodes* a patch's contribution mask progressively — feature-by-feature — before replacement, and a CGF 2019 companion ("Distribution Update of Deformable Patches") keeps the patch distribution Poisson-like under compressible surface flow. [LazyFluids](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2766983) (Jamriska et al., SIGGRAPH 2015) is the appearance-transfer formulation: flow-guided synthesis where each frame is synthesized from the exemplar with the advected previous frame as initialization/constraint, with uniform-patch-usage enforcement preventing the wash-out plain advection-plus-synthesis accumulates. All run seconds-to-minutes per frame — none fit a real-time fragment shader — but they define the quality target and the regeneration triggers: a deformation metric per patch or feature, coverage holes, feature-map mismatch.

For poseidon: not runnable in budget, but it validates the design poseidon is converging on from the cheap side — foam that stretches, separates and merges needs (a) transport, (b) a distortion measure, (c) local regeneration gated by that measure, (d) popless fade of regenerated content. The baked Voronoi lace is the "exemplar"; the strain-thresholded carve is a degenerate one-shot regeneration (the field is re-read fresh every frame). The patch-erosion idea has a shader-sized analog: rather than crossfading a whole phase globally, gate the phase blend *per feature* with the lace field itself — erode the old phase's contribution through the F2−F1 web before the new phase fades in — so regeneration happens along foam filament boundaries where it is invisible, which is precisely the paper's motivation for eroding instead of fading.

## Foam-to-geometry feedback

### Unpublished territory, not a documented dead end

No published or shipped real-time FFT ocean pipeline feeds breaking back into the spectral surface. War Thunder / NVIDIA WaveWorks — verified slide-by-slide — uses its turbulent-energy field only for foam intensity, foam thickness-by-stretching, and refraction milkiness; Tessendorf's course notes stop at "extract the overlapping region and use it for other purposes"; Dupuy & Bruneton and every surveyed open-source implementation are shading-only. The coupling poseidon is considering is unpublished territory — but crucially, it is *not* a rejected idea with a documented failure mode. Where crest geometry does change when breaking (Horizon Forbidden West 2022, its SIGGRAPH 2024 follow-up, Wave Curves), it is always an *added*, authored or baked deformation layered on the ambient sea — because Fourier modes are global, local dissipation is impossible in the spectral domain and must be applied per-texel post-IFFT, exactly like War Thunder's shipped distance-driven cascade fade (the same operation, a different driver signal).

### War Thunder / WaveWorks: turbulent energy never touches geometry

The full text of Tim Tcheblokov's CGDC 2015 deck ["Ocean simulation and rendering in War Thunder"](https://developer.download.nvidia.com/assets/gameworks/downloads/regular/events/cgdc15/CGDC2015_ocean_simulation_en.pdf) (also surveyed in [Ryan 2025](https://rtryan98.github.io/2025/10/04/ocean-rendering-part-1.html)) confirms the pipeline. Four spectrum cascades (5 m .. 1 km tiles). Basic foam: the Tessendorf Jacobian with a raised threshold, `J < M` with `M ~ 0.3..0.5`, foam intensity `= saturate(k*(-J+M))` — "Foam disappears!" is listed as the failure of the instantaneous version. Advanced foam: "Breaking waves inject turbulent energy to cascades. Energy dissipates over time (exponential fade out) and in space (blur). Simulate for each cascade using PS, combine results." That turbulent-energy field is then used *only* for shading: "Turbulent energy = foam intensity"; foam textures modulated by energy *and* by surface stretching ("stretched — thinner, squeezed — thicker" — the same idea as poseidon's strain-driven carve thresholds); dense foam added on breaking areas; and "milkiness" modulated by energy added to the refraction color. Nothing in 56 slides feeds energy back into displacement or normals — and the deck exposes two structural reasons. (1) Slides 39–50: the same FFT displacement is re-simulated on the CPU for deterministic networked physics (readbacks for buoyancy, iterative raycasts for projectiles), so graphics-side displacement must stay bit-identical to the analytic FFT result ("Physics displacements vs Graphics displacements" is called out as a challenge); a turbulence-conditioned damp would desync them. (2) Per-cascade attenuation *is* used, but distance-driven: "Fade out & exclude cascades at distance — less noise, less work on GPU." So the exact operation — spatially varying attenuation of one cascade's displacement-plus-normal contribution — shipped and is artifact-free; only the driver signal (turbulence instead of distance) is new.

For poseidon: the accumulator is a per-texel version of WaveWorks' turbulent-energy field (theirs adds spatial blur; poseidon approximates that with coarse-mip neighbourhood reads). The distance-driven cascade fade is the strongest shipped precedent that attenuating the 24 m cascade's displacement/derivative contribution per-texel is safe rendering-wise. The physics-consistency reason WaveWorks never coupled foam to geometry does not apply to poseidon (no networked buoyancy or raycasts), so the main historical blocker is absent. And the milkiness-added-to-refraction trick is a cheap, uncoupled win matching poseidon's submerged-grey tonal layer.

### Tessendorf's notes: full folding machinery, no post-breaking prescription

[Tessendorf's course notes](https://jtessen.people.clemson.edu/reports/papers_files/coursenotes2004.pdf) ("Simulating Ocean Water", section 4.6 Choppy Waves) derive the folding criterion completely: `J = J⁻J⁺` from the 2x2 deformation matrix of the horizontal map `x -> x + lambda*D(x)`; folding onset is signalled by the *minimum* eigenvalue `J⁻` going negative, with analytic eigenvalues `J± = ½(Jxx+Jyy) ± ½[(Jxx−Jyy)² + 4Jxy²]^½` and the eigenvector `ê⁻` pointing "in the horizontal direction in which the folding is taking place." On what to do afterwards, the notes stop at: "With this information, it should be relatively easy to extract the overlapping region and use it for other purposes if desired." There is no suggestion to damp the spectrum, filter the surface, or modify displacement after breaking — the notes treat the FFT sea as statistically stationary: the empirical spectrum already embodies the long-run balance of wind input versus breaking dissipation, per the Phillips-type equilibrium reasoning that also underlies [Horvath 2015](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2791261.2791267)'s DigiPro spectra. Critically for feedback design, `D` is purely horizontal in eq. 44 — `D(x,t) = Σ −i(k/k)·h̃(k,t)e^{ik·x}` — so the Jacobian contains only horizontal-displacement gradients; vertical height perturbations never enter `J`.

For poseidon: three payloads. (1) The eigenvector `ê⁻` is the physically correct *local* axis for the wind-frame anisotropic carve — computable in closed form from the derivative maps poseidon already produces (Jxx, Jyy, Jxy), giving per-texel carve orientation instead of a global wind frame. (2) The vertical-displacement-never-enters-J fact is the stability foundation for a crumble bump: any vertical-only micro-displacement added under the fresh-cap band has, by construction, *zero* influence on the Jacobian and therefore zero feedback into the foam accumulator — an unconditionally stable geometry coupling. (3) Since the spectrum already statistically includes breaking losses, accumulator-driven damping should be treated as local redistribution (contrast), not a correction — keep it mean-preserving-ish or the sea reads as under-energized for its wind speed.

### The universal consensus: foam is a shading decal on pristine FFT geometry

[Dupuy & Bruneton 2012](https://inria.hal.science/hal-00967078v1) — the canonical whitecaps paper — computes whitecap coverage from the Jacobian as a linearly pre-filterable quantity (mean/variance via mip-mapping, coverage from the filtered statistics), explicitly so it works "from centimetric to planetary" scale, and it is a pure shading overlay with geometry untouched: their [demo](https://github.com/jdupuy/whitecaps)'s `ocean.glsl` carries `LAYER_JACOBIAN_XX/YY/XY` as texture layers consumed at shade time. The same holds across every implementation checked: [2Retr0/GodotOceanWaves](https://github.com/2Retr0/GodotOceanWaves) (linear foam accumulation, exponential decay, foam-culled GPU sea-spray particles — spray, not surface deformation), [gasgiant/FFT-Ocean](https://github.com/gasgiant/FFT-Ocean) for Unity (the `min(J)/recover` turbulence-accumulator pattern poseidon uses), tessarakkt/godot4-oceanfft, and the [2025 rtryan98 ocean series](https://rtryan98.github.io/2025/10/04/ocean-rendering-part-1.html) (`foam_factor = jacobian < bias ? 1.0 : 0.0`, computed after all displacement/normal work, no geometric consequence). No published or shipped real-time FFT pipeline was found that damps displacement from a foam or turbulence field.

For poseidon: this confirms the premise — the foam-decal-on-sharp-crest contradiction is industry-wide, and attempting the coupling means doing something no surveyed pipeline documents. A side benefit: Dupuy & Bruneton's filtered-Jacobian statistics are a better regional signal than raw coarse-mip `J` reads — the coarse-mip neighbourhood reads already approximate the mean, and adding the second moment (`E[J²]` in another channel) would give variance-aware coverage that anti-aliases the fresh-cap band at distance, directly compatible with the existing mip infrastructure.

### The pipelines that do change crest geometry: authored deformation, never spectral feedback

Hugh Malan's ["Rendering Water in Horizon Forbidden West"](https://advances.realtimerendering.com/s2022/SIGGRAPH2022-Advances-Water-Malan.pdf) (Advances in Real-Time Rendering 2022, full slide text extracted): breaking waves are a baked, hand-tuned animated cross-section of a Houdini breaker stored as an XYZ-offset texture (one row per animation frame), applied by compute shader along artist-authored wavefront curves. The crest steepens, curls (with the inner tube loop modeled), turns to foam at animation parameter ~0.5, and — the key detail — "we need the animation to end at a flat undeformed surface, so the deformation can be removed without artifacts." The shipped answer to "what does a broken crest look like" is: the crest collapses through crumble to flat, over an authored timeline, layered onto the ambient water. Foam is passed via vertex color, which caused "foam popping" undersampling — their stated weakness. Deformation strength has an independent fade parameter to create alongshore gaps ("we need an additional parameter to modulate the strength of the deformation, so we can fade it to zero"), and one deformation texture served every breaking wave in the game. The [SIGGRAPH 2024 follow-up](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3641233.3664308) (Lopatin, Vossers, Malan-Revell, "Simulation and Representation of Topology-Changing Rolling Waves for Massive Open Ocean Games") extends this with approximation curves capturing sim data with overhangs and topology change under strict budgets — motivated explicitly because height-displacement flipbooks (Assassin's Creed Odyssey, Death Stranding) cannot represent collapsing crests. Cem Yuksel's Wave Particles and [Skrivan et al.'s "Wave Curves"](https://pub.ista.ac.at/group_wojtan/projects/2020_Skrivan_WaveCurves/wave_curves_2020.pdf) (SIGGRAPH 2020 — Lagrangian wave packets on spline curves attached to deforming surfaces, numerically stable, trivially parallelizable) are the academic relatives: all *add* breaking geometry as a layered, advected structure rather than damping the spectral sea.

For poseidon: the published consensus is that breaking geometry is added or authored on top, never fed back through the spectrum — because FFT synthesis makes local spectral surgery impossible (each Fourier mode is global; any spectral-domain damping damps the whole tile). The practical consequence: geometry coupling must happen in the *spatial* domain, post-IFFT — per-texel/per-vertex attenuation of the sampled 24 m-cascade displacement at surface-assembly time, exactly like the distance fade — or as an added deformation layer. HFW's "animation must end at flat" constraint is also the right mental model for a cheap crumble: whatever bump is added under the fresh-cap band must decay to zero with the accumulator so removal is artifact-free.

### The physical basis for damping only the smallest cascade: `gamma_t = 2*nu_t*k^2`

[Ermakov, Dobrokhotov, Sergievskaya & Kapustin 2020](https://doi.org/10.3390/rs12213618) ("Suppression of Wind Ripples and Microwave Backscattering Due to Turbulence Generated by Breaking Surface Waves", Remote Sensing 12(21):3618) measured Ka-band radar backscatter over mechanically generated breaking waves with wind ripples present: after a breaker's passage "the radar return strongly dropped and then slowly recovered to the initial level," with suppression ratios (intensity before / after) of ~3 to >10 (≈5–10+ dB) for centimeter–millimeter ripples, verified by subsurface velocity measurements to be caused by breaking-generated turbulence. The model is enhanced viscous damping: the wave damping coefficient `gamma_t` takes the standard viscous form with molecular `nu` replaced by an eddy viscosity `nu_t ≈ C_t*sqrt(u_t^2)*l_t` — i.e., damping rate `∝ nu_t*k^2`. The `k^2` weighting means breaking-generated turbulence preferentially annihilates the *shortest* waves — the physical justification for attenuating only the highest-frequency cascade, hardest, with strength proportional to turbulence intensity. The wake also accumulates surfactant via bubbles, adding further short-wave damping (foam-covered water is anomalously smooth). This is why breaker wakes are visible in reality as smooth, glossy/dark "scars" in sun glitter — a normals/roughness-scale phenomenon so well documented in remote sensing that breaker wakes are routinely mistaken for oil slicks. Complementary field work: ["Field Observations of Breaking of Dominant Surface Waves"](https://doi.org/10.3390/rs13163321) and micro-breaking backscatter studies in the same journal family, plus "Suppression of shorter waves by longer breaking waves."

For poseidon: a direct recipe for the trail band. Where the accumulator is in the trail/recovery band, attenuate the 24 m cascade's contribution to *derivatives* (normals) by up to ~70–90% (matching the measured suppression ratios of 3–10), attenuate its displacement less or not at all, and drop specular glint density — lower normal detail means fewer glints. Do *not* raise roughness in the wake: the physical wake is smoother and glassier than the ambient sea, distinct from the foam-covered fresh cap, which is diffuse and rough.
